name: Jonathan Adler
text:
Solare excels in all respects as one of the best Italian fine dining establishments.

The restaurant is large and very well designed, featuring gorgeous private dining rooms with wine rack walls as well as a full bar and spacious dining areas.

The Staff recommended the Tasting Menu which consisted of:

Insalata-lettuce wedge in egg mouse with mustard seed caviar. This was a superb and memorable combination of flavors.

Ravioli in brown butter, sage, arugula with ricotta

Papardelle al Sugo di Salsiccia-house made pasta aged a year with sausages and pistachos. This dish is a winner featuring a delicious crunchiness and deep flavor.

The highlight was my first ever Hawaiian Monchong fish in smoked tomato broth and fingerling potatoes. The fish was perfectly cooked, very fresh and tender.

My wine selection, Montepulciano was exceptional and perfectly complemented the food.

I also had a Voltaire mixed drink which I highly recommend.

Before and afterwards, the Owner and head chef from Sicily were gracious enough to welcome me as a guest.

Solare also features a gorgeous outdoor patio and is full of art which really enhances the mood.

Verdict: Solare is well deserving of its #1 rating in San Diego magazine for Italian restaurants and is easily within the 100 best in the nation in my experience.

Kudos to the exceptional team there.

Captains (smart casual attire) are stationed at the front register that keep tables quickly turned over and filled.  Leutenants (green vests) seat you, get your tea and take custom orders while overseeing floor operations.  Foot soldiers (green aprons) man the dim sum carts.  Food quality is top flight in ingredient quality and preparation.  Great service.  Fair pricing.  A hard earned 5-stars in a highly competitive segment.

name: BD
text:
Anybody with some cash can buy a franchise. But remember, employees can make it work or break it! And the only way your going to pick out the gems during the interviewing process is by experiencing the hiring process for a few years. And then, you'll most likely have a well tuned and profitable franchise!
I say this only because I listened to a customer complain to a manager about the disrespect they got from one of the employees.
Look, making a franchise profitable isn't easy! If it was, do you think the selling company would actually be selling them to you, or keeping all of the locations as corporate owned and operated? They want you to invest YOUR money so YOU have a vested interest to make the business successful! And I totally get that.
Average employees treat your business like aa renter treats your property! This is why management that hires and runs a retail business knows that they are just well-paid babysitters!
So the lesson is: Hire a manager that knows how to A) Hire good people, and B) Manage good people in a way that they like going to work and want to stay!
Statistically, the food business already is doomed from the beginning. A lot of competitors, a lot of employees just looking for ways to milk the job and steal you blind. Sorry, that's the truth of the matter.
When the customer has way too many choices for dining out, it just takes one bad experience with an untrained and uncaring employee to lose the customer for good.
Assistant Managers, keep your ears open and mostly just listen. Listen to what the customers are willing to share with you, and most of all listen to what the employees are saying to each other. That's where a good assistant manager earns his or her pay. Reward the good employees and don't be afraid to let the not so good ones go. Because bad attitude is like a cancer when it comes down to spreading from one employee to another!!

HELLO, MY NAME IS FROSTY!!

Several years ago I worked at Camp Hammer in the Santa Cruz Mountains. All of the staff were given camp names to use for the summer with the kids and other staff. The names were assigned to us - we didn't get to pick them ourselves. I was given the name Frosty.  I believe this happened because in my camp application I had mentioned how much I love eating the Frozen Dairy Dessert from Wendy's: aka The Frosty!!

This Wendy's wasn't far from my parent's house, where I lived from 1989 to sometime in the 2000s. My parents liked to cook dinner at home, and I didn't eat a lot of fast food, but I camp here countless times over the years for the dessert and sometimes a baked potato with chili. I like their tiny side salads too.  They have a good value menu and it has a few healthier options. That's nice.

They cleaned the place up a couple years back - redid everything and it looks very nice. I think that was around the time the talk of In N Out coming to the area was starting. Smart decision! This Wendy's looks great and service is still just as friendly as ever.

This location is always busy but never crowded enough that it prevents me from recommending to others or having meetups.  The clientele is very chill, mostly being frequented by the surrounded businesses and studio employees. text:
Classic breakfast place. During COVID they are only serving out of one restaurant. Do you don’t get the same ambiance but the food is just as good. The Waffle Spot draws a lot of locals as well as tourists. When you arrive check in and put your name down. Due to the small dining room and social distancing the wait might be longer. You can scan the menu outside so once inside your ready to order.

The menu features eggs, waffles, and other classic breakfast favorites. You won’t get anything unique or special here. The food is fresh and well prepared.

If your staying in the hotel I’d recommend calling and ordering take out.  It will be less social interactions and will save you time.  You could also eat in the pool area.

Ample parking out front. Staff is friendly. They have a few hand sanitizer stations inside.

8/5/20 - 2 stars

So when you order on the mobile app you can no longer go inside to pick up, and you can't change this option once selected. So if you don't pick curbside delivery and enter your strap number, they make you wait in the drive-thru line which today took a total of 18 minutes after our order was placed. So we are left with cold fries in our car right now...
Oddly, they were able to walk a drink out to us but the girl said she thought we already got our food and did not walk food back out but instead directed us to go through the drive-thru.
Wow...  Totally love cold fries... doesn't everyone?

3/5/18 - 4 stars

This McDs remodeled itself maybe a couple of years ago now. Opened up with a beautiful new building. However, at the time of the remodel, they removed the chocolate flavor from their swirl cone. So now, it’s vanilla only, rather than vanilla-chocolate mix. But aside from that disappointing change, everything else has been an improvement.

The dual drive thru lines are great, even though some other customers have no idea how to merge politely. But not a big deal since you never seem to be in the line long anyhow, as food comes out hot and fast.

We weren’t the only ones thinking about ice cream sundaes and shakes last night; the car in front of us had the same order. Vanilla swirl cones ($1.62 each). So good!

My family and I have dined @ Senro Sushi several times since they first opened @ this location.

The staff are friendly and helpful. The prices can be steep. For 2 adults and 2 pre teens, we dropped $75 and change. Although, the entree's and sushi have been consistently fresh and delicious.

Except when I ordered the Yakitori, which is grilled chicken skewers. I was very dissappointed when the server brought it to our table.

The skinless pieces of chicken didn't have any grill marks and lacked flavor. It tasted like it was boiled and  just drizzled with  the teriyaki sauce over the dry chicken. I didn't send it back because I was too hungry!

I lived in Japan for 3 years, Yakitori translates to " grilled chicken" I guess I shouldn't be too critical since it may not be a traditional Japanese restaurant.

Usually, customers are welcomed with a saying " Irasshaimase" by the staff. Which translates to " come on in" or welcome to the store.

Anyway, we will still eat @ Senro Sushi. I just won't order the " grilled chicken".

Was it expensive? I don't know, I think Home Town buffet, or Golden Corral would have cost about the same, but, without the exotic foods you find here. 12/24/12 - five stars

This review is based on our recent Happy Hour experience in the bar area of Black Angus - we did not have dinner in the restaurant.

Hubby and I enjoyed spending a Friday together when I recently had a day off from work. We decided to stop for Happy Hour at Black Angus and sat down in the Bulls Eye Bar. Most of the tables we full so we took two seats at the bar in front of the bartender, Ieva.

We ordered the appetizer sampler ($13.50 normally, and $5 off during happy hour), cheesy garlic bread ($3.50), and a couple of margaritas on the rocks. The drinks were really well made. Service was fast (sitting at the bar is usually a good way to get good service).

The cheesy garlic bread was really cheesy but not super greasy. It had a taste we couldn't recognize. Mayo perhaps? Or maybe just a garlic spread.... not sure but it was really good. the outside pieces were crispy and delicious and it was a really good size for sharing.

The appetizer sample came with a shrimp cocktail (which was really only three small shrimp with some cocktail sauce - the sauce was good though!). The potato skins were so crispy on the outside! How do they get the skin like that? Please message me if you know how! The buffalo chicken was really good - not too hot (I like hot but hubby doesn't) and not too saucy. The chicken was tender and juicy on the inside.  The fried zucchini was good too. There was the most of this which wasn't a bad thing since it was good and had it's own dipping sauce - a blend of dill flavors.

Had a great experiene and look forward to coming back again soon!
($22.73 total)

name: fer bas
text: If you are within a 100 miles, you have got to visit this place. Established in 1898, in Stockton, Ca and has been here ever since. The prices are not bad, really, were talking A1 Chinese food, at affordable prices. Some worry about the location, but, that is a by-product of the old racial laws of California. For many, many years in Stockton, Ca, the Asian community was not allowed to live, or have any business's  North of Main Street in this diverse city. The community in which the restaurant stands now used to be the Chinese Community of Stockton. If you take a ride through the area, you will find many old buildings with Chinese writings on them. The area has changed a lot, and the neighborhood is very poor, but, it is still safe in my opinion. Don't be afraid to come to this restaurant because of the area it is in, it just adds more authentic flavor to the place. I found the food to be exceptional , very clean, and well prepared. The booths actually had curtains for privacy, and there was a large crystal chandelier in the main dining area. The tea was very good, brewed with tea leaves, and not some tea bag thrown in a dispenser with hot water. The place was packed when I went on a Saturday afternoon with families, and regulars. I ordered Mongolian Beef with white rice, and it was delicious, not overly spicy, and actually kind of sweet tasting. I also ordered Hot and Sour soup, which was so good, I ate two bowls, It had shrimp, chicken, vegetables, and was very fresh, with a distinctive flavor all it's own. I was not rushed, and felt very comfortable there. The beef was high quality , thick, and tender in my order. I highly recommend anyone to go here and get a taste of Old California Chinese cooking.

11/1/17

After 90 minutes of horseback riding on the beaches of Half Moon Bay, Fred and I stopped in Pacifica before braving all the traffic headed toward the East Bay. He knew of Nick's and suggested we share a plate of fried calamari and a couple cold drinks while enjoying more of the beautiful coastal view. I'm not one to turn down a romantical idea, (or calamari for that matter), so we ended up at the bar facing the crashing waves and enjoying light conversation with the bartender.

We each finished one Moscow Mule, deliciously made and served in the chilled copper cups, before taking our last crispy bites of perfectly cooked calamari. It was a great stop and the perfect end to our amazing weekend. ($38.31 total before tip)

name: Daniel Delong
text:
Always a very satisfying experience at chic-fil-a! I love going to any chic-fil-a! These kids that work here either really REALLY enjoy their work or they're secretly getting bonuses for having a GREAT attitude! No matter what time of year, what extreme weather these kids are standing outside in, they almost always have a great attitude and a smile when taking & filling your order. Since the pandemic has been in our lives, my lovely daughter and I have made it almost a weekly ritual to have our father/daughter dinner dates at a Chick-fil-A. This one in particular is near, if not AT, the top as far as customer service goes.

These kids will be out there in the blistering hot summer sun, the whipping windy days, the occasional downpour and through the bitter bone chilling cold 🥶 evenings in winter. Not only are they prompt and precise, but they do so with a genuine happiness in their work. It is a very welcoming experience, especially in today's time of division & turmoil, to have even the littlest of interaction be as pleasant as it is with this restaurant and more importantly it's employees who all seem to be happy young adults!

I often joke with my family that if the government would have let Chick-fil-A handle the vaccine distribution, all of the world would be taken care of by now. Because they seem to handle an extremely long drive through line like you are the only car there. What looks like a 45 minute wait is a five minute one, and even then it seems shorter.

Would love to add 5 more stars if I could!

name: Del Tafoya
text:
I visited this location between 3-4am on my way home from work. Let's start off with the fact that the grill was being cleaned so they weren't serving burgers for the next 30 minutes or so. Normally this would affect my opinion in a negative manner but the way they handled the situation definitely deserves 5 stars.
I was only able to order chicken nuggets and fries but had originally come to pick up burgers. I'm not sure why but the drive thru line was taking forever so by the time I got to the window to pick up my food, it had been almost 20 minutes. I had asked the woman at the second window if the grill was back on yet since the guy that took my order said if I wanted burgers I'd have to wait 15-20 minutes. She apologized for the misinformation and informed me that it can actually take a little over 30 minutes. Making a long story shorter... This trip took me about 35 minutes but they did compensate me for the inconvenience and handled the situation in a friendly/professional manner.
This is also the only location, closest to Sherman Oaks, that is open 24-7.

I finally got chance to buy Popeyes famous fried chicken sandwich. I went to this location around 5:20 in the early evening and I had to wait about 15 minutes and the drive-thru.

I asked for the spicy chicken sandwich and when I took it out head look like a chicken sandwich but the chicken was fried. Compared to Chick-fil-A which is kind of steamed or baked. And I've never really like McDonalds chicken sandwich which was never crispy. The piece of chicken almost look like two pieces of breast meat and it was moist and tender. And the best part was that it was spicy and crispy on the outside which is what I would have expected. Hopefully Popeyes will be able to keep plenty of chicken sandwich and stock for all to enjoy.

I can't wait to get another one!

name: Majinkain
text:
This was the only and newest sushi spot we hadn't tried yet (within reasonable travel time/local), and now I wish we had sooner so by now we could have tried a broader range of items to review. But, for what we experienced, here's our feedback!

First off, parking is not an issue as it is a shopping complex where it is located. A set back for some will be that there are no wheelchair acceasible ramps leading to the door anywhere along the storefront where it is located. However, the curb is not high so it should not be much of a problem. Since there is no official big street sign yet, the cross streets are Sanderson and Devonshire.

The entire staff is personable and greets you both on the way in and way out, this made an impact on my wife. We had three children with us ranged 7-10 and they were completely patient with us and the fact it took us longer to order being first timers. The waiter was excellent and a key part of the staff, he had been mentioned in reviews we had read before trying it out and he certainly lives up to the reviews and exceeds expectation. We never had a pile up of empty dishes and everything was very prompt to arrive, even our impromptu additions!

All of the food was hot, delicous, and accurate, not to mention abundent (they do not shy on portioning). The bakes messels, agadashi tofu, and our rolls (can't remember the mame or i'd elaborate) were excellent. The jalapeno poppers were perfect for me (iron stomach), but a little hot, but still delicious for the wife (no heat resistance at all!), so keep that in mind when ordering for varying palettes.

All in all, great time for us and the children, certainly worth anyone's time, and a place we will visit again!

name: Amy Palmer
text:
10/26/14

We ate dinner here on a Friday night before a two-day rafting trip this June with a company only a couple of miles away (Mariah Wilderness). It was close to closing  time when we arrived and they had run out of their red sauce veggie pizza, so I ended up with a large slice of pesto potato.  My husband had breadsticks and ranch, and a slice of a chicken pizza (since they were out of pepperoni). ($20.65)

The place was packed but our group of six found a table out front and drank some wine (purchased there) will we waited. There was a loud band in the back and even more people and some dogs.  The pizza took forever to get to us - it was pretty good when it did arrive but the wait was awful.

There was a really long line for the bathroom, but the trees/woods aren't far away for the not shy. While one of our friends waited at the table, a woman came and grabbed her pack of cigarettes off of it, ready to help herself to one. Our friend stopped her, but realized later in the night that her phone was missing (she'd had it there with her earlier). Perhaps the same woman took it.  When she checked back with the place the next day they said they had not found one, that more than one was missing, and not to have high hopes for getting it back.

The food was good and I really liked my second-choice slice, but since there aren't a lot of restaurant options in that area, I would imagine most weekend nights, especially in summer, will always be that packed - so expect a long wait for your yummy food.

text:
1/10/18

Wanting to try somewhere new for lunch over the weekend, the boyfriend and I stopped in the Park n Shop plaza near home and noticed the picture on the outside wall of Stix: curry in a bread bowl. It was a drizzly day and we were both getting over colds, so a hot bread bowl meal wasn’t a hard decision to make – comfort food! We told our server that it was our first time there and Ko T filled us in on the mostly family-style eating and large dish portions.

Even with this information, we totally over-ordered! A complimentary bowl of soup started us off and it was delicious! Chicken satay ($10) was our favorite dish. Really nicely season chicken on skewers and a subtle peanut sauce that didn’t over-power any of the other flavors. Shrimp balls ($6) was our least favorite. Kind of chewy, rubbery balls of fish? We washed these down with a couple of Thai iced teas ($4 each in a large mason glass) then sampled the chicken wings ($6), which were good, but not quite as good as the boneless skewers. A large portion of fried calamari ($10) was a hit, though it seems slightly overbreaded. The meat was still tender though – fried to perfection! Finally, the yellow curry chicken bread bowl ($10) which we barely broke into with all the other plates. It was delicious though and the bread was fresh and complimented the sweet flavors of the curry.

Service was great and the food was good with large portions. I’d totally go back and order the satay and bread bowl again.

name: Jonathan Adler
text:
After having a great time at their Pico-Robertson location, I decided to try out their place on La Brea(about midway between Beverly and Melrose).

The place is very clean and well lit with an excellent Staff.

On the recommendation of the Manager, I had the Japanese Pizza(crispy rice, spicy tuna, avocado, nacho jalapeno) Meshuga Roll(spicy tuna, fresh jalapeno and ponzu sauce) and Yellowtail Special Roll(spicy yellowtail, avocado, cucumber, cilantro and ponzu sauce).

I was extremely pleased with the selections and devoured all 3.  Frankly, it was the best Kosher sushi I've ever had including in Israel.

It was all superfresh, beautifully presented and super tasty.

For dessert, I had their Oreo Insanity(vanilla ice cream surrounded by fried oreos drizzled with chocolate). I found this very creative as well as another very delicious offering.

Service was fast and friendly and the A/C was great on a hot day.

Conclusion:  Hands down best Kosher sushi restaurant I have ever been.

Well done Meshuga Sushi.

text: I'm a fan of Korean fried chicken and saw this was close to the San Leandro BART station. I was very hungry, so when I saw the lunch specials I figured it wouldn't be enough. So I ordered a small combo with half soy garlic and half spicy. They warn you on the menu that your food might take time (30 mins) since it's usually cooked to order. I also ordered a banana milk (I thought it'd be home made but it's in a carton) and seasoned fries. The seasoned fries were seasoned perfectly and cooked well. When my chicken order came out, I was surprised at how large the pieces were. They're much larger than Kentucky Fried Chicken. I had to double check I ordered a small because it was enough to feed two people. Everything tasted great, including the side of daikon. I will definitely recommend this place to others who like Korean fried chicken.

text:
The atmosphere here and service ranks in the best in LA.  This is a family run restaurant and it showed in the personable, caring attention I received during my dinner.

For a Starter, I had the Cuore di Lattuca(hearts of lettuce) with Gorgonzola, Guanciale(cured pork cheek)and Balsamic Reduction.  This was one of the tastiest salads I've had in years with an exquisite combination of flavors.

My entree was the Linguini ai Gamberoni.  The shrimp were some of the largest I've ever seen swimming in delicious pasta and spicy tomato sauce.

I really enjoyed the ambience(lighting, seating arrangement and decor with beautiful Italian watercolors on the walls) turning this into a wonderful fine dining experience.

Very highly recommended for the finest Italian cuisine in WLA.

text:
The name means "The Daily Bread".  This location in Westwood is just steps away from Wilshire behind LA Fitness on Gayley.

There was a nice, upscale crowd when I entered comprised of locals, businesspeople and a large group of ladies celebrating a birthday.

I immediately liked the large airy dining room bursting with morning light.

They have a very extensive breakfast selection; so it took me sometime to decide.

I had the omelette with salmon, scallions and added gruyere cheese with a fruit bowl side.

The omelette was especially delicious and I rate it best omelette I've had this year.

The very friendly, warm, professional service by server Danielle and Manager Anna was a 10/10-Magnifique.

I really enjoyed the Belgian european cafe atmosphere which retains a strong local, homey flavor like its been in Westwood for many years.

I finished my Breakfast with their signature 3 pastry dessert and coffee which capped my morning splendidly.

This restaurant is now one of my top ten choices for breakfast in LA.

Interesting place. Not your typical American nor Hawaiian fare. When I came for lunch it seemed like more people were ordering burgers. Burgers offered were a selection of both standard fare and some with unique toppings. It looks like it use to be a Dairy Queen or other fast food place. Music would be nice as it eerily quiet.

I had the bowl which was just ok. Chicken was pre boiled, chilled, then cooked on a flat top. This was described as “grilled chicken”. Not even close to the moist grilled chicken you get at most Hawaiian restaurants in the Bay Area. Toppings were ok. But it was a weird mix of poke toppings mixed with your standard Hawaiian fare.

Service was good and friendly. But not much help with the menu or up selling.

Soft serve customers be warned. Soft serve ice cream machines are notorious for mold and bacteria growth. Machines need to be emptied and cleaned at least once a week. I prefer soft serve at fast food places that have strict cleaning and sanitation regimens.

For breakfast, I had the bagel cream cheese lox(includes cucumber, capers, dill).  This was the best I've had in WLA.

I was very hungry, so I also had their California Club sandwich with turkey, ham, bacon, cheddar, swiss on a pretzel roll...another winner and enough food for lunch later as well.

My Maple Scone dessert had just the right flavor-not too sweet with a delicious buttery accent.

The atmosphere is great for study, meetings and also quick takeouts with parking(cafe is in Vinci Plaza).

The team of Steve and Andrew did an outstanding job being courteous and prompt with orders.

Verdict:  Board House Coffee  is my #1 choice for coffee, scones and sandwiches in WLA.

name: Vincent D
text:
Go Falafel Greek Food

Located on the corner of Alpine and Pacific Ave. In Stockton, CA

They do have an IG @Gofalafelgreekfood

Here's our Story;

This review is from January of 2019. I wasn't really writing back then. But I've been inspired since September, 6th of this year. So here goes my review.

So I got this flier about Stockton restaurant week. I checked online and picked out places I was going to take my children.

Asked my youngest Princess if she wanted to come here. She said yeah and threw up the deuce.

Note: There's a reason we (My Children and I)  throw up the peace sign. It's our way of approval or really liking something.

I knew what I wanted right off that bat. I wanted a Gyro. Now I attempted to make them (Gyros) at home, but my Gyros end up looking like a Soft Taco, lol. But the Gyro here, was on point. Especially because I threw some fries inside.

My youngest daughter, ordered Chicken Souvlaki with pita bread. Fries and va bottled water. The chicken Souvlaki is like a chicken skewer or kabob. I'm from the hood and we just call it meat on a stick.  I loved watching her stuff the pita bread with chicken and fries. We always get creative and mix food together on our plate. I  love spending time with my kids.

It's pretty small inside and cozy perfect for a date. Swoon. Bring your boo for a nice one on one.

They do take card and cash. Customer service was pretty good and our food didn't take long.

It was in January and the weather was cold outside and Go Falafel Greek Food hit the spot. Everything always comes together for us. So I did have a memorable moment with my youngest daughter. Good Company And Good Food go hand in hand.

Yes, I'm a fan and definitely be back.

"My children are my world and everything else in life is a bonus"

"Enjoying the simple things in life"

"Life is beautiful"

name: Richard E. Gentry
text:
Juanillo's Mexican Grill is just what this location has been waiting for, probably since the 1970's. There hasn't been a really good restaurant there since then. Most of which didn't even warrant a second visit. Yet, I've been to Juanillo's three times in the first week. And I plan to be a Regular. I'm currently working my way through the menu.
Three days a week, they offer daily specials at discounted prices. Torta Mondays, Taco Tuesdays and a 3 Taco plate (with rice & beans) on Wednesday. They also serve breakfast (all day), burgers, salads and seafood. And Menudo & Pozole is served everyday. Plus most orders come with fresh, warm, perfectly seasoned tortilla chips. And yes, those come from their handmade tortillas, made fresh daily. So meet me at Juanillo's. I'll be the guy sitting in the corner, stuffing his face and smiling.

7/11/16

I love stopping in at this taqueria (right off of Monument) when I want to grab a quick bite. Good tacos, great salsa, and really consistently friendly service. The tacos are my favorite thing here - they are inexpensive and you get a lot for your money! The marinated chicken is delicious! And their hot salsa is really spicy and full of flavor! Fresh ingredients and a clean restaurant - exactly what you want when you go out to eat!

Updated from 4/9/13:
Our most recent taco stop was at Los Rancheros after it received Review Of The Day on Yelp.

I ordered one carnitas and two chicken tacos (one grilled, one marinated). Husband ordered three tacos with sour cream. I confirmed at the register that grilled jalapenos came with that, as I'd seen in other Yelp pictures. Yes, yes they do.

We had a rather long wait for the food - it seemed long given how many people were in there (not many) but finally it arrived and they'd forgotten our jalapenos and his sour cream.

The tacos were really, really good though! The two salsas were located next to the register and the hot one was actually very warm! The mild was also very  tasty. We enjoyed eating the chips and salsa immensely! The tortillas were super fresh. I've probably never had a fresher tortilla. the girl working brought me a plate of jalapenos to make up for the forgotten ones, but it was mostly pickled, not grilled. Oh well.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
9/16/14

Why do people order pizza for delivery? Perhaps one reason is because while relaxing on the couch with the TV on after a long day at work, every other commercial we see has something to do with food. After seeing the Pizza Hut stuffed crust commercial a few times, my husband decided to get online and order a pizza.  We ordered delivery so that we could finish America's Got Talent without interruption. We used the computer to place the order because it is a convenient option.

In the "notes" section online, he went to type in "please cook well done so that pepperoni is crispy" but only had enough characters to type "Please cook well done". Thinking about parmesan cheese about thirty minutes later I called to make sure the driver would have some. The girl who answered said they usually carry it with them, but that she would call the driver to make sure.  He was already on his way.

The driver did not have parmesan cheese, so I called just to let Pizza Hut know. If they have a delivery option, they should have the same free cheese and red pepper packets they have in their stores.  How hard is it to carry a few packets?  The nice driver said he had just run out. How smart would it be for them to throw a few packets in each box so that no driver has to worry about running out.

Diana on the phone told me I need to call and request cheese if I want it. Hmm, instead of an apology, the first thing she did was ask if I had called to request it.  I told her that I had called, but that I had placed the order online, and there is nowhere to ask about it on their site. She said again I have to call. I asked her if it is Pizza Hut's policy for a customer to order online and then have to call to request cheese. She said yes. I asked again if it makes any sense for me to use the computer to order, if I have to call also and I was told if I want cheese I need to call and request it.

The Pizza Hut notes section obviously is ignored. Our pizza was not cooked well done. The crust was not browned in any way - super greasy on the bottom (but yes, it's a pizza) and unfortunately a very soft, not crispy at all top crust. So they completely ignored the "well done" request. Perhaps we should have put "cheese please" in hopes of getting that instead.

$3.50 Delivery fees should be waived if the drivers are not going to bring toppings. Red pepper flakes are the best.

When I rate a place, its not just about service, food, or cleanliness.  They passed hands down on cleanliness.  Service was lacking, and the food was lacking.  I don't go into a place and order the most difficult thing on the menu. I orders garlic curley fries, and jalapeno poppers. I regret tipping before eating my food or getting service. Heres how my experience started.
I noticed not a single customer was inside, hesitantly, I walked up after figuring out what I wanted. Asked what the difference was between regular curly fries and the other option on thr menu. The gentleman stated he had been gone for a while and the menu was updated since he was there last. He offered to get someone who could explain the difference for me, but I declined and said that I would just like the garlic curly fries and the jalapeno poppers. I paid, added a tip, then sat down.  I waited 10 minutes before the guy who was behind me in line was brought my food.  The lady who brought it out looked upset already, I didnt think anything of it.  The gentleman who took my order walked up and corrected the mistake, and so I proceeded to eat my food...and I found out that my curly fries were lacking any sign of garlic.  So I stood up and walked to the register. When I did, the same lady who brought out my food gave me a dirty look for some reason, I dont believe I had any ill or angry look on my face when I was standing there waiting to ask about the garlic that was missing.  But since she gave me a dirty look, I walked back to my table to get the receipt. Then walked back to the register and asked the gentleman as I looked at her with frustration, "are these garlic fries?" Then showed my receipt to her so she could see the fries weren't garlic and that the reciept said garlic.  She gave me another dirty look. The gentleman apologized and took the garlic fries. The lady, after that wouldn't even glance in my direction...I was disgusted to the point that I walked out and gave my overcook fries and overcooked jalapeno peppers to a guy who looked hungry enough to not care.  1 star because I have to, the second star for cleanliness. Missing 3 stars for these reasons:
1st: order was wrong
2nd: dirty looks from the lady
3rd:for lack of quality and actually making a decent attempt at fixing my order. And to clarify, overcooked, and garlic clumped on the top. They could have at least tossed it all in a bowl so it was actual garlic fries instead of using a spoon to spread it across the top.

text:
2/2/15

The first thing I noticed when I walked into this Jamba Juice was how clean it was. It was 7 p.m. so perhaps the rush of daytime crowds had long passed - but still it was a couple hours before closing. The two guys working tonight were cleaning up but stopped to greet and help me. I was meeting a friend who had showed up first - I sat down at a (clean!) table with her and her boyfriend to look over some papers and happily reminisced about once upon a time sixteen years ago when I was the seventeen year old behind that juice counter.

I talked for a minute with Josh and Thomas before I left - they were really friendly employees. No music playing (perhaps there's a manager somewhere reading these reviews), and they actually seemed happy to be at work. I enjoyed my visit in here much more than the last time I was inside a Jamba Juice, and I left with a smile on my face!

text:
3/10/15

I've been coming to this RT since my sister and I were little kids. We used to play on the Simpsons arcade machine at the front of the place before they remodeled it years ago. When my sister died unexpectedly a couple of weeks ago, my co-workers helped out my family by bringing homemade dinner to my parents and family every night of the week. The night before the funeral they ordered a Large and X-Large pizza for delivery to my parent's home, a mile away from this location. A special request to make heart-shaped pizza was included on the online order, and the pizzas were customized to end up with one meat and one veggie.

I received a call around 5 pm from RT - I had nothing to do with the ordering, as I'd been with my family all day handling funeral prep. They let me know that they weren't currently making the heart-shaped pizzas, and that pizza would arrive in about 40 minutes. However, it had been requested by the office that the pizzas be delivered at 6:40, so at 5:40 I was home wondering where the pizza was. I called RT back around 6 and asked what was going on - I was told that the person on the phone hadn't looked at the entire order, so I'd been waiting around for nothing. Everyone was really happy when the doorbell rang at 6:40.

My husband asked the driver if he'd already been tipped. He replied "well, sort of". We looked at the receipt. He received $5 to drive ONE MILE. It's a yes or no question. Sort of? What? Do you need more money for a 2 pizza delivery or are you just trying to trick a grieving family? We THEN saw that it was $98 (yes, NINETY EIGHT US DOLLARS) for the 2 pizzas. I called the manager, insisting there must be some mistake. But I was told by the supervisor on duty that customized pizzas are pretty expensive. I asked if there was anything she could do - these weren't very special pizzas. And their L/XL aren't very big. NOPE. That was it.

The girl in my office meant well by ordering something we'd like, but should have started with a veggie pizza and added toppings, rather than taking off and customizing, etc. Also, she thought she was getting heart-shaped pizza. Her heart was in the right place; and Round Table has no heart. They are just another greedy restaurant chain who lost someone as a customer who had so many fond memories after being a loyal fan for decades.

Um, have I been missing out on killer breakfast, so close to home, for a few years now? I returned to G-Cafe a weekend ago (and I haven't been here in years!), only to find that the rumors of "BEST Crab Benedict" are TRUE. No joke - it's the best. So much tender, meaty crab with great Hollandaise sauce (I always get mine on the side) and the hash browns were exactly how crispy I wanted them. My plate was great!!

Fred ordered chicken-fried steak and I couldn't help but steal more than a couple of bites from his large, 2 plate serving! The gravy was really creamy and delicious and the breading was light and crunchy and perfect. At the end of our breakfast two slices of watermelon were brought out to us. I'm usually not one of those people that's like "oh, best 'this' ever"... "best 'that' ever".... but the watermelon was FOR REALZ the best watermelon ever!!

It was packed inside when we arrived but we were seated and served quickly. Really friendly staff and our coffees were kept full. I can't wait to go back in and enjoy another impressive (and affordable!) breakfast!!

[PS - My ONLY advice to the restaurant. Take down the pictures of plated food on your wall and replace with new ones. Many are blurry or out of focus, the salmon plate looks brown, rather than pink and appetizing, and they just aren't doing your food justice. Have them retaken or remove altogether. Your food is better than that!]

5/28/13 - Four stars

OH FOR THE LOVE OF BENEDICT

I love egg's benedict. The first time I had this was less than a year ago and it's been a recent favorite of mine. Mostly because I love English muffins and eggs! I am NOT a fan of Hollandaise sauce. It's not that I dislike it, I just enjoy food without heavy sauces and don't need all the empty calories. Plus, I prefer to hot sauce everything I eat.  MmmmMMmm hot sauce.

We were really hungry and this place is super close to home. it was our first time here since the name change. We arrived and I barely noticed a couple we're friends with sitting two tables away. They totally came over and said hi after we ate and that's when I guiltily realized my eyes probably hadn't left the table the entire time I'd been there. I didn't get a really friendly vibe from the two staff people working, though they weren't by any means unfriendly.  And our food wasn't bad, in fact, parts of it were quite enjoyable, but there were a couple things that made it overall just A-OK.

I had the veggie benedict with spinach added. I forgot to ask for no sauce but I often forget, and I can generally remove it with an empty bowl and spoon. However, there was sooo much on here that the muffins were really soggy. I seriously filled the better part of a large bowl with sauce. Oddly, one egg was a little underdone (just a little bit, but it was just enough for me to notice to clear egg parts) and the other egg was just a little overdone (it had almost no runny yolk).

Husband had sausage links on his breakfast and on the end of each of them there was this amazing crunchy piece. It was really good. They had good flavor and weren't too greasy. Our hashbrowns (which we requested extra crispy) were served perfectly. Great crunch and there were lots of them.

I'll definitely be back since this place is so close to home. I'd like to explore the menu just a little more.

I really enjoyed their location on University in North Park last year and was in the SDSU area so I tried this branch out.

I had a large Poke Bowl with tuna, salmon, shrimp, crabmeat, avocado, edamame etc.

It was great like the last time at Poke 1.5. Everything is fresh, high quality with alot of choices...can't beat it.

Service by Manager Jennifer was outstanding. She is a very friendly and skilled manager as I was there during the lunch rush and the place was running like a swiss watch.

They should open some stores in LA County.

Congratulations team.

name: Endless Possibles
text:
UPDATE: I have now been here 4 times and still 5 stars! Tonight was my first weekend evening and wow, I had such a great experience... for the paid entertainment, unlike anywhere else where a band or DJ begin to set up while you eat and eventually play music... this is what happens... You're casually dining when a old VW bus pulls up sporting some speakers and conspicuous lighting. Guess what, its DJ Alf Alpha who ends up pulling up to the curb, parks, opens up his roof and starts spinning music with a nice sound system mounted to the vintage roof rack! There is also burning incense and a monitor showing interesting videos. This was awesome. Music is properly played starting slow and slowly evolving to hip hop and more. BRAVO
Okay onto the food. Tonight I tried the hummus again, my favorite Bianco pizza add Pepperoni, Caprese pizza add jalapeno, the Boom Boom shrimp and also the meatballs.
The meatballs are dense and have great flavor. The boom boom shrimp are coated in a Panko type of airy crispy and light breading and then smothered in a slightly spicey sticky sauce TRY THIS! The pizzas were great as usual and of course the hummus, oh the hummus. Youd typically have a hard time convincing me that a place has better hummus the most but guess what this place does. They put some sort of oil in it which adds to the flavor and the texture. I'm telling you, this place must be experienced.
Here is my original review, it's worth a read
I love this place. Really consistently good food. Nice selection of sandwiches and pizzas etc. The ingredients are all high quality and the chefs are passionate about what they do and what you're about to eat.
Hummus is really really good, served with pita that is also fresh and delicious with a tiny bit of char flavor it's so delicious.
I got one of the simple pizzas but added pepperoni which wasn't a problem and also made it an 11! Again, fresh quality ingredients over a top quality dough (slightly sweet, savory and chewy) mixed with a light but very flavorful sauce makes for one delicious pie!
This place is absolutely worth a try.
Service is A+ and food is A+

3/15/17

I simply wanted a bowl of soup after a weekend snowboarding with my boyfriend at Bear Valley. On our drive home we stopped in Murphys and found Doke Sushi. Oh how I wish we'd just gone on a little further to Copper. The experience was pretty awful overall, though, the food itself was okay.

After being seated at the sushi counter, it took the one waitress who was working a long time just to acknowledge us. Then she finally came over and took our drink order only. We had to wait a very long time to receive drinks and even order food. Noticing the one sushi chef still hadn't completed the 3 plates for the couple next to us, we knew it would be a while before Brad received his roll and I got my soup.  Wrong. My soup came out almost immediately!!

I commented to the waitress that I'd like to receive my meal at the same time, and she mentioned that the soup was very hot and needed to cool. I took a bite and asked if they'd mind just holding on to it until his food was ready. 15 minutes later he got his plate, and I waited briefly while they heated my soup back up. The soup was ultimately kind of disappointing (but his roll was awesome!) Thai Iced Tea was only $2 but was really weakly brewed.

It should never take an hour to get your one or two item dinner in a restaurant that only seats 20 people total. I don't think this place would survive if there were several competing sushi restaurants nearby.

text:
Napa Valley Grille is an outstanding fine dining establishment.

First, I was very impressed with how large it is with a nice long bar, spacious main dining area(there is also a private dining room) and a beautiful, large, airy lounge with plush couches overlooking Westwood.

I decided to enjoy my dinner in the very comfortable lounge.  My server, Carlos, did an excellent job telling me about their offerings.  I also met the Manager, Sebastian, who was very helpful and informative.  The bartender, Erik, was also very professional and on point.

Napa has a large variety of classic American cuisine to satisfy the palate.  I decided on mussels, roasted filet mignon 8 oz.(medium rare, Nebraska corn fed beef) and an Artisan cheese board.

The mussels were succulent and delicious as well as tender(many restaurants cook them too tough but these were just right).

The cheese board was wonderful.  The variety was very good with raspberries, blackberries and honey to complement the fine cheeses.

The Star was the roasted Filet Mignon.  I asked for medium rare.  The steak was cooked perfectly.  The taste in the steak juices and sauces was phenomenal.  I also added the soft cheese from the cheese board for even more flavor variety.

The Steak I had here is the best I've had in LA so far this year.  Well done Napa and Chef Carlos(also named Carlos like the server).

For wine, I had a glass of Frank, Cabernet Sauvignon 2014 Napa Valley-superb complement to the steak.

The atmosphere at Napa was very comfortable, classy and works well for either romantic dates or business meetings.

Napa Valley Grille is one of the best 10 restaurants I have been to this year in either San Diego or LA and my #1 pick for steak.

text:
On my 2nd visit the food was even better than the first time. Everything I had from the Buffet was superfresh and superdelicious! The Alaskan king crab legs, smoked salmon rolls, succulent, plump shrimps were all outstanding-very impressive.

The wait staff came out with an exciting selection of premium meats including skirt steak, ribeye, sirloin, pork sausages-everything just kept coming and fast, no stalling, waiting long like some all-you-can-eat establishments.

Service was impeccable. My main waiter, Fernando(ask for him if possible), being a consummate professional with excellent timing and demeanor.

After two visits, I rank Reo de Gado(King of the Herd in Portuguese)the best Brazilian steakhouse I've ever patronized and a top ten San Diego restaurant.

Well done.

Very highly recommended, would rate food, service 6 star if that were possible.

This is right across the street from the popular Horton Plaza downtown.

I liked the traditional storefront and the restaurant name translates to "King of the Herd"(cool name).

This steakhouse features a huge seafood/salad bar that is all you can eat!  I think I have entered a foodie paradise!  I gorged on succulent crab legs, large shrimps, smoked salmon, salad and even quail eggs.  The seafood salad bar was great enough but it did not end there, no sir.

The big draw is the Brazilian steak meat and I had large portions of filet mignon, lambchops, chicken/cheese, ribeye and turkey sausage delicacies.  I am not a huge eater but the food was so good my stomach miraculously enlarged to accommodate these tasty offerings.

I also had to try out one of their wines from the huge racks on the walls and opted for the Salton Talentoro which is 60% Cabernet, 30% Merlot, 10% Tannat which is one of the best Brazilian wines.  I also had the Brazilian Xingu Black Beer and they were both winners.

The Brazilian waiter did an outstanding job and is the best dressed waiter I have encountered so far in San Diego.

If all that wasn't awesome enough there was also a pianist playing many of my favorite tunes and I was told he is there most evenings.

Yes, in case you have to ask, Rei Do Gado is the King of Brazilian restaurants in San Diego and maybe even all of southern california.

Some of the best Greek food I've had, fast or sitdown.

Very kitschy with the classical sculpture but what would one expect from a Greek restaurant.

They actually have a number of standard Greek recipes. I had a whole lamb gyro (which is uncommon, as the vertical rotisserie meet is usually a combination of beef and lamb or pork), and I love lamb, ergo, I loved it!

The service was fast enough. The prices are moderate, which is expected for quality food.

There are plenty of places to sit inside, which is helpful during the summer and winter months as the temperatures can be extreme.

So, on my way to Vegas and back -- this may become a mandatory pit stop.

If you miss the stop at Baker Ca. to LV: not to worry, there's a location at State Line.

name: Hope Lanza (Embra)
text:
I love this place, don't get over here as often as I'd like since I'm not living/working in the neighborhood any longer.
I like their rolled tacos the best out of all the various local quick Mexican eateries (and I've tried most of them) One of the reasons I like Rancho Villa's the best is because they don't charge extra for lettuce and tomatoes, and they are not stingy, they put a generous amount of lettuce tomato and shredded cheese on top. You can order either beef or chicken rolled tacos. The guacamole is made  fresh and is full of avocado, they don't mix sour cream in it, the sour cream is available separately. You can order them with the sauces on the side if you wish. For a small fee, you can also order larger portions of guacamole or sour cream.
Another one of my favorite things about this restaurant is that their free salsa bar also includes free corn chips, which are available whether ordering dine in or take out. They have reduced the size of the bags for the take out option: they used to use the #4 paper bags, now they are #2 which are half the size. You can always fill an additional bag or two, especially if you have a larger party. There is a sign asking " please limit the amount of chips and salsa to that which will be consumed" - apparently there was too much waste (which of course would be costly for them if left unchecked)
The service was, as always extra pleasant, I always get friendly service here. The meal was just as delicious as I remembered, I will definitely be back.

text:
HB is right across from the cruise ship terminal and between the USA Midway Museum and old India ship museum. The view, especially during sunset is fantastic. I even got some pics of Marines marching and singing on the water.

They have probably the best deli on the bay with salads, sandwiches, breakfasts, deli items, wine and even a candy section

I had the signature "Big Rich" sandwich named after the owner. It was full of cheese, ham, turkey and enough for 2 meals.

The antipasta salad with boars Head Genoa salami, cheeses, olives and Italian dressing is the best I've ever had, it's addictive and reasonably priced for the high quality.

I also had a bag of candy including gummi bears, sours, bubblegum.

There is alot of seating on a large patio with as I mentioned the spectacular Bay view.

Service by shift supervisor Jesus was 100% on point, courteous and professional. One of the best I've met in the Industry.

Highly recommended for locals and tourists alike.

text:
Unremarkable atmosphere at the cost of overpriced, ordinary chicken. I had quite the appetite that afternoon. No breakfast or lunch whatsoever and I just finished with an intense workout, but even that didnt stop from reminding me how painfully average the quality and overall taste was. That's not a good sign. I ordered the california buffalo chicken burrito, not knowing what to expect except something along the lines of,  you know, meat (in this case fried chicken) and fries or potatoes- the common ingredients of any cali burrito. That is literally ALL I got. Diced wings coated LIGHTLY with sauce, and an overbearing proportion of fries wrapped in a surprisingly small package.
That may satisfy some people but for the price you pay they really couldn't think of putting one more ingredient to even out the density of the fries? It's understandable. My boyfriend and I were in Ed's for our first time several weeks back around lunch time on a weekend. We both ordered the special: fish tacos! (With Bloody Marys and beers to wash it down.) The bartender made a tasty drink and then brought out the food to our seats at the bar, but really didn't speak to us aside from taking our orders. When another man (who given their conversation was definitely at least in a managerial role) came behind the bar to talk about the big police officer party they'd hosted the night before, the bartender at that point finally asked how everything was or if we needed anything else, but I definitely don't think we would have had any interaction had there not been someone who mattered right there watching. Small talk goes a long way when you have two people seated a few feet away and it's their first time in a restaurant.

A $60 lunch deserves at least a little personality served on the side, especially when we were the only 2 people seated at the bar, but the food was very good and we'll definitely be back in here to explore their menu a little more! Just hope someone else is behind the bar when we make it back in.

10/26/14

After finding a limited selection of food available at the Walnut Creek Centennial birthday party across the street at Shadelands, we stopped into this plaza and strolled over to Toyo Sushi. I've taken food to-go before, but it was my first time dining here. My husband and I sat ourselves at a table near the back.  There are probably only 10-15 tables in the place - it's not super big.

We looked over menus for sushi and checked out the specials.  I ended up ordering the spicy Concord roll, miso soup, and a green salad. After asking about the "crunchies" in it's description, my husband ordered the Walnut Creek roll with extra unagi sauce.

My soup and salad came first. The soup was awesome but the salad was soaked in dressing. It was way too much so I picked around a few bites of lettuce and ignored the rest. My brief disappointment was soon forgotten when our huge rolls were set on the table.

Casey's "crunchies" (little bits of puffed/fried rice?) covered his roll and were sooo good! I kept scraping up pieces off his plate with my chop sticks (and then eventually with my fingers).  He was able to finish his roll - and I ate most of mine.  The spicy scallop on top of the spicy tuna was outstanding.  I love ordering new types of rolls when I eat sushi, but I'll likely order this one again next time we come. And there will definitely be a next time!

Sushi was fresh. Service was sweet and fast. Price was right! (About $12/roll)

There were no issues timing the food delivery. Everyone's entree arrived at once. My seafood cioppino was easily the best I've had. Ever. Anywhere. So much seafood, an the hot broth was delicious! I couldn't finish it, or I wouldn't have had room for dessert, so they boxed it up for me to take home! Chocolate cake for dessert. Yes, please. And once again, boom! Blown away with their outstanding food.

The only thing better than the food was the service. If you are planning a special event, group party, or even a romantic night out in the Santa Cruz area, this place is fun, upscale, trendy, and perfect! Extremely reasonable prices and for the quality of food and service.

name: Mihir Meghani
text: Casual nice place in Oakland serving mainly macaroni and cheese. They have many varieties. The spicy mac & sriracha macs are good & spicy. The garlic mac is also good - add breadcrumbs to that. In the past, have had Vermont White Cheddar & the 4 cheese mac which were very good - not an overwhelming cheese flavor but cheesy, Gilroy Mac which was also good with the garlic was not too strong, & Jalapeno Popper Mac which was off the menu, but very good, not truly spicy but has a slight tinge that is just right. The Ivy leaguer, Spring Mac & Popper Mac were also very good. We also had their side of minty peas which was nice. Spicy cauliflower was ok - I would not get that again. The macs are quite filling, so one is good for 2 people. The grilled cheese with jalapeno jam was good, but sweet so you may or may not like it. The peanut butter pie is unique & good. We also liked their brownies & grasshopper pie. They have their homemade drinks like limeade, key lime pie, & rootbeer. The service is good. Lunch is a good time to go, but in the evening, the space gets tight, it is lively & louder. Parking is on the street.

This is probably one of the prettiest parts of Oakland - Jack London Square is right on the water and it's fun to walk along the shops and look at boats. They also have a lot going on - and a great weekly email telling about all their fun activities.

Last weekend they had Tall Ships - a couple of large boats that are being shown there for the next couple of weeks as they make their way up and down the coast. You can tour the boats (only the upper deck, since the crew lives below) and they do a battle between the two boats which you can be onboard during (for $75).  Only one of the ships was harbored when we walked by, but it was cool to check out.

There is a small park for kids, and for adults there is the new Plank bar/restaurant with bowling, arcade, and more! Restaurants, bars, music, desserts. Pretty much everything needed to make a great afternoon or romantic date.

The Jack of All Trades market and the Farmers Market take place on Saturdays and Sundays - really fun to check out!

A couple of weeks ago I had afternoon reservations to attend the Grand Opening celebration of Oakland's new Cat Town Café. I was attending with my husband and one of my best friends (Lauren) who is a resident of Oakland and who suggested we brunch first at The Grand Tavern.  We met at the Tavern bar where Lauren had found a seat but ultimately headed outside to the back patio. I detoured first to a table inside to say hi to two awesome yelp friends (Markus and Elaine - you know who you are, sweetie pies!) Finally making it out back, we found ourselves seated at a bench surrounded with cute Halloween decorations.

I ordered a Bloody Mary ($9), Casey had a Ginger Ale ($3 - much too gingery for him), and Lauren enjoyed a couple Old Cubans ($11 ea).  I didn't find a lot of breakfast items on the menu that really caught my eye. It took several minutes to decided and I ended up ordering the Garden Sandwich ($10). It wasn't really a brunchy meal but I like veggies so I was content - plus it was on Acme bread and that's the best.  Lauren had the PEB ($11) and Casey had the Duck Pate ($9) with a  side of Artisanal Bread ($3). My sandwich was pretty good - I finished the whole thing. Casey was disappointed that the pate was already spread onto pieces of bread, and not served as a whole piece of pate.  His side of bread was very good!

I mostly enjoyed the outdoor seating and the style of the place.  Arlene was our server and she also did a really terrific job.  I'd rather come back here just for the Bloody Marys out back and maybe another side of the bread, but I will definitely come back.

text: Northstar ski resort was a blast to ski at. The lodge was well laid out there were signs everywhere to fine whatever you were looking for. I rented skis there and the staff were fast, efficient, helpful and very informative as I am a first time skier.  They fit me with the right size boots and explained the differences between the different types and sizes of skis from beginner to advanced. They also had a small shop to purchase some goggles and gloves since I didn’t have any of my own. I went with some friends in a Friday morning and stayed all afternoon. It was not too busy and the lines were not long at all. The lifts were quick, comfortable, clean and easy to use for a first timer. I skipped the lessons since I consider myself to be a fast learner.  I did to ribs on the green hills then 2 runs on the blue hills. Then 2 runs on he black diamond hills. My friends were impressed with my quick advancement. They hills were all fun and exciting. Definitely got a workout in on the black hills. There  were well groomed trails with some fresh and some packed snow as it was snowing all day. All in all my experience there was amazing and I would recommend to my friends and family to come here again.

text:
Bivouac is a new, rather unique restaurant and bar that specializes in their own house made cider with alcohol.  The place looks brand new with gorgeous furnishings(I got to sit at a booth with seats suspended from the ceiling that rock...fun).

There is a full bar and restaurant seating.

I had the cider flight consisting of 4 glasses ranging from apple to currant which was my favorite.  The cider is made in large, brand new, very cool looking distilling vats on the premises(that I photographed).

I ordered mussels and their signature "Impossible Burger" with shoestring fries and remoulade.

The mussels are top quality PEI(prince edward island canada) and were plump and exceedingly delicious in the buttery broth.

The burger was cooked perfectly to my specifications with gouda cheese on top and was so tasty; I award it best burger I've had so far this year.

Service by Owner Matt and server Anna was 1st rate.  Matt went over the selections with me and explained some interesting facts about the cider making process.

Bivouac is my favorite restaurant/ bar in North Park now...not bad for only being 8 weeks young.

Fathers Day Brunch price was $30 a person. Paid for two of us. We were not very satisfied with our experience at all. It was not worth the price! Maybe $12.50.

I have visited this location on Fathers Day 2019 for their brunch and I did not find the food to be on a high level of expectation of flavor, texture, some of the meats were overcooked and dry, shrimp dishes were not the best of flavor, but edilble.

The menudo barely had any tripe and only slim pickings were availble probably due to it being very extremely busy, being Fathers Day. Hot chocolate was not hot, just luke warm.

The young waitress never asked if we we alright of if we wanted more water. She never told us that champagne was included in the price either. But thats ok, because we do not drink alcohol. She never smiled at all. I srill tipped her 15% for just serving us ons glass of water and then ignoring us the whole time. I had to call her waving to her for just two straws and she came over unwilling.

However, I did love their corn cake and the flan was excellent.

My family and I have visited and ate at the 18512 MacArthur Blvd, Irvine, CA 92612 location in the past for the brunch and wehave always enjoyed their brunch as their food was very very good and delicious. My co workers and I also enjoyed their brunch as well.

Hopefully the quality their food improves. Hopefully the bad experience was due to the craziness of cooking so much all at the same time, etc.

7/17/13

Right before arriving at Playland-Not-At-The-Beach, my husband had a sudden craving for chicken that he HAD to satisfy. Weird.

There were 3 of us in the car and none had ever been to a Church's before. The drive-thru was like any other, but the menu was new to me! I wasn't at all hungry but I had to try SOMETHING! So I tried the Cajun rice (side) and one piece of crispy chicken. Husband had a chicken sandwich with fries and a drink. Food came pretty quick and I asked for hot sauce, but it was already in the bag. Sweet. Wish I had a couple extra packets. It was pretty good stuff!  My piece of chicken was crunchy and good. I liked the crispy breading but it was a little greasy for me after a few bites. Good flavor though. I don't know how to explain the cajun rice. It was like a mash of rice and meat. We all agreed there was meat in the rice. It's probably my fault for not knowing that cajun rice has meat, but I didn't want unidentifiable meat (or any meat for that matter) in my rice so I tossed this.

Husband's sandwich lasted about as long as my rice. He took a few bites and then took a look inside. The patty just looked really unappetizing. It was a grey-ish color in the middle and something just wasn't right.  His fries ended up in my lap at this point as he tried to wash away all the bad with his giant soda. I decided to abandon my piece of chicken after viewing his. I'd return here, but only for the hot sauce.

text:
I must say I was over the top surprised when I took my first bite. Admittedly, I was disappointed to see udon noodles in the red miso initially. HOWEVER, these noodles were among the BEST I have ever had anywhere. They are cooked perfectly and taste so pure and delicious. Couple these perfect noodles with rich, flavorful broth and ingredients, and you have some of the best noodle soup you'll find anywhere in the world. Bold statement but I assure you it's true.
The gyoza was also very delicious. Crispy and chewy golden brown with a very generous portion of goodness stuffed inside. The dipping sauce was like anywhere else but the gyoza stands on it's own here as a top contender. It's so great that they have spice and fresh minced garlic tableside to add to your liking. Adding just a hint of fresh garlic really set off my spicy red miso ramen.
Please try this place. Incredible!!

Tiny little hole in the wall with exceptionally great food. This place is located inside of a liquor store and is easy to miss. Which may actually turn you off at first... rest assured you need to try this place. The menu will grab your attention quickly with burgers titled, "Ghengis Khan", "The Bull", "Cash", and "Chance". They have Instagram worthy food here. Wide variety, thoughtfulness in every bite.
I had the Cash burger which I would order again without the bbq sauce. It was a little sweet for my taste but you could tell the quality of the meat, bun, and all ingredients are of the highest quality. Every flavor profile is carefully crafted and placed on purpose for your tasting pleasure.
Also had their hand dipped chicken strips. Delicious pepper batter with real chicken breast cutlets. Amazing!
Truffle Fries were as expected delicious. Plenty of parmesan all over, not like moat places where the cheese is used sparingly.
Absolutely eat here.

Overpriced. The soup bowl can't be bigger than one large Campbell's soup bowl. Those cost $1.50 at the grocery store for the "deluxe" soups. Considering shipping costs of Campbell soups their actual cost is likely .75 cents. Humboldt soup co charges 7.50 for this bowl after tax. That means their markup is hovering around 1000%. If their ingredients are locally sourced that likely increases costs to $1.00, then overhead is probably equal to the soup cost, so $2.00, that is still 350% markup. Average restaurant prices are 100% markup. I would suggest that this restaurant increases it's serving size if they want more folks coming back. If I ate my full and still had some leftover I would probably have been a happier customer. I was also expecting a decent bread selection as a side for the soup. All they had was some of those hard biscotti breads (gross) and saltines. Ill might come back here but I won't be a regular. The soup was good but nothing overly spectacular. Staff was very friendly. Their tables are kind of dangerous when I pushed on one side it almost toppled over.

May i suggest having a bottomless soup option? Or how about a nice fresh bread selection to go with the soup? Then it may be worth that $8

Tut's is a new mediterranean restaurant on Washington just west of Inglewood. The food is authentic, very fresh and great tasting.

The Lentil Soup starter was excellent.

I had the 2 meat combo(chicken, Kofta((ground beef))and salmon on the side).  The entree was huge with alot of meat, delicious rice(very well seasoned).

I also had their greek salad which was very big and the feta cheese was very fresh and tasty.

Service was top level by Dio and Nick. These guys are really friendly,  professional, on point and knew the answers to all my foodie questions.

The Baklava dessert made by a Turkish family was one of the best I've ever had.

For food taste, value and service Tut's ranks in my LA top 10 for mediterranean.

I am really looking forward to my next visit.

text:
5/5/15

Service kind of made up for the pricy portions we were forced to swallow at breakfast this morning at Perry's in SFO.  Our server, Amged, steadily flowed from table to table in his section. Nobody had to wait long to get his attention, and he did a good job offering a second round of Bloody Mary's and making sure everything was tasting great.

We declined the second drink. The tiny glasses were $9.50 and had no garnish. Give me an olive! (You can make your drink a double for $3 more.) It was a good indication of what our first meal would look like. Husband had a two egg breakfast for $13.50. It came with toast, potatoes, and he had sausage links for his meat selection. The one slice of sourdough was really hard and dry. Aren't we in sf? Not very many potatoes on the plate, but the ones there were pretty tasty.

I had clam chowder in a bread bowl ($10). Lots of big clam chunks and delicious sourdough bowl. This was the best value on the table. The portion and price resembled what I would expect to get at most places.

text:
This is a cool restaurant only about a year old specializing in Taiwanese street food.

It is located in a small mall in the middle of scenic Chinatown which is close to Union train station and the iconic City Hall building.

I went with the sausage party with rice(includes egg).  This tasted delicious with a large amount of thick rice, corn pickles and spicy sauce that was hearty and flavorful.

The popcorn chicken were also fun to eat with nice consistency, texture and crunchiness.

Lao is on the small side seating wise but they do alot of takeout.

They are on the 2nd floor of the same mall with the popular Howlin' Rays on the ground floor.

Definitely worth a visit and something different from the usual chinese places.

text:
This is my favorite Starbucks because it use to be a burger king and when I was a kid our school bus would actually take us here for some unexplained reason, this sealing a love for the King and his burgers. Fast forward a decade and there I was as a young adult and it had become a cheesesteak shop, the sandwiches were delicious but the big secret was the amazing Mexican food the nice older gals in back would wip up if you knew how to ask, yet it went out of business, dark times indeed.

Skip forward another few years and this guy Bill who while super nice was clearly on some sorta drugs you would buy at a party in sun valley stole the menu from T's Rotisserie in a incline village. This was hilarious to me because the recipies were actually from the family of a man named Sergio whom Bill was also able to steal from T's. I dont know this T person but they were probably upset at this whole situation. Anyway they gave away free food their first day open and I ate 8 burritos. Swear to God, EIGHT over a 10 hour period. We had been lifted from the dark times of no great food next to the mousehole. After what seems like 5 years those party drugs seemed to have done their job and the thousand yard stares from the Bill's Rotisserie senior employees had gotten too consistent. Their talented chef left and opened Golden Rotisserie a few blocks away and sealed this weird buildings fate to be empty again. It was empty and grossly neglected looking for a while. Picture homeless meth heads and bears staying away. Imagine how that feels to see a childhood friend who became a lifelong presence existing like this.

Finally, Starbucks, came to the rescue and remodeled this place into what's now a rather nice location. I was able to convince a girl to move here from another state for this location and my dog so you will have a hard time convincing me it's not the best, highest rated Starbucks in the world, actually. Halle is my favorite barista, she makes the chocolate milk with half coconut milk and it will blow your mind.

A lot of cops hang out here, I dont have a problem with this but you might, man.

Fyi, I dont even like Starbucks or coffee in general so I would imagine if you got this far into my review and are into coffee you will be well served by visiting.

text:
Chardonnay Golf Club is one of the most challenging courses to play in Northern California for all skill levels in golf. The staff is extremely friendly and helpful from Head PGA PRO Bob Becker to the Pro Shop staff including administrative staff to the restaurant staff. I chose to make Chardonnay my golf home and joined the club since it really is the best deal you can get for golf in the Napa Valley. I love the course and it is a great place to work on handicapping as well as play in tournaments. The Members Range is great including the Members area where you can work on your game including a private practice green and bunker.
Roger Billings, Director of Golf is who you want to speak with if you are interested in joining this wonderful semi private, non proprietary club. Start your golf membership today at the Chardonnay Club. It is money very well spent if you golf  2 days per week or more.
I love early morning golf since you can see the sunrise to the wild Canadian geese flying around to seeing the mist rise off the ponds of the course while playing in a links  that has characteristics of a Scottish course. You will never be bored here and it will always present you challenge so do manage your game.
Chardonnay Golf Club truly is a gem of the Napa Valley and already I have met many people who come here from all over the world. World Class Wine is not the only offering of the Napa Valley. Golf at the Chardonnay Club is also a World Class Experience and it offers golf and more!

text:
The moment your boyfriend volunteers to go over the Benicia Bridge with you and wait for your 3 hour hair appointment, you immediately know something's up. But I totally get it! Exploring nearby towns is fun, and Benicia is a great little spot not far from our home, that we don't get out to very often. So Fredie patiently (haha) waited for me at Rookies while I got highlights at Luxe by Colleen.

Once I finished my appointment, I joined him and his new friends and we enjoyed great food and conversation over a few beers. The chicken wings were okay ($12) but we have a couple spots closer to home I like better, a spilled glass of wine (another patron's half full glass) cost us another $7. Which, to be fair, he did spill, but accident's happen and on a $120 tab you'd think they could've just put another splash into a clean glass, imports are discounts to $4 on Tues, Bud Lights are still cheaper at $3.50. Jameson is $7.50 and delicious house-cut garlic fries are only $8.00.

The bartender, Luna, was awesome. She shared about her family's place in Thailand that we'll keep an eye out for when we visit in a few weeks. Another guy behind the bar was also awesome. Overall, wonderful service, drinks, food, and new friends!

1/3/15

My husband took me out to lunch a few weeks ago just before he started his new job -  I picked Oyama because it's close to my office in Walnut Creek. We struggled to find parking - downtown Walnut Creek  isn't my favorite place to spend my lunch breaks because of the parking.  They don't have a private lot here and  the garage on Broadway was completely full; nothing on the streets seemed to be available either but eventually we found something several blocks away.

Casey ordered the Rock and Roll (roll - $7.50) and I had the grilled salmon lunch special ($8.95). The roll was really good but it would have been nice to know that one roll isn't expected to fill you up - be prepared to order two. Also, the salmon was really good but it was also a small piece. The rice on the plate was the only substantial part of my lunch; even the asparagus only consisted of a couple tiny pieces.

Our server (Ken maybe) was awesome. He filled my hot tea for me over and over, even though an adorable tea kettle was left on our table. He was also really friendly and told us all about happy hour and other specials they have. Mr. Eye Candy made us want to come back just so he could be our server again. The food was good enough to return, but next time we'll have to order double the portions.
