text:
The prices are high.

Their social media pricing is deceiving. They have a price rate of "$$" and its should really be labled as "$$$$". The cheapest item on the menu are their Tacos and they are 2.50 per taco.

The water is not Free... its $1 and bottled, also for every drink you order its charged, unlike most restaurants.

The wait for food took a little longer than it should have... we waited for about 30mins. (Our order consist of 3 Tacos & 1 plate of sushi) not to mention they had forgot one of the taco plates and that added to the wait.

Their cutomer service is vague, when addressed about an issue such as forgetting a plate, their waitress gave us a look as though we were wrong. I firmly belive that little saying the customer is always right. Therefor leaving your restaurant with a top notch customer service review, however this was not the case.

When we finally got served, our food was good but its definitely no El Ricon... $2.50 for a pretty plain taco with just cilantro and purple onions is kinda steep, i will admit their taco did have a fairly decent amount of meat, as you can observe from the image posted below.

I came with a friend and the waitress just assumed we were paying together and it was apperant she didnt think to ask, all together or separate. We got the bill and of course it ended up being together, no biggy I love my friend but im seriously at a loss of words with their customer service.

However, The Mangitomich sushi roll was 100% spot on. It's very kid friendly and kid approved. It was topped with mengo, pineapple and a sweet sauce. Even my sick child mustered up some energy to take a few rolls and eat.

One other thing I would like to point out is their outrageous price on their Micheladas. They looked good for $10.00, but as yku can view for yourself, was filled with a large quantity of ice.

40 minute Side Note: Right after eating, We all ended up havent to go to the restroom in a rush.

name: Mark Ames
text:
Check my previous reviews; I've eaten BBQ in the backwoods of North Carolina, in Houston and Dallas and El Paso and lots of BBQ in Kansas City. I say this just to make it clear this review isn't skewed by this restaurant being 2 miles from my house.
Smokin J's is maybe the best BBQ I've ever eaten. Bought the Burnt Ends, Brisket, Pulled Pork and Ribs, along with the Cajun Fries, Cracked Beans, Cole Slaw and Mac and cheese.
All the sides were fine compliments to the meat; none of them were especially special, but they were freshly made and tasty (which is unusual. Most sides are either canned, nasty or boring).
It's the meat that's something special, and actually something rare. The meats are so good and so well prepared I was stunned. The brisket was full flavored and so tender you could cut it with a fork. The pulled pork; cooked to perfection; not greasy or dry. The ribs were excellent, although on the small side, but meaty and not overcooked like most places, and the burnt ends are by far the best I've ever tasted. It actually put all the burnt ends I ever ate anywhere else in the country to shame (and that's a lot of burnt ends).
The sauce was sweet with a nice tang, but I barely used it; didn't want it to take away from the taste of the meat.
Like all BBQ joints it's not a cheap meal, but that's okay. BBQ is supposed to be a treat, not a bargain. I don't know how long this place will be able to keep this level of quality up, or how long they'd be willing to stay in this tiny corner of Poway, but if you're bringing friends or family into town and want to show off, bring your wallet and bring them here. They sure won't be disappointed.
I'd go so far to say this is the best food in Poway, and Poway has some fine choices.

text: This restaurant was such a fun experience. Three of us (60, 72, & 88 years old)  decided to get a burger but we wanted something different. My daughter (27 yrs. old) said that it was one of her favorite eating places where her and her friends can get good food at a reasonable cost. We ordered off of the breakfast & lunch portions of the menu. It took us at least ten minutes to decide because there was five pages of choices. I ordered a waffle and I have to say that it was the worst waffle that I'd ever tasted. So I called the waitress (Shelby) over and explained that I would like to order something else and that the waffle was terrible. She was so sweet about not making me feel crummy about sending back my food. So, I ordered a BLT and it was the best that I'd ever had! So all went well. My two friends also thoroughly enjoyed their meals. Now on to the restaurant..... It was so cool because the walls were covered with everything from the 50's. Cars, pictures, Christmas decorations and anything else from that era that you can think of! We were there about an hour mainly looking at everything. They even had the walk of stars. It was just too cool! 😎 I can honestly say that this was the most enjoyable lunch that I'd had in a very long time. We paid our bill and left a nice tip for our waitress who was a wonderful asset to our experience. As we were walking out, I walked up to Shelby and handed her an extra $6.00 tip and I told her thank you again for not making me feel bad about sending back my waffle. She gave me a big smile and that made me feel even better. So, if you want a great lunch (except for the waffles) along with a trip back to the "good old days of the 50's", stop by and enjoy the abundance of choices including breakfast, lunch or dinner and their friendly staff and great service. Thanks Chubby's ☺ for the yummy food!

name: Endless Possibles
text:
MUST TRY! Wow, talk about a food joint that puts passion into what they do. This is one of those rare eatery's that actually cares about what they serve you.
I had the Pastrami. Here's what it was like:
Super fresh artisan roll, not too crunchy, not too soft with good flavor and consistency. Perfect for a pastrami. They're spin on this delicious sandwich is a Cole slaw lathered in a delicious chipotle sauce. The cheese tastes of great quality and the Boars Head pastrami is delicious. It's got delicious dill pickles with some unique mustard, not deli mustard, more of a yellow 2.0 .  It helps that it is prepared by someone who cares what you're about to eat. The potatoes salad was so good I had to ask about it. The potatoes weren't soggy but also not undercooked. These folks have clearly been in the food game a long time, sprinkled with some paprika and not too oniony, the perfect side to my sandwich.
The ambience is cute and welcoming. The bar I found out is old basketball court planks which is a cool story and looks outstanding (I sat and ate at the bar). The owners are a husband and wife who were both there and very tentative. The service was over the top good and personal.
The iced tea was fresh brewed and slightly on the strong side for a clean rich flavor. I like when places do this because you can always dilute it with water (my dad likes weak tea, I prefer STRONG). I cant stress enough how noticeable it is that not only have these folks been doing this a long time (it shows in their food and their efficiency) but also that the truly care about what you're about to eat. Massive win from this place I recently found out about.
I'll be back way too often.

I had not visited in years and now it will become a regular for me. It's a very small interior so dont plan any large groups in the winter, but that is also one of the things that will draw me here. Make a reservation and have a mellow date here. The food quality and presentation are on par with the best fine dining you will have in Tahoe, especially Tahoe city. Portions are filling and abnormally cheap. Its BYO beer or wine so I suggest a visit to the West Shore Market or similar if you want alcohol. All of the staff was welcoming, even the cooks engaged with us and our server, Kristen, was super helpful and friendly. Will be back many more times.

name: Jonathan Adler
text:
I was walking down the street in the Gaslamp district and saw this really cool sign for Tony's Pizza that reminded me of classic Italian places on the East Coast where I'm from.

I was greeted by a really nice and professional man at the counter who turned out to be the Owner, Brent(points for that because of all the chains now with employees that don't care about their business and absentee owners who are just about their "investment" or tax write off).

I was really hungry and had the Pizza large supreme and Stromboli.  The cheese, crust were amazing and the tangy, super flavorful sauce was phenomenal.  I am not a big eater but basically devoured the huge pizza in a short time because it was so good and I was so hungry.

The stromboli and zucchini sticks were also outstanding and large portions.  They even had my favorite blue powerade from the drink machine.

They deliver and do takeout and are very busy on the weekends as word gets out about the great pizza.

I think Tony's is the best pizza restaurant in downtown san diego.

Highly recommended.

name: Jonathan Adler
text:
I was strolling down Pico just west of Westwood Ave and thought this restaurant looked really cool from the outside.  I was not disappointed and immediately enjoyed the chilled, upscale and fun ambience.

Backdoor has a nice combination of fine Asian dining and full bar with an excellent drink selection.

I started out with the "Blushing Geisha"(one of the best drink names I've ever seen-points) which consists of premium Le Poire/Grey Goose vodka, soho lychee and fresh lime. It was worthy of the name.

The Manager, Jun, also provided me their best Sake which was in fact the best I've ever had...strong effect and not too sweet, with no bad aftertaste like others I've tried.

My softshell crab starter was phenomenal(crispy shell cooked perfectly with soft tasty meat)...best I've had in the last few years.

They are known for the Yakitori(Japanese shish ka bob) which was also excellent.  I really liked the ribeye, filet and shitake mushroom.

I'm a shrimp lover and the shrimp tempura was above average portion sized and delicious.

The sushi nigiri-yellowtail, eel, tuna and salmon were also superb.

Service by Jun and staff was outstanding with just the right amount of cordiality and attentiveness.

The Backhouse earns my top choice for Japanese Yakitori and Asian style drinks(#1 Sake) on the westside.  I plan to check out their happy hour deal on my next visit.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
12/26/17

My boyfriend and I braved the recent So Cal fires and drove down for our friend Zach's surprise 40th birthday party and the coinciding lighted boat parade in Huntington Beach. Before returning home on Sunday morning (Dec. 10th), we stopped a few doors down from our beach-front hotel and grabbed breakfast at Woody's. (Our friend Chad from Phoenix had also attended the party and recommended Woody's to us before hitting the road to go back home himself, since he had just finished breakfast there.)

Dude. So good. Really cute environment and good value on the delicious food, but what really stood out was the service! Our waitress wasn't the only one provided us with great service-with-a-smile throughout the entire meal. Every single staff person we encountered greeted us as they walked by, asked how we were doing, refilled our coffees, cleared plates, etc.. It really seemed like everyone who works there truly loves their job! Plus, they have fantastic deals on morning-time mimosas and Bloody Marys (though, we just stuck to coffee due to the long trek home). $25.71 total for both meals and drinks.

When I dream and crave about Moules (mussels) and frites (fries), the Marinière is what I crave. Garlic, white wine, lemon juice & parsley sauce. Amazing.

text:
I guess the food is suppose to be from Xi'an China.  I was just in Xi'an and I can say they missed the mark.

One of the worst meals I've had.  The sweet and sour chicken with baing baing noodles was bad.  The chicken was glazed in a hard candy glaze that was overly sweet.  It was served on top of the thick wide noodles, with broccoli on the side.  There was no sauce on the pasta or broccoli. And the broccoli wasn't seasoned.  Adding hot sauce (chili oil) on the side helped, but it didn't make up for the lack of flavor.  The service was ok, but it was so loud in the restaurant that it was hard to hear the cashier.

The other frustrating thing is the homemade noodles.  Instead of calling them "house made noodles" or "wide noodles" they called them Biang Biang noodles.  I wasn't sure if the pronunciation, nor is it noted on the menu.  So when the cashier said do you want Ramen, I said, no I'll have the other.  Which she then replied "Which one?"  So I was forced to butcher the pronunciation.  I understand Biang Biang noodles is the official name, but can you just call them Bang Bang noodles, or add that below the actual name in quotes?  They put meat paste and not Ròu jiàng which are the same.  Make it easy to be a customer!

Terrible experience. I ordered delivery from Mel’s. I live about 1 mile from this location. The expected delivery time was an hour. Mind you I know they didn’t need to make my food (meatloaf dinner) as it’s something already cooked. After an hour they changed the quote to 2 hours. I called and the restaurant said my food was ready and would picked up soon. It finally arrived after 95 minutes of waiting.

I guarantee if I went into the restaurant in person it would not take 60 minutes to get my food once I place my order.

On top of that my meatloaf was only half meatloaf. It was a very thin slice of meatloaf served on top of a dry hamburger patty. I’m not making this up. They were different textures. The meatloaf part was delicious!

I also ordered cheesecake which for $8 was a thin slice of frozen cheesecake. Such a rip off. I get the same exact cheesecake when I order pizza for half the price.

So many other places in San Francisco to get diner food.

Usually good but not tonight.  Table dirty, server SLOW.  Not what I expect from this Chili's.  It's been a year since I had the opportunity to dine here.  In the past, I have enjoyed great food, good service, and the place was clean.

This time the gentleman helping the hostess brought us to a table that needed to be wiped down and had a few pieces of papers from the straws littering the table.  The gentleman brushed his hand across the table then walked away.   My husband ended up cleaning the surface.

Our server took our drink order but walked away as we asked a menu question.  Two other employees to ask her to come back to our table and she still took 20 minutes. Once answering, we asked her to come back in one minute so we could decide  what to purchase with the additional information she finally provided.  It was at least 15 minutes before we saw her again.

At least the food was good and still hot when it arrived.  After another 15 minutes, we were given the check.  The server walked away before we could ask for boxes for the uneaten food (who can eat that quickly?) She came back a bit later to see if we were ready to pay.  Did we need help with the quiosk?  Getting boxes after that was quick.  I guess she wanted to turn the table for more tips.

In total, we were in the restaurant a little over 3 hours and were given 15 minutes between the arrival of the food and the arrival of the check.

I will go back because of previous good service, but if I have a similar experience, I'm done with Chili's for good.

My meal was so disappointing.  BUT my husband's crunch roll was HUGE and delicious, and about $5, and his Super California roll (closer to $10), was also huge and really good. Before your food arrives, you get the free items mentioned above. The miso soup has no tofu or seaweed, just broth, and salad was really heavily dressed, but hey, it was free.

The employees here are very nice. You can tell they are very hard-working. But a little more attention to detail would go a long way here. (Like clean menus). name: Amy Palmer
text:
9/16/15
This small taqueria sits in the Four Corners shopping plaza at the Monument and Oak Grove Rd. intersection. It's across the street from Milo's Lounge, which may be important if you want a beer with dinner. I think I saw sangria in their soda fridge, but I don't recall seeing any Coronas.

My husband and I came in for dinner tonight and I ordered 3 tacos ($1.50 each): pollo (chicken), carne asada (beef), and adobada (seasoned pork). They didn't have a fish option or a veggie option (perhaps they will add to their menu as they grow). I also didn't see guacamole on the menu (side note: today is National Guacamole Day!) but you won't need guacamole with your chips if you like spicy salsa. Free chips are served to guests dining in the restaurant in a basket with a large bowl of a red salsa that was more like a hot sauce. It was a really liquid consistency, but maybe that's to protect the consumer - this stuff is spicy!! They also have two bowls of salsa on the counter (the type that they make the salsa in by smashing all the ingredients on the rough walls of the bowl). When they bring out your food they include two more hot sauce bottles (both a red and a green), plus they have a variety of premium hot sauce bottles on each table.

It's a family owned restaurant and so other menu items may appear and the salsas may change based on ingredients/tastes; and so far, so, so good! Our tacos quickly came out with steaming grilled onions on top. Each taco is served on two small, fresh, corn tortillas, and they pile on the meat and fresh onion/cilantro topping in large mounds on the warm shells. Really great value and the food was delicious. text:
Wow, some of the best Chinese food I’ve had!

Kenny’s is located off the beaten path in a shopping center. There is ample parking in the parking lot. When you get inside you seat yourself. Staff is friendly and eager to help. Make sure you check out the daily specials. They serve a lot of Chjnese food, but also a smaller American food menu. At first I overlooked the American food, but I noticed many people ordering the Prime Rib special.

The general chicken I got was amazing. Huge pieces of flavorful chicken, light on the sauce, mixed with onions, and fresh broccoli on the side. I get this dish from various Chinese food places in the Bay Area at least once a week and Kenny’s was the best.

The egg roll was interesting. At first when you get it it looks huge! It’s about twice the normal size. But then you realize it’s double fried. The outer breading is a more puffy breading. It wasn’t bad, but not great.

I’ll be back. Now to decide if I want General Chicken again or American food. Mmmm...

10/12/14

With less than two hours before our plane was scheduled to leave San Diego, we sat down with our friends for one final meal. Naturally, I wanted tacos and chips and salsa, because that's pretty much what i always want.

We told our server we were in a rush and he quickly took our orders. A basket of chips was brought to the table but halfway into it all we found were tiny little broken corners of chips, too small to even dip in the salsa. I had asked twice for a spicier salsa, which he said they had, but he forgot to bring until the end of the meal. Also forgotten were the beans and rice or friend ordered, but we ran out of time to get it removed from the bill.

Drinks were kept full, although my husband's soda had iced tea on accident with one refill. My tacos were good. Also had a bite of husband's taquitos but they were just too crunchy and we didn't care for them. A good quesadilla was shared by one of our friends. Not bad. Honestly the chips and salsa were the best things on the table. Wish we'd been given fresh, full chips instead of pieces. Both salsas were really outstanding. Even if you have to ask a few times, be sure to ask for the spicy; it's so so good.

TLDR; Order canceled after we left the drive thru speaker, and never bothered to get it right. Not the first or even the second time based off multiple regulars I've talked to for this review. Find a reason to go to the Santee or Chula Vista location. Terrible drive thru lines, and even worse parking during high traffic hours

The Juicy Review:
I'm sorry I have to do this to you, Wendy. I thought what we had was special!! What's not to get right? Four meals with standard drinks and an additional sandwich. No substitutions requested. Sounds easy, especially when the customer make the extra effort to be clear and concise. No mix-ups and convenient service between customer and company; all that fast food should be. Apparently, that's too much for the Spring St. Wendy's.

This is the input of my experience as well as my fellow consumers, if you will, that informs you of the pattern of this Spring St. circus act. This is the experience you're going to have when you visit this location. I understand mix ups happen all the time, but when is it going to be enough? I had to get the attention of the drive thru cashier three different times to completely correct or remind them of what I ordered. That's terrible. People get impatient behind you, and the line keeps growing. Fast food becomes a marathon of patience for room temp food and finding out they got only half of it right . Balance out the incompetency by getting some new blood in there and sending the other mooks out to pasture Wendy, come on.

In the end, I'm still going to go to this Wendy's. Wendy's is just too tasty, even when it's all lukewarm. That, and I'm not driving to Santee or Chula just to get a burger, but I'm definitely checking my order at the order screen, receipt, or bag twice. Remember, you've been warned. Don't be surprised when the 2+ meals you ordered brings the circus to Spring St.

name: Jack Flynn
text:
Brunch is great.  View is Great. A must go for Sunday Brunch.

If you are Staying in the San Luis Obispo or Pismo Beach area, this is a must go for Sunday Brunch.  Make sure to make a reservation, as this place fills up fast.

Doors open at 10:00am and there is a line starting around 9:45am.  When you get inside, you're given a table, told that there are bottomless mimosas and bloody marys and you can stay as long as you want.

As the cost is pretty expensive, over $40.00 for brunch, make sure you are hungry or go with the plan to stay for awhile.  They are always changing up the buffet and have wonderful food.

The service is wonderful, their staff is attentive and wants to make sure that you have a perfect brunch.  There was live music, soft, not too loud, and fun.  The food is better than any buffet I've had, piles of crab legs, fresh made tortillas, omelets, desserts, carving station, and loads of other items.

To sum it all up, make a reservation, get there early, go hungry, stay for as long as you can.

For dessert, I had the sweet cinnamon strips which were delicious.

Pieology now ranks in my top ten fast food pizza restaurants ever been list and number one for VALUE!

text: The Corona Airport Cafe is delightful.  It's over by the little Corona Airport, and now it's completely open.  A couple weeks back it had outside dining only, but now it's both inside and outside.  I have been going there with family and friends the last few weekends - Saturday morning is a great time.  The service is fast and proficient.  The cooking is quite good, and they have a varied menu that is somewhat original.  A real highlight of the food is their biscuits and chorizo gravy.  I suppose you can have regular white gravy, like everybody else serves, but the slightly-pink-brown chorizo gravy is the best gravy I've ever tasted.  I've only been there for breakfast, so I can't comment on their lunches, but I can say that their breakfasts easily compete with anybody else in Corona.  They're a mix between all-American and Mexican ... kind of a Mexican-American fusion.   Try it, you'll like it!

name: Richard E. Gentry
text: Dickey's Barbecue Pit is the first franchise barbecue joint in Compton, ever. Compton has always had good barbecue. Really Good Barbecue! But many of the local pit masters have closed, retired or passed on. Thus, leaving a void in the city. A void that even a franchise barbecue joint can fill. Fortunately, Dickey's is bringing it. Offering real barbecue, for people who know real barbecue. With tasty sides, desserts and even Sweet Tea (anyone with Southern roots can appreciate that). And they do it in a nice setting (clean dining room and restrooms), with a great staff, that are trained to give good service. Although, they are a franchise, so don't expect the portions sizes that the locals have grown accustomed to. But after you experience the ribs, brisket, links and pulled pork, you'll know why Dickey's Barbecue Pit is the first franchise barbecue joint in Compton, ever. And hopefully they are here to stay.

It creates an atmosphere that help customers relax, get comfortable, and excited. Personally, i call it a visual polution that unfortunately make people do or buy  something that they would not ordinarily do. The items in this store look very appetizing; however, they contain little to no nutrients. As a result, after eating them, my body, for instance, does not identify any sense of fullness or satiety. Even though all items are  very delitious and nice looking, they lead to increased hunger and overeating. Keeping all these in mind i purchased no more than just 2 items at the time. Finally, i did not see any gluten free bakeries in this store. Everyone knows that gluten can cause serious health complications. I wish this store sells at least one or two items that are healthy. 7/26/15

My husband and I went to La Veranda Cafe for dinner a couple of months ago after watching our friend's kids play a little league game at Clayton Community Park up the road. The Warriors game was on and we'd already missed the first half to watch the Littles play, so we cozied up to the bar where a small, silent TV sat in front of us. But it was better than nothing.

Delicious, delicious bread soon came out. I think one of the types was rosemary - it was my favorite. I ordered the calamari appetizer and Casey had a personal pizza. My calamari was served with warm marinara sauce and it was really flavorful. The pieces themselves were tender and good but the sauce was especially memorable. I'd definitely return for more food.

Service was good I guess - employees were friendly but probably could have made a little more effort to interact with us since we were already sitting so close to them (and there was some food prep going on in front of us since the kitchen isn't far from the bar either), and it's not like we had volume on the TV. Hostess was pleasant but not especially warm or welcoming.

name: Trevor Kadletz
text:
I feel the majority of restaurants in Montrose and the surrounding communities are mediocre at best and only stay in business as a result of convenience. Sometimes it's easier to settle for less instead of driving 10-15 minutes away and having to deal with busier street traffic and crowded parking structures.

With that said I would describe Portebello's as mediocre and of course I will explain why. I met my parents for dinner and this was the restaurant they chose, despite growing up in the area and still living locally this was my first time eating here. The ambiance is pleasant and the staff is very friendly, I particularly enjoyed the large windows offering a nice view of Honolulu. My mother ordered first and asked for the filet mignon, surprisingly she was informed they were out of the filet despite being one of the first tables to be seated at 5:00 on a Saturday evening. This was strike one. When it was my turn to order I couldn't decide between two items, both having filet as the main ingredient, so asking our server she recommended what's essentially beef schnitzel. The breading on the filet tasted equivalent to the breading on fast food chicken strips and the filet inside was over cooked and tasteless. This was strike two. Trying to make the best of the situation I asked our server if they had a sauce similar to A1 (thinking they wouldn't have A1), to my surprise I was told they have A1 and she would bring it right away. Almost immediately a different server is at my side apologizing because they are out of A1. This was strike three. My father thinking I was exaggerating about the lackluster taste of my meal decided to try a bite, it was then he realized I wasn't exaggerating in the slightest. I also sampled a bite of my brothers lobster ravioli which was nothing to write home about.

Having only eaten here the one time and having no prior visits for comparison it is possible my experience was unusual. However I will say that not a single member of my dinner party so much as commented negatively or positively during or after our meal.

text:
We've been to Thailand twice and Erawan is definitely serving authentic Thai Cuisine.

Whenever we eat @ a Thai restaurant we've never been to, we order items which we can experience at least 4 out of 5 senses-salty, sweet, sour, spicy, and bitter.

So we ordered the satay chicken, stuffed chicken wings, roti with a side of curry sauce, pad kee mao - pan fried flat rice noodles with basil, chili, and vegetables.  Prawn & calamari pad prig-sauteed prawn, calamari and vegetables, and chili. Also, tom yum soup and fried bananas dipped in batter served with coconut ice cream.

Everything was fresh and delicious. There was so many levels of flavor! The portions were adequate, prices were ave compared to other Thai restaurants in SJ, the service was ok. Would have been 5 stars if the staff weren't so robotic. They didn't smile or were attentive.

There was a total of 3 tables with customers including us. But they were 3 times busier with take outs. They should have more staff dedicated to the take out orders.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
2/21/18

Time after time I've enjoyed my stops in at Domenico's on the Monterey Fisherman's Wharf. This weekend's visit was not a disappointment. Service really made the afternoon; Joaquin was our awesome food-server, but several other people checked in on our table to make sure we were happy and well-treated.

We started with two Bloody Marys ($25 total), followed by a clam chowder bread bowl ($14.95). We decided to share the bowl which the person taking our order seemed to imply wasn't enough for two, even making a hand single of the size which was half of what the true size was (which is a normal bread bowl serving). (Same bread bowls are available to-go in other wharf restaurants for $10.) Trying to upsell us an extra bread bowl was kind of a turn-off. We were on vacation and this was not our only food stop, so no need to fill up all in one place. But aside from that, service was stellar and food/drinks were as good as we expected.

5/19/14 - Four stars

My husband and I are semi-regular visitors of the Wharf in Monterey.  By no means are we tourists, but by all means we do enjoy playing the "let's try every free sample of chowder we can" game.

The person representing each restaurant, standing outside offering clam chowder samples, has the task of bringing the customers inside.  Yesterday I felt like we walked past robot after robot, until we came to the adorable face outside Domenico's.  I'll be honest, we were going to stop in here anyhow for a $3 Happy Hour drink in the lounge, but we stood out front for a minute first savoring some delicious hot chowder.  Lo and behold, the guy out front wasn't just repeating himself over and over about chowder and drink specials. He was telling potential customers about the restaurant's owner, and how he personally catches the fish he serves and is also friends with the nearby crabbers, to ensure freshness in every dish. This is the type of person you want standing out front!

We cozied up to the bar and I was happy to see a new face.  Often times we've had service from an older gentleman who talks sports with my husband, but today it was a younger bartender who included me in the conversation too.  Trevor was very personable and told us about the lounge renovations, talked about types of tequila, explained the pineapple-infusion I noticed behind him, and more. How lucky were we! Two employees so far who were both outgoing AND easy on the eyes! There are tons of nice places on the Wharf with great views and fresh fish.  The staff are what keep us coming back to this one.

The views through the window-wall here really are spectacular.  The women's restroom is in the very back so you walk past the gorgeous dining room to get to it. Walk to the back and enjoy the view! It's such an outstanding location.
(Note: women's restroom had classy, beach-themed decorations and was very clean.)

We did see a manager-type individual walking around through the lounge, dining area, and even up to the bar. It goes a long way when a higher-up stops to personally interact with customers.  Asking if they're enjoying their food/drinks, or casually thanking them for coming in doesn't take much time - especially when youre already walking past them over and over. That's such a nice touch, but this one only interacted with his staff.

Overall this is a great place to stop: for food, drinks, and if youre lucky, perhaps a little eye candy as well.

text:
5/25/15

We were most recently at La Tapatia for a PaintNite event, which was a night of painting led by an experience instructor. Here it was in a private room outside of the restaurant's main dining area. I'd previously attended a private surprise birthday party held in this same room, but have also eaten in the restaurant once.

PaintNite is super fun and the instructed painting sessions take place at a variety of restaurants. I can't wait to attend another one! La Tapatia provided servers to take drink and food orders for our room of amateur painters. Most people were only ordering drinks, but a few people wanted food and/or chips and salsa. I only wanted chips and salsa, but thought I had to order food to get some, so I settled on a side order of French Fries. We ordered a couple of drinks which came out pretty quickly (the bar was on-point all night), but the fries still hadn't arrived by our class' first break, so I asked one of the servers to check on my order. Shortly after, a plate of cold fries were delivered. Okay, so not "cold", but not warmer than room temperature, and not hot! Soft, soggy, room temperature fries ($4).

Chips and salsa were tasty though - and the event was a lot of fun - we'd definitely return if they back to this location. (We found a great deal for PaintNite on Groupon!!)

HOPE THE MEAT'S FRESHER THAN THE JALAPENOS

The meat counter here actually looked really good. I understand why all the reviews are happy with it. I came for the produce though and it was a tiny section of tired greens. I picked through the jalapenos to find one that didn't have the black spots that turn into bigger black spots of mold. Only found one that called my name and grabbed an avocado and bottle of coke to go with it.

The avocado was $1.29 and I assume the medio litro bottle (the large one) was about the same because my total was under $4. The girl at the register and didn't give me a hard time about using Visa to make a $3 dollar purchase, so that was cool.  I felt pretty cramped in the small store. Living close to Monument spoils me I think. Not a bad place for this area, but I need something bigger when doing my shopping. With fresher jalapenos.

The guy goes and asks his manager and comes back to me and says his manager said they can sing happy birthday but you have to purchase the desert. I said no thanks. It's not the point. 6/14/13

HABANERO TOBASCO! BE MINE!!

It was soooo late at night when we stopped in here. I wanted something to eat and can pretty much always go for a crispy hashbrown. Even though he'd just had hot chocolate at the casino, husband wanted MORE hot chocolate.

Two amazing things happened while we sat here. First, I learned about Tobasco's new habanero hot sauce. F*kn awesome. It was good! I put it all over my hashbrowns and spoon. I felt it would be too hard to steal this since the place was empty, but the thought crossed my mind. It was the best thing about the hashbrowns, which were crispy-ish, but so greasy I actually took a napkin to them, and I NEVER do that until it hits a certain level of grossy greasy.

The second great thing was the hot chocolate, which comes in a mini mug, has a free refill. He opted for a refill but just couldn't get the second one down. Too much chocolate! It was very rich and good. Whipped cream on top.

Service was nice. I felt bad for the waitress who had to work such late hours. She did a good job!

Total $11.68 - (husband had pancakes too but I didn't try these)

1/3/15

My husband and I visited a friend in San Diego 3 months ago and one of our first stops was to Bootlegger Plates & Pours. The bar is really open with lots of natural light and fresh air. The 3 of us found a table by a window and enjoyed watching people walk by while we feasted.

Coors was on special for $3 and I think the waitress misunderstood when I asked if this included Coors Light, because I was brought a can of Coors Banquet. Not my favorite, but the price was right. It was followed by a pint of Gunslinger ($4), Mule ($8), a Bug Light draft ($4) and eventually my bottle of Coors Light ($5).

Our table shared several small plates form the happy hour menu: Jumbo prawns, seared ahi, and ahi poke ($7 each) and a delicious mac-n-cheese ($10).  The mac n cheese was a huge portion and it was delicious - the prawns were also very good and easy to share!

Service was kind of slow but Lala was very nice and checked on us often to make sure we didn't need anything else. Just under $60 and a great way to start our San Diego vacation - everything about this place made us feel welcome and it was a beautiful and fun environment.

name: Endless Possibles
text:
Really great burger place! The service was slower than it should have been but hey, they just reopened from the whole pandemic nonsense, so I forgive it. I ordered the
DECLARATION DAY Burger: Let's start with the patty, killer meat! Not over salted or seasoned. Pure, delicious beef with great flavor. So many burger joints get their meat from the same suppliers and just fall into the salty trap. Not here. This is genuinely delicious meat you're getting. The next most important part of a delicious burger is the bun... thisnplace serves fresh, squishy with a little bit of chew Brioche buns. Theyre very delicious and have great texture. Lastly, the lettuce seemed a bit old but still tasted of quality. The tomatoes were clearly fresh and so were the pickles. Lightly spread with 1000 island and you've got one hell of a delicious, no nonsense burger.
Fries: the fries were very generic beer battered fries but honestly tasted great! I didn't expect some unique one of a kind fry here so don't get my wrong. The fries are a great accompaniment to their burgers. Beer battered and fried golden brown with a nice crisp. No undercooked sog nonsense here.. delicious, crispy, seasons battered fries. Delcious
Cream Cheese Eggrolls: Beware on this one. I actually had to sneak a peek at the menu on my way out to make sure I didn't miss something... whatvim talking about is a smokey flavor. This completely ruined it for me. It is NOT disclosed on the menu that they have a smokey cream cheese so if you are not a fan of smoked cheese like I am not, it actually makes me a little sick... then avoid these. The shell is crispy and delcious and the avacodo melts nicely in your mouth. They would be great if they offered a non smokey taste option or if they at least disclosed it on the menu.
House made Blueberry applesauce: this was a must try. Its a sugary overload of a apple sauce and I LOVED IT! So yes, it tasted like freaking candy more than applesauce but hey, I'm not complaining haha. It has a bit of a cotton candy like flavor coming from something... if you're okay with trying something sweet and very unique, give this a shot.
Overall, I was very pleased with this spot. I own a place near the village and will absolutely return here.
I did not try the beers as they were overpriced for my opinion. The tourists will happily pay it and I'm okay with that.
The theme of the restaurant is music btw with guitars and drum cymbals hanging on the walls. The chalk wall outside is fun.

name: Pensive Pundit
text:
I visited Rodrigo's Mexican Grill in Corona (near Norco) and had a great time.  We went about 6 pm on a Friday night, and we were seated in the outside patio, which is pretty big, with about 50 other people.  The patio has a wood-grill cover, so sun is substantially blocked, and it almost feels like sitting inside the restaurant.  There were 6 of us, and they seated us at a larger table that easily accommodated our food.  It was very noisy in that patio, and we could barely hear each other, but it was FUN!  It was really lively,  and very active.  It's just great to visit a place like that.

The food came fast, and it was delicious, and, wow, they really served a lot for guys like me who has a huge appetite.   The warm chips and tasty salsa kept coming too, all throughout our meal.  The drinks we ordered were delicious too.

Honestly, when the server took our orders, I figured he would get them all wrong because it was so noisy, and I'm sure he could barely hear us.  I was prepared for that, because it was simply that noisy.  We told him it would be 3 separate checks too, and I figured that would cinch it that the checks would be wrong.  Two of the checks had a large guacamole bowel on them, and all three had two different drinks on each check.   Well, when our meals were over, we got the checks, and they were spot-on perfect!

The meal was a great success and we all had a great time at Rodrigo's Mexican Grill in Corona.  They perform at 100% , even during the Covid-19 difficulties.  I give them 5 stars for great food, for a great and fun environment on the patio, and for 3 perfectly detailed checks.  Big tips for the server!

text:
7/14/14

This girl loves her veggies. I also love pizza, so, naturally, my favorite pizza has lots and lots of veggies on it.  My least favorite type of pizza is the "two topping" or "three topping" version - how do I decide what topping I want? I generally veer toward veggie specials when they're offered, wishing the price didn't go up with each topping on a custom slice. Oh, happy day when I walked into Pieology Pizzeria.

Our first visit to Pieology was today and a happy day it is.  My husband and I  were finally at the front of line and had two crusts flattened out for us in an awesome pizza pressing machine.  The manager was wonderful as he told me about the options: my husband put herb butter sauce and two types of cheese on his pie, I picked red sauce for mine (they also add a little olive oil to keep the crust from burning).  I had mozzarella and gorgonzola on top of the sauce.

Then, the veggie station.  Casey skipped this step and layered on the meat. I, however, tried to picture a pizza with all the veggie choices they offered. In my mind, it was crazy talk, so I picked three or four favorites. Or maybe it was five but who's counting?! Not the nice girl on the veggie station; she was happy to put on as many as I wanted.  She properly placed my mushroom, olive, artichoke, jalapeno, and garlic choices. And by "properly", I mean that they were evenly spread about the pizza.

Our slices were cooked "well done" at our request and were still out in a handful of minutes, being delivered to our table by another friendly face. They only had a staff of four out front - and the food and service was excellent. Hot, fresh, fast, tasty. Everything you want in thin crust pizza.

I had mine finished with a pesto sauce and hubby's was drizzled in ranch. That's the beauty of this place. It's totally customizable - and they have something for everyone.  Less than $10 each and the pizza was big enough to take (a little) home.  Can't beat that price! Even sodas were only $1.75, and that seems low.

I will be back for more tasty pizza. I can't count the times I've complained that "all the good pizza is on the other side of the tunnel", and even last week someone asked me for a pizzeria recommendation, and I said "Oakland". This is my new favorite local pizza for sure.

text:
4/19/13

IF YOU LIKE SHOPPING, YOU'LL LIKE BROADWAY PLAZA

If you're looking for the actual Walnut Creek (as in H2O), it once flowed where Broadway Plaza stands now. Walnut and San Ramon Creeks were covered over during construction. Imagine the outcry from environmental groups if you tried to build a shopping plaza over a creek now! But 60 years ago this must have been less of an issue because today stands an outdoor shopping plaza that other malls nationwide have tried to recreate. The design of the plaza is very shopper-friendly.

Going hand-in-hand with the scenic, outdoor mall, is the great weather of the Bay Area. Who wouldn't love walking around the shops and fountains with the sun shining on your shoulders?!

I don't like shopping. At all. But I do enjoy walking around Broadway Plaza.
The See's candy store is my favorite. Free sample if youre in line!

5/9/13 - Broadway Parking Garage

MORE GREAT PARKING IN WALNUT CREEK

Come one, come all! Bring your cars and park on Broadway! This inexpensive parking lot is much more spacious than the nearby one that always seems crowded in front of Jamba Juice/Starbucks/Bank of America. They are literally only a couple blocks apart.

The Bay Area is known for it's beautiful weather. Enjoy it as you walk to your destination from the Garage on Broadway. Nearby shops and restaurants are abundant. Broadway Plaza isn't all that far and there's so much nearby on Main and Locust streets. Your car will be safe here while it waits for you.

Back again for breakfast with my boyfriend. Holy smokes! The corned beef hash here is my new fave. It's a juicy, flavorful breakfast that made me wish I had ordered it for myself instead of having to steal so many bites from Fred's plate.

My combo breakfast with apple sausage and bacon, potatoes, and eggs was also delicious. Both meals came with sourdough Acme bread. $27.36 including our two coffees. Such a good deal!! Perfect portions and exceptionally good taste! Plus, Molly was an excellent server throughout our meal. Cannot wait to go back!!

7/25/14 - four star

Husband and I were rewarded with Benicia's downtown dollars after doing a favor for a co-worker. We decided to put the dollars to work at First Street Café.  I was disappointed to hear they were out of clams (mussels too!) as I'd been thinking about shellfish all day long. I settled for a Cobb Salad and went with the small option for $10.  Husband had a 6 oz steak sandwich, ordered rare ($15, I think).

After a basket of yummy bread our food arrived. I had to confirm that the salad I received was the "small".  I filled the to-go container I had brought from home for leftovers, before I even started eating. There was soooo much salad! A delicious blue cheese dressing on top left me very satisfied. My poor husband on the other hand picked at very fatty pieces of overcooked, tough meat. I rarely see him cut off fat, but the huge amounts of fat he cut off this small steak were unbelievable. He said something to our server Lisa and she righted the situation.

Actually, Lisa made everything about our dinner service nice. Even teasing me when she caught me licking my finger after running it through the oil on my bread plate. Holy cow, I have no manners sometimes. (Delicious olive oil does that to me.)

I'm not really a dessert person but I've had crème brulee on my mind for a while. When Casey got up to look at their dessert cooler, I followed and spoke for us both when I ordered the  custard.  He got all sugar-crazy-eyed and ordered a chocolate, salted caramel mousse dessert as well.  We actually couldn't finish either one.  We were so full!

Oh, man. Now all I can think about is crème brulee! I want more crème brulee!!  I wish I'd brought the leftover crème brulee home with me (even though it was only a couple spoonfuls left!) Yes, it was that good.
(At least I have a large container full of leftover salad.)

I came for lunch 8/9/12 and was going to just go through the drive-thru then head back to work and eat at my desk, but when i arrived I noticed the drive-thru was empty and the parking lot was full. Seriously, I got the last spot! This intrigued me so I decided to dine-in.

I went in and ordered my crunchy tacos and found one of the few tables that wasn't taken. Very quickly my order was ready and it was served on a clean tray which I took back to my table. I noted the clean floors and counters and table tops.

The employees were fast, friendly, and obviously very busy.

I enjoyed my  lunch inside and watched groups and other singles dine around me.  It was much better than sitting back at my work desk to eat. Plus, the tacos were awesome. Even distribution of lettuce and cheese. Consistent quality across the board! Hmmm, writing this review really makes me crave Taco Bell.

4/18/12 (4 stars)

I was very curious about the Dorito Loco taco supreme ($1.79). I ordered that and a soft taco chicken fresco ($1.79) and two regular crunchy tacos ($1.09).  Okay so the Dorito Loco is nothing to write home about. What TB needs is a spicy taco. A shell with flavor. They tried the volcano shell for a bit. No bueno. Always had a stale taste. Maybe make the inside of the taco spicy?? And have a spicy, very-spicy, and we-warned-you trio of hotness.

I love getting my tacos fresco sometimes, which is just what they call their healthier option. I think a little less meat, no cheese, and tomato.  I wish all their tacos came with tomatoes but only if you order supreme, and then they  have sour cream too.  I always forget to ask for extra lettuce.

The regular beef tacos are an okay deal for a fast taco for a dollar. I like them with light meat and extra lettuce and cheese. Obviously, that's prob not for everyone. But they really do put a lot of meat in. Now if only they would make a veggie option!!  Extra spicy, of course!

Service here is generally fast and the employees are really nice. I normally go inside but hit an empty drive-thru and full parking lot at lunch today. Lucky me ~ 5 min and $6.24 later... I was back at work in no time!!

text:
Wonderful Neapolitan pizza! They also have a selection of sandwiches, appetizers, and entrees. Prices are reasonable. Parking is free on the street or in the free parking garage directly behind the restaurant.

If you have never had neapolitan pizza you must try it! The crust is thin and it’s baked at a higher temperature. Unlike other thin crust pizzas it’s intended to have a softer crust.

To other reviewers: I understand if you don’t like the toppings on the pizza, but you can’t criticize the style of pizza. It’s intended to be thin with a softer crust. Some black on the edges is normal due to high heat. To be called neapolitan pizza it has to be baked at 900F for 1-2 minutes. Most traditional neapolitan pizza’s have simple toppings (Margarita) as the intent is to taste the crust and toppings as equal.

I would agree service is not good. The service needs to be honed to the level of the amazing food. I’ll be back!

We took our teenager here for his graduation celebration and we had a wonderful time!

Perla was our server and she asked us if this was our first time. We told her once before but today we came to celebrate a special occasion. Then she asked us our sons name since he was in the restroom. We didn't think anything of it and we just continued to look at the menu.

We ordered the grilled salmon with white wine butter sauce and spinach,  linguine & clams in white garlic herb sauce and the veal parmesan with spaghetti.

The table service was pretty quick, we were served warm bread and our drinks immediately after  ordering and received the rest of our food maybe 15- 20 mins afterwards.

Everyone enjoyed their meals, everything was delicious.  The salmon was moist, the pasta had lots of clams and the veal parmesan was nicely breaded, covered with the perfect amount of marinara and lots of mozzarella!

After we finished our meal, Perla walked over and presented to our son, Vera's lemon cookies! We thought that was really sweet and thoughtful of her!  Thank you Perla for a wonderful dining experience!

We'll definitely be returning and hopefully we'll have Perla again!

The side of noodles tasted like something we make at home. No where near enough seasoning. However, the sauce was really good.

The restaurant is located just off the tourist area on the end of a quiet street without street lights. When you enter you are greeted by a wall with employees running past you. I assumed I was to wait, but without being acknowledged nor having a host stand to walk up to, it was hard to know what to do. The restaurant was only half full, yet Yelp showed only minimal restaurant times (it never did fill up during my visit).

Service was good and attentive.

The food was just ok at best. The free carrot amuse bouche was good. The bread and butter were good, but some flake salt on the butter would have been appropriate. My pate appetizer took a long time to come out. The pate itself was bland and the portion was about half what I’m use to in San Francisco. The mustard was standard brown hotdog mustard.

My osso bucco was tender, but again lacked flavor. It came with 4 individual sugar snap peas. Both presentation and amount of vegetables could have been increased.

I won’t be back and I look forward to finding better French food in Monterey/Carmel.

text: First of all our server made a snide comment to a question my friend posed to him...in most restaurants fajitas are served with the steak chicken and vegetables separately on the plate wth guacamole in the middle and the tortillas on the side...so you can fill your tortillas with any combination you want..at this place it all mixed together. The meat and veggies are all cooked together. So when my friend realized this she asked him about it his response was.."well, i dont know what resataurants you go to but thats the way its served everywhere" as if she was some idiot. She's latino born and raised. There was just no need for a service provider to answer a question that way. It was insulting to all of us at the table. Then..on top of that..he got the orders wrong. One friend orders steak tacos and it came out with pork..which she never ordered. And the fajitas came out there was barely any steak in them at all. All of us looked thru their plates and we were hard pressed to find any steak at all. I couldnt believe you would order steak fajitas such a well known dish notorious for having plenty of meat in it and find so little steak in this dish...especially a place that has a good reputation. I wanted to send all of it back and make a complaint to the manager but my friends told me not to. So i let it go. To top it all off..the place was not to crowded considering its a monday night...and he was very slow in coming to our table and taking our order and following up. We asked for straws to drink our water and he never brought them..i had to go to the bar myself to get them. The rest of the staff however was very attentive to us...the follow up guys...not our main waiter took care of us far better then our waiter did..who mostly ignored us. They made sure we had extra chips and picante sauce...filled our water and brought me another diet coke when he saw my empty glass. I wish the tip would all go to them..because our waiter didnt deserve any tip. All in all it was a poor experience. I wont be recommending this place to anyone.

text: You definitly feel transported back to old Hollywood when eating here.  The interior is very classy and all the serviers/ bartenders are dressed in proper old school server uniforms. The food is definitely on the pricey side but not ridiculous.  Drinks are stiff.  I've almost always sat at the bar because there is normally been a wait whenever I've gone.  The bar allows you to order food as well as drinks.  The location is a pro and con as it's right off of Hollywood Blvd so traffic and parking in this area can be a little dicey.  They do have a parking lot in the back but  it's valet might cost you money.  I would have given Musso & Frank's five stars but unfortunately they service sometimes has just been bad.  There was one time I sat at the bar waiting over ten minutes before somebody acknowledged me, then it took another ten for them to take my order.  They even got the order wrong.  Eventually they fixed it but for such a renowned establishment, the service should definitely be better.

text:
This is the absolute best. I've been coming to this Pub for as long as I can remember, it is an evergreen, sunny days are even brighter with a stop here for a gorgeous bite and cooler days are definitely meant to be warmed up with hot tea and some deliciousness. Over the years I have tried pretty much everything on the menu, and I fondly oh so fondly remember the taste of bangers and mash with that English gravy and peas.. or the English bacon (it might look like ham but it's nothing like ham... )
Or those mini sausage rolls while having the most royal of the English afternoon teas ever...
Such memories!
Now that I've gone fully vegetarian though options are not less tasty on the contrary the Market scramble, wonderful fluffy scrambled eggs with fresh vegetables from the Santa Monica Farmers Market... Such a simple delicate pleasure.. and those breakfast potatoes on the side.. Ye old Kings Head Rule. Dilly Dilly! 😀🇬🇧♥️❤️❣️
And the vegetarian full English breakfast is as tasty as the 'original' one, it's just healthier with two soy patties as substitute of the bangers and bacon..

Definitely my comfort place, my go-to-pub no matter the season nor the time of the day..
🇬🇧❣️♥️♥️❤️❤️😍Staff is incredible and it feels like home. Pure Bliss.

text:
3/14/15

We celebrated my brother-in-law (Jon's) birthday at La Bricola - it was a Sunday night and we had a party of 9.  I sat with my parents and husband at one end of the table, and Jon had friends and family around him at the other end. Less than a week had gone by since an accident had claimed the life of his wife, my sister, so the mood was quiet and tearful, instead of the happy and fun birthday dinner she had planned for him just days before.

A few appetizers were ordered but I only remember eating lots of crispy, fried calamari. A plate of it landed in front of me and I enjoyed tons of lightly breaded, flavorful, crunchy pieces. I also went a little crazy with the bread and olive oil on the table. Pretty sure I ate more than my fair share of all the community dishes.

For dinner my husband had lamb, served in a plateful of gravy - he ate every bite and said it was delicious.  I had a seafood pasta with squid ink, which dyed the noodles black. Seemed to appropriately fit my mood - and also looked pretty cool. It was delicious too. Lots of seafood and a great sauce. I hardly remember eating, or what anyone talked about, but I also cleaned my plate.

Service was great - friendly without being more enthusiastic than we could handle. I think a dessert with a candle showed up at the end of the meal. Thank goodness the staff didn't include a song with the dessert. Everything was really enjoyable (as much as it could be) and I'd definitely return!

Tong Fong Low is a very popular restaurant in Oroville. It is the family tradition with locals and has been in business over 50 years. I like their egg rolls but would like them even more if they were chicken instead of pork. I do not like their sweet and sour sauce. It tastes like they put a lot of vanilla in it. Not very appetizing. The fried foods were very greasy this time. The walnut shrimp was very good! Fried rice was good.
The Egg Foo Yung was rather dry, shaped like a scoop of ice cream, and had hardly any gravy.
It would be nice if it were served in patties instead of tightly packed scoop shapes. The chow mein was okay this time, but quite greasy and hardly any vegetables, with a few very small pieces of bright red colored meat, pork?
But they were doing a very large amount of business when we got there to pick up our food.
So our food was hot and freshly made.

text:
Good food, decent service, and highly updated from the Applebee's I remember as a kid. This would be a great place to go with friends to watch the fights or a game. Their big screens everywhere inside are on point. Everything is super clean and fresh. I'll definitely be coming back as a regular.

I'd say with a little more training for their staff, this place will be a solid 5 stars. Our order had the wrong soup put in entirely. The waiter recommended one type, but we ordered a different one which was what my mom was craving when she chose that she wanted us to go to Applebee's specifically, and that's the only item she ordered. They brought out the one that was recommended making her feel like she wasn't listened to fully. My poor mom was so hungry, but we were patient. Life's too short to get mad and the waiter genuinely didn't mean to mix it up.

It was said the soup would be comped when they brought out the right one since they got it wrong and they took a long time to finally bring out the right one, but it was still on the bill and we paid for it anyways. That isn't an issue, but simply don't say you'll take it off the bill if you don't after the order was already wrong, you know? By that point we just said forget it and decided not to mention it. We had been there a long time and we were ready to go home.

Really nice waiter though and I'd he happy to be served by him again, hence my suggesting upping the training and maybe streamlining the operational processes a bit. I think the waiters were overwhelmed and distracted due to that. It wasn't only one waiter. I noticed a bit of the flurry all over, and it wasn't that busy to be honest. I think with time and training it'll get sorted out.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
I have been wanting to check out Moresi's after I first found them on yelp while looking for a treat for my boyfriend's birthday, way back in June. I wish I had come in sooner, but this past weekend was our first visit. First of many to come! INCREDIBLE!

Service was soooo awesome. All the staff are great, but Mel was our waitress and she went out of her way to give us a terrific experience! Very friendly, great suggestions, and she was really wonderful about checking in on us at the perfect times. Our waters were kept full, which is a true feat when you have a small water glass in front of me. Even as I finished off a couple Bloody Mary's, I kept drinking my water and they never let me see an empty cup. Then we saw Ed Moresi, who my boyfriend recognized from Ed's Mudville Grille!!!  We had no idea the two restaurants were related. He took time to come over and chat with us too. And we made friends with the table next to us as we dined outside. The ENTIRE experience was EXACTLY what you want on a Sunday afternoon.

On to the good stuff... the food!! We knew before arriving we weren't doing entrees - I had my heart set on French Onion soup, and Creme Brulee dessert, so with a few drinks and appetizers there wouldn't be much room left! We'll come back another time for just entrees. We started with calamari (loved it - especially the fried jalapenos and green beans they mix in!) and seared ahi (very good too!) Then our soups arrived which I enjoyed very much too (sadly, I left my leftover soup on the table). We each made it about halfway through the soup - starting to get pretty full and still wanting dessert. The fantastic Creme Brulee was served perfectly chilled (like it should be!) I was so full but I made it to the very last bite. Probably should have split one because they're a fairly big portion size!

Given my love of a great Bloody Mary, I'll end in saying:

DO NOT LEAVE UNLESS YOU ORDER A BLOODY MARY.

Perfect amount of spice, great flavor, specially made smoked jalapeno bacon, which was nice and crisp - holy cow. What a fabulous place to enjoy a nice meal. I wish they served breakfast too!!

text: I can remember going to El Charros as a kid some 30+ years ago, honestly couldn't imagine Montrose without it. Definitely one of the easiest if not the easiest restaurants to find in the Montrose area, its located on the corner of Verdugo Blvd and Honolulu. There's normally plenty of parking in the lot directly next to it, the lot can be accessed from Verdugo. The restaurant itself is clean and comfortable, the staff is friendly and service is normally great. The food is consistently good, the menu consists of straight forward Mexican dishes with no surprises. El Charros is a great place to eat with the family or friends and can accommodate groups of all sizes. There's also a full bar that serves excellent margaritas. Like any restaurant business picks up around dinnertime, especially on the weekends, early arrival or reservations will help assure quick seating.

name: Jonathan Adler
text:
Caffe Roma is right in the middle of the famous Canon St. In Beverly Hills.  Friday night is very lively with an eclectic crowd of regulars, celebs and tourists.  They have a full bar and DJ, as well as large dining areas in and outside in the enclosed outdoor courtyard. I arrived there early but enjoyed the atmosphere and music so much I chilled out for an extra few hours.

My main server and head waiter Jesse Sanchez(told me he's been there since they opened 38 years ago)provided outstanding, personable and flawless service.  He was assisted by Adam who was also excellent.

I hadn't eaten all day so I ate alot starting with the Gamberi Salad(huge succulent shrimp) in fresh and healthy spinach leaves and topped with very large, creamy avocado slices.

The Summerland, Santa Barbara white wine suggested by Jesse was perfect with my linguini entree which was also a winner.

The dessert of peach and lemon sorbetto was also one of the best desserts I've had in awhile.

I am a coffee fiend and my espressos and cappuccinos were as good as, if not better than most top coffee bistros.

I had the pleasure of meeting the Manager, Davide Giliberti(real Italian)who was running the place very smoothly considering the large crowd in the demanding BH market.

The Staff is all well dressed​(shout out to Mr. Giliberti) and my courtyard table amply heated by a nice electric flame.

Overall, I am really impressed with Caffe Roma and this is now my go to restaurant in Beverly Hills for the best Italian cuisine in a stylish, classy and entertaining atmosphere.

Bonus: The fine art portrait photography of celebrities is some of the best I've seen anywhere.

Well done Caffe Roma.

Beyond the absolutely incredible atmosphere, the food stands out from the crowd as something unique and highly delicious. I haven't been to a place that has wowed me and or given me a reason to come back through a unique meal in quite some time. The bar specifically is so cool! It is CAMBRIA with a backlit veining. Tempura avocado: perfectly breaded and deep fried. The house pickled onions add some spice and unique flavor. Must order for sure.

Calamari Taco: this was my favorite thing this visit. Perfectly cooked and seasoned calamari on a delicious tortilla. Do not underestimate this taco, this is an absolute MUST TRY!!
Carnitas tacos: as you would expect, a delicious carnitas taco. The carnitas is cooked perfectly and has delicious flavor. You do not need any salsas with these tacos, indulge as is and enjoy.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
5/17/18

Treated my parents to Brazilian Steakhouse for dad’s birthday last month. We had previously been to the one in Oakland, and very much enjoyed it, but wanted to try something new, and the one in Concord doesn’t open for a few more weeks still. So I made a reservation in Point Richmond at Pikanhas for the four of us.

We did the full buffet and Rodizio combination which is about $40 per person. We started at the salad bar and enjoyed hot peppers, microgreens, delicious meat balls in a wonderful red sauce, and chicken salad, house rice, and more.

Since it was $3.50 for a can of soda (no refills) my boyfriend and I both ordered iced tea instead ($3). However, after several minutes with empty glasses, we asked for a refill from a staff person walking by, but the woman said she didn't speak English. We pointed at the table's empty water and iced tea glasses crossed our fingers. When that didn't work we flagged down a different employee and he brought one iced tea refill. We felt like the restaurant was just a little overwhelmed by hosting two very large dinner parties at tables in the front room and in the back where we were.

Chicken hearts were my favorite, with one of the sausages being a close second. The meats we tried were outstanding but we probably were only offered half of the number they boast about serving. I mentioned that we were celebrating a birthday when I made the reservation, but they didn't acknowledge this at all (which was fine - definitely don't need any free dessert after a big meat buffet - but a simple "happy birthday" comment would have been nice). I'd probably give this place another try, but not before I check out the new Brazilian Steakhouse closer to home when it opens next month.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
6/12/13 - Tres Stand at AT&T Park

NOT AS GOOD AS THE GARLIC FRIES

We waited in the long, slow line, watching the game on screens instead of live as we inched forward. Honestly, it was nice to watch the food being prepared, but it was also a little difficult to conceive how a couple workers moved at super snail speed. But husband wanted a bacon wrapped hot dog and I wanted the hot peppers he was going to discard from it.

I'm glad I bought garlic fries next door when we left Tres. The hot dog wasn't all that big, the bacon was fatty - the uncooked kind of fat that you pull off - I need it crispied up. There were a few chps but I'd already eaten nachos somewhere else.

Noteworthy: they sold bowls of food in reuseable plastic containers with tight-seal lids that are microwave safe. Great idea for ballpark guests who want to eat at every food place they see and might not finish everything on their plates! And slightly more environmentally conscious than other park vendors. Nice move, Tres!

text:
Speaking as an El Compadre Virgin:
I just pulled off the highway for a quick stop at the gas station across the street.
I noticed this place and thought I'd try it out. Not knowing what to expect, at first glance at the menu, I thought it seemed a bit expensive, so I only ordered a Beef Taco  and Beef Burrito. That came out to just over $11. I was expecting something just above maybe Taco Bell or Del Taco. Boy, was I wrong!
The first clue was when he handed me the bag out of the Drive-Thru window. It was so heavy that I almost dropped it. But I only ordered a Burrito and a Taco, right? So I pulled into the parking lot to see what I really had.
The second clue was the heavenly aroma that immediately overwhelmed the car. Then I opened the bag...Both items were Huge! And they were stuffed to the brim with the juiciest, most flavorful, shredded beef and all the extras. I was very, very (uh, did I say very) very surprised. It was soooooo good that I finished it all, right there in the parking lot.
That's when I realized that it wasn't expensive at all. I got exactly, if not more than what I paid for! And had I ordered more (as I initially intended before checking the menu), I don't think I would have been able to finish it. Those two items were enough.
And spoiler alert: If you're dressed nicely, you're gonna need to change your shirt after you're done.
So if you're like me and just passing through town and decide to give El Compadre a try...I can confidently say, you will be so happy that you did!

After my sister-in-law had her baby several months back, we all came here for dinner (well, not sis and baby), but the rest of the family who'd spent so many hours at the hospital. We revisited for dinner this week to celebrate a birthday!

What a treat! On both visits we've ordered the pate plate.  With this, a homemade pate, homemade salame, and peppercini order came out with a slice of each item for each person at the table. It was very good. The bread that accompanies it is toasted but still soft and fresh. Two types of bread are in the basket with several pieces of each. The garlicky bread is more thinly sliced and is very tasty, but the plain French bread is good too.

For an additional price, your meal can be served with soup, salad, and dessert. We've done this both times I've dined here and so glad we did. I've liked the soup (I've tried both watercress  and potato leak) and the house salad was nicely dressed with blue cheese crumbles on the side. They really make the salad. Tiny little pieces of cheese! On EVERY bites if Casey P. is the one putting it on your plate :)

I've had rack of lamb as an entree and it was phenomenal. Also very good is the scampi with prawns. Most noteworthy (which 3 at this table ordered this week) was the filet mignon. Lucky for me, husband was one of the three. He'd eaten too much bread and was getting full around the time of its arrival. Not a problem! I'll help you with a few bites. It was huge. And so tender and juicy. Wrapped in bacon and cooked perfectly rare. A little more seared on the top than he expected but a nice bernaise sauce on the side covered this taste.

French fries had been substituted on his plate for the potatoes and they were excellent. Small, thin and crispy!

We all received dessert. Several flavors of ice cream (spumoni, mango, chocolate, or vanilla) or rice pudding. I went with the pudding and it was really good until about halfway through when it became too sweet for me. Golden raisins floated in it which I usually don't eat but I enjoy them in the rice pudding. I didn't have a chance to try husband's chocolate ice cream but he said it was delicious.

I brought my own take-home container and filled it with his leftover veggies, a few fries, some steak, and two of my scampi prawns. It was nice to take something home with us!

Service was the right speed. We didn't feel rushed but there also were long period between dishes. Just enough time to be hungry enough again for the next course. We had to ask for drink refills a few times, but the restaurant was pretty busy and the glasses are actually pretty tiny.

We've sat inside both visits but the outdoor area is beautiful. There's also a bar (not sure if they serve food but they did have the Giant's game on). And employees are nice enough to give you score updates at your table, if you ask.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
2/21/15

Every year for the lunar new year's eve we meet with my parents, sister's family, and a ton of friends at Chinatown SF to celebrate and light off firecrackers. This year we had plans to do the same thing, but found ourselves in the hospital instead. Our family lost a very special person on the morning of the Lunar New Year and we were all exhausted from days of sadness - nobody had eaten a thing.

After hours of planning at a Oakmont Memorial Park, 9 of us met at Uncle Yu's around dinner time, and found a full house! We asked for a tale for 9, and they asked if we had a reservation. Ohhhh yeah, the New Year! We luckily were sat at the only open table within minutes and began hungrily staring at their menu.

Before long, chow mein, chow fun, steamed rice, honey walnut prawns, Mongolian chicken, peking chicken, garlic prawns, orange chicken and a couple other dishes... found their way to our table. We finished almost every plate - all sharing and taking turns eating through our tears.

The food was outstanding. Service was great too - especially for how full they were that night. I wish we'd gathered there to celebrate the New Year, but regardless, it was a great meal.

text:
4/26/16

I've enjoyed food from the lunch truck before, but today was my first experience dining inside the restaurant. I was lunching alone so I sat at the bar. I was immediately greeted and given a clean menu and a choice of mild or hot salsa to go with my chips. Hot, please!

The chips and my water came at the same time, and I ordered a crunchy shrimp taco, a soft taco with grilled fish, and a side salad. The salad was delicious. A little Italian dressing drizzled over lettuce, garbanzo beans, and a beet and more. Chips were light and crispy and the hot salsa was spicy and delicious. And the best part, my two tacos were outstanding. The grilled fish was seasoned very well (the soft corn tortilla fell apart but was also fresh and tasty). The shrimp taco had a crispy shell that also broke into pieces, but the yummy shrimp were cooked perfectly and had lots of lettuce and cheese on top. I was also offered more spicy salsa without asking - it was so good!

Service was great and my tacos were delicious (and lunch only totaled about $10). Definitely will be back!

text:
Our office is fortunate enough to have bosses that celebrate the birthdays of our team with monthly lunches. It's so terrific when I plan/organize these staff lunches and everything just flows smoothly with no hiccups! Today was one of those days. A 21-order pick-up from The Mediterranean! Thanks to the hard-working operation of their employees, all 21 combo and wrap meals were perfect! Everything was correct and everyone enjoyed the delicious food.

Today, I ordered the combo meal with falafel (instead of an animal protein), and bakdonsieh and foul medammas as my sides. Delicious! I heard from our lamb eaters the meat was slightly spicy (for their extremely delicate palates), and everyone who ordered chicken seemed happy. We finished lunch with their perfectly made baklava (it's not too sweet!)

It's really hard to pull off that many lunches without forgetting one, maybe mixing up the sides, leaving something out, etc. It literally happens to us all the time, which is a real bummer because by the time we realize it, there's not much we can do about it. So today's 100% perfect lunch by Sam and the others at LaMed was the best scenario possible, and almost nobody in our office had eaten there before, so now everyone has a new place they know and enjoy!
