text:
On my 3rd visit yesterday, I had the mixed plate with chicken and lamb kabobs including side Greek salad with feta cheese & Kalamata olives. The chicken was the best quality I've had all year, succulent, juicy with great seasonings.

There is alot of food for under $15 and it filled me up for the whole day.

Service as usual was perfect.

This is my favorite Greek restaurant in San Diego and they also do delivery and beer.

2nd visit I had the mixed plate with lamb, beef kabobs(onions, peppers), gyro and side salad.

It was even more delicious than the first time. Everything was cooked perfectly, juicy and tasty. The salad had alot of my favorite Kalamata olives and feta cheese.

Service was very fast and everything hot and fresh from the grill.

The staff is extremely gracious and courteous like the 1st time.

This is still my favorite Greek restaurant in San Diego.

They draw a large lunch crowd but stay open for dinner and deliver to around 9pm

Highly recommended immediately next door to the Starbucks.

right on the end of the Liberty Station complex off Lanning next to Starbucks. There is ample parking in the Station lot. It is across the street as well from the Point Loma Naval Base Annex.

I had the Owner recommended Greek Combo(lamb/beef gyro mea and chicken) which was amazing...one of the best Greek meals I've had in years. The white meat chicken was succulent, juicy and in a generous portion with the gyro lamb meat and tzaziki sauce.

For $15 it is alot of food with a very nice greek side salad.

Service is excellent and fast-it was ready in under 15 minutes(I see why they get so much business from the military base)alot of great quality food at a very reasonable price.

Harbor is now my favorite Greek restaurant at reasonable prices in Point Loma.

text:
Hey all, I am an avid fan of Castenedas and will absolutely recommend you eat at this franchise. They simply have the best chips you'll ever have, that could be a challenge, drop me a comment.
NOW FOR THIS LOCATION, WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW: I have ordered the "Chips with cheese & guacamole" 4 times from this location, and many times from 3 other locations, Palm Springs, cathedral City and Palm Desert off of Varner and Washington. PAY ATTENTION here truly as what this location is doing is highly shady and unlawful... when you order this menu item from any other castenedas, you get exactly what you expect, chips, covered in guacamole, and topped with shredded cheese. It's delicious. When you order this from this location you will be charged an extra dollar. They wont tell you about it, you simply have to catch it. They will then argue with you (yes argue, as much as you'll let them anyway which isnt much since I'm not a fan of arguing with establishment employees) about how their boss says its one or the other. Not both. Even after clearly pointing out that the menu says "chips with cheese AND guacamole" they will stick to their guns. (I have since told them twice that they need to change their menu if this is the case) My visit yesterday ended up in chips and only guacamole... If I wanted cheese, I would have to pay the 99cents. The most disgusting part is that this is the 3rd time they have tried to HIDE the dollar. I actually doubt most people even realize they are being charged extra fees than what they expect. Who knows what all menu items this is happening on that you aren't aware of. Hopefully enough people will pay attention and continue to bring this up and this place can be held accountable for their actions. I encourage you to go order this item and see what happens and of course hold them accountable and also see what happens. My hope is that they will either give in and change their menu or simply comply with all of the other franchises that dont practice this unlawful act. Thank you for your time and feel free to comment and or ask questions.

We came to Phone Mai because it was close to Seafood Market and they serve Filipino and Vietnamese food. However, the Filipino dishes are mostly breakfast and a few entree's that I noticed.

The restaurant was busy and cramped,  the wait for our table was just a few minutes. While waiting @ the entrance, they have about 20 pictures of characters who "dined & dashed" - customers who left without paying... that's unfortunate not just for the owners but for this neighborhood.

I ordered the vermicelli bowl with grilled onion beef with grilled shrimp. First thing I noticed when I received my order, my bowl was missing the shrimp and the noodles were cold.

I'm used to having the noodles warm or room temp. Also, the onion beef was over cooked, it was tough. Instead of asking about my shrimp, I just made sure that we were not charged.

Also, we ordered the rice plates with grilled chicken and grilled beef with shrimp.  My family said it was "okay,  we had better"

The service was quick and the staff was friendly but we had better food @ other Vietnamese restaurants like Vung Tau, Thein Long or Sonny's Cafe to name a few. I don't think, we'll be returning.

name: Alan Harnett
text:
It’s been a couple years since I’ve been to Flore. I appreciate the new owners trying to revive a tired, old horse. Sadly it’s just not good.

During my Saturday night visit, the restaurant was dead. I think there were 6 people total during my visit. And half of them were friends with the bartender. Service was good at the start then quickly fizzled away. Over hearing the conversation, it sounded like the servers personal life was more important then her job. I received my appetizer after my entree. She never came back to refill my water or check in on how my food tasted. Bartender was very nice and attentive. I think he should work alone next time.

Food was mediocre. It has so much potential but fell flat. The blue cheese fries appetizer was an interesting concept. It could have been amazing, but the fries tasted like they had been reheated.

The chicken sandwich I had came with a mound of hot fries (thank you). But the sandwich was meh. A dry crusty roll, with a thin slice of lettuce, tomatoes, and over cooked chicken.

Here is some advice: Of your looking for a decent sandwich or burger try Super Duper, HiTops, or Hamburger Marys. If you want a lively atmosphere on a Saturday night try Hamburger Marys or Harvey’s.

The thin thread still hanging on for Flore is the patio breakfast. Now only if they could bring the atmosphere back that Cafe Flore was known for. Drink specials, live music, good food, and good service are a start.

I work here. I only have some advice to offer for customers to make their dinning experience even better.
-call ahead or use our app if you can (it lessens the amount of time you'll be waiting)
-if you order and are told less than 18-20 minutes, please understand that it takes us at least 18 minutes to cook your food. It's chicken, not burger patties and need to be cooked all the way through.
-we do get busy. If you know the time of day/night you're ordering your food, that might impact the amount of time you will be spending with us. Lunch and dinner times are usually the busiest.
-we actually pride ourselves on customer service; however, if you wait or your food is wrong, yelling and throwing a fit doesn't help us, or yourself. We are more than willing to accommodate your needs. Please just communicate with us.
-we have one of the largest stores in our chain. It gets busy, loud,  and tables get left with food on them because we don't have trash cans for the customers to use. It's PART OF OUR CUSTOMER SERVICE.

I would have never thought I'd fall in love with Burmese food. Burma burma is one of the best restaurants I have been to and two main reasons are great food and great service.

Upon entering we were greeted with a smile and our waitress was super friendly and nice. She even brought a nice scoop of ice cream on the house since it was birthday. And yes they did sing me the happy birthday song.

There are plenty of seats available and during busy house the wait time is usually less than 10 minutes. They have booths all around and chairs and tables in the middle.

Let's go over their food. They have all sorts of meat. Chicken, lamb, beef, calamari, shrimp, fish...you name it. I tried the black pepper chicken and lamb chilli and gotta say the lamb was so good that I took 2 to go for my dinner and next day's lunch.

Prices are fair for the quality of food and service you receive. All in all I highly recommend burma burma in Dublin.

Hollywood Pies is a cool looking Pizza restaurant with nice indoor and outdoor seating.

They specialize in Chicago deep dish pizza.  My pizza, the Angeleno,  was very large with loads of very tangy and very delicious pizza sauce.  It includes artichokes, red peppers and I added sausages.

The combination of flavors worked great.  There was also so much pizza I had enough for a 2nd days meal.

Their location is excellent on Pico just east of La Cienega.  They also do alot of takeout and delivery.

Overall, Hollywood Pies is my top choice for deep dish pizza in LA.

name: Joseph Valdez
text: There are a lot of worthy pizza places in reasonable driving distance from spring valley. Nara's, Fillipi's, Fernando's, and probably a few more that I haven't tried, but Gaetano's has been around for decades, and their pizza has never failed to satisfy whenever I've gone. Their customer service is also awesome, and dining in is always a cozy experience. Certain pizza joints may load a ton of toppings and cheese, or specialize their pizza to make it unique from the competition. Gaetano's is just an all around good pizza, and doesn't go heavy on any particular quality to distinguish themselves from someplace like Fillipis who loads toppings on their pizza. It's a solid pick for any pizza lover, and you'll be sure to have a favorite specialty or custom pizza to come back for.

My wife had the Waimea Omelet sauteed mushrooms, bell peppers, onions, spinach & cheese with potatoes. She lived there for awhile and said it was awesome especially the potatoes. I know we'll be going back. It was packed due to the day I'm sure. There are not a lot of big tables. I'd call ahead for 5+.

This was our first time of course. The best way there is from the Santo Road exit on SR52. It's at the back of the complex towards the south end so take the south entrance at the 2nd signal. It's between "The Market" and Coldwell Bankers before you get to the Valero upfront.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
6/25/18

This family-style serving restaurant on the Coast is a MUST! If youre driving through and youre hungry (like, really hungry!) come here for your meal. I know they serve lunch and dinner (not sure about breakfast). It's an old logging mill and they have a museum with tons of historic stuff inside (the place is huge!)

My boyfriend used to work at a lumberyard so he enjoyed walking around and talking to the kids and me about some of the tools, and checking out old boots and the like.

But the FOOD!!! And service... that's what youre going to go for! Our meal started with a bowl of delicious soup (and an offer of a refill when we finished it), a loaf of fresh baked bread, salads, side dishes (veggies, beans) and incredible chicken parmesan. We were there for lunch. Ham came with that meal had we stayed for dinner, for only a couple dollars more. Really, really good deal for the amount and quality of food you get.

text: If you find yourself in Old Town Temecula, you owe it to yourself to stop by Mad Madeline's Grill. This Family Friendly, neighborhood spot offers an eclectic menu of Award Winning Burgers (that are hand patted and charbroiled, not fried) and in some cases require a knife and fork to start in, before you can actually pick it up with your hands. Along with other savory sandwiches, large salads and sides, like beer battered onion rings, french fries and sweet potato fries. An especially nice touch is that the buns are branded with the restaurant's logo. The presentation is definitely Instagram worthy. They offer covered patio dining, complete with misters to ease the heat of Temecula's summer days. The management and staff provides exceptional service that will definitely keep you coming back. So treat yourself, your family and friends to Mad Madeline's Grill.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
5/28/13

I EAT HERE FOR MY HUSBAND

I don't know that I'd actually eat at Mary's all that often if it weren't for my husband. He loves paying for overpriced breadsticks with ranch. While I enjoy these, I don't think they're a very good value. I'll admit, the breadsticks are very good. I usually add a little dill and garlic to the ranch. But its $4.55 for one order and he normally eats almost two orders.

We usually get this food to go when eating at the Mary's in Walnut Creek. It's been a long time since I sat down inside one. He told me they have free breadsticks for the taking when you dine in, but you get no dipping sauce (ranch, butter, etc.) What?! And he pays for something he could get for free? I just don't understand... I guess fresh is best.

Our server Shelby was really great. She was friendly and fast and brought me lids for the butter I didn't finish without me having to ask. I had a small Mary's salad $5.65 with my Coors Light $3.85. The salad was very good and fresh and had lots of toppings, but it was really small. Guess it's better to have a small plate and finish it than eat 'till I'm stuffed.

Overall, this location seemed as clean and nice as the one we have at home. I was suprised there weren't more people in it, but perhaps there are others like me who just don't see much value here.

text:
Barrel is one of the coolest Pubs I've ever patronized. The establishment is upscale, clean with a nice sociable atmosphere without being too loud and rowdy.

Service by Host Grant was outstanding(friendly, professional and very knowledgeable). I took him up on his recommends based on my preferences and had D'La Costa Sangria(Napa Valley), Judgement Day(from Lost Abbey, San Marcos) and Classic Nod(Belgian style) from a Carlsbad brewery.

I really enjoyed all 3 selections-definitely some of the best beer and wine I've had ever.

There is great seating along the street counter or inside at tables; it is roomy so excellent for groups.

The beer selection is fantastic.

A must visit in North County for beer lovers.

text: This place ROCKS.  Went to the restaurant Saturday and went early in the evening.  We were greeted with a warm hello, and seated at a nice booth.  We chose the all you can eat for 2 hours menu choice.  We also order a house favorite Soju.  Try the green apple, the best.  Being our first time, we asked a thousand questions of our waiter Andy.  He brought us a variety of dishes, as much as we could possible eat.  I would name the items but you just have to try them for yourself.  Every waiter made an effort to ask us if we needed anything, it was a group effort as we were treated to a awesome dinner.  The dinner was very reasonable at just $27.99 for each of us and the Soju was $9.99 for a bottle.  You cook your own food right at your table, so the traditional waiting for your food to come is gone.  You cook it and enjoy it hot.  Be sure to ask the waiter to change the grill when it starts to get dirty with burnt food.  They happily bring a new clean one.  The place fills up fast on weekends, so be early for the best service and enjoy no waiting to be seated.  I just loved the place and you can be sure I will be going back and soon.  Bring your friends and enjoy a great meal and a fun experience.

name: Jonathan Adler
text:
Monzu is a new addition to the Italian restaurant scene in the Gaslamp and also just up the street from Petco stadium on 10th Ave(nearest cross st. Island).

The Owners are real southern Italians and I could tell alot of care and attention goes into the offerings.

On Owner suggestion, I had the Traditional Tagliatelle Bolognese. The pasta is 100% organic made by hand at the restaurant with famous Oakland based Giusto's flour. It was some of the best I ever had.

I would easily pay double the $13 Monzu charges at many other Italian restaurants. I feel this is fine dining Italian quality for pizza shop prices making this my #1 pick for Italian restaurant value in San Diego.

My Burrata Salad was phenomenal-the soft delectable cheese with fresh tomato tasted incredible.

The bonus was the direct from central Italy Montepulciano D'Abruzzo. The wine has a smooth, just slightly fruity taste that was marvelous.

Even the Italian coffee was better than most coffee shops in town.

Monzu impresses me as a great addition to the restaurant scene in downtown San Diego and my #1 pick so far for Italian restaurant value.

Salute Monzu.

I ordered one piece of baklava and I was able to pick out the piece I wanted from a mound of plastic boxes next to the cashier.

I kind of wished they had served the one I ate there on a small paper plate, or even a reusable glass plate/dish. name: Amy Palmer
text:
7/9/18

After a long weekend camping on the beach in perfect weather, having only BBQed steak and fresh oysters to eat, my boyfriend and I pulled into the Taco Bell parking lot with naked on our minds. Naked chicken, that is. Fredie had never tried their naked chicken tacos before, so we went wild and got the spicy fried chicken shell. A couple of those, a couple regular crunchy tacos, and two Tacos Supreme. We had worked up quite an appetite that afternoon on our kayaks, so it was time to get down on some TB dinner.

We had our dog in the car so we quickly ate inside. Service was fast and cashier Jack was friendly. Soda machine was out of order (no ice) but it sounded like this wasn’t a new problem for them. Restrooms were clean and so was the entire restaurant itself. We were back on the road and headed toward home in almost no time at all. Delicious fast food and great value. This location is A-OK if you happen to be driving through the area!

If youre in Monterey youre definitely going to stop at Fisherman's Wharf. It's a wonderful collection of restaurants offering hot clam chowder and cold, raw oysters. Lots of other amazing food, drinks, and shopping also dot the row of wharf destinations.

Abalonetti is one of the places we enjoy stopping for oysters. For a little under $10 you can get 1/2 dozen oysters and a non-alcoholic beverage, which is exactly what I ordered when I was last here in May 2014.  Flora was our server that day and we had great service, and a great, icy plate of sweet shellfish.

We've been here more than once. Abalonetti has been on the wharf for many years and we always enjoy our visits here.

name: Jack Flynn
text:
Great Simple Mexican Food

This is one of our "go to" places. We always know what to expect, the food is well prepared, tasty, hot, and authentic.

So, you like street tacos, well these are great street tacos.  So, you like breakfast burritos, then they have those too.  So, you like carnitas, well their plate is piled high and has crunchy fatty bits that melt in your mouth.

My wife and I keep trying other local Mexican places, but we always come back.  We compare everyone around to the Burrito Factory, we've found some aspects that we like more at other places, but no one has consistent menu satisfaction like this place.

Just figure, the Burrito Factory will become an easy stop to satiate that craving for a burrito, or tacos, or re-fried beans wrapped in a flour tortilla.

This place is just good.

text:
He was born in Madrid, Spain as the third oldest son of Prince Amadeo of Savoy, Duke of Aosta and his first wife Donna Maria Vittoria dal Pozzo della Cisterna. Prince Luigi Amedeo was a grandson of King Vittorio Emanuele II of Italy. He was born during his father's brief reign as King Amadeo of Spain. His siblings are Prince Emanuele Filiberto, Prince Vittorio Emanuele, and Prince Umberto. Shortly after his birth his father, who had reigned in Spain since 1870, abdicated and returned to Italy in 1873. Prince Luigi Amedeo was a member of the House of Savoy, well known in Europe since the 12th century. His uncle became King Umberto I of Italy in 1878, and his cousin became King Vittorio Emanuele III in 1900.
The title Duke of the Abruzzi (Italian: Duca degli Abruzzi) was created by King Umberto I in 1890 for Luigi Amedeo, who was a son of the abdicating King of Spain Amadeus and initially was given the title of Infante of Spain. His ducal title referred to the central Italian region of Abruzzo.
From 1893 to 1896, Luigi Amedeo traveled around the world, including Eritrea, then an Italian possession, and Vancouver. In September 1893, he traveled to Italian Somaliland to quell the unrest and stayed for a month to guard the port of Mogadishu, giving him his first contact with a land to which he would later devote the last years of his life and in which he would choose to die.[3]He had begun to train as a mountaineer in 1892 on Mont Blanc and Monte Rosa (Italian Alps): in 1897 he made the first ascent of Mount Saint Elias (Canada/U.S., 5,489 m). There the expedition searched for a mirage, known as the Silent City of Alaska, that natives and prospectors claimed to see over a glacier. C. W. Thornton, a member of the expedition, wrote: "It required no effort of the imagination to liken it to a city, but was so distinct that it required, instead, faith to believe that it was not in reality a city."[

name: Amy Palmer
text:
9/18/14

Awesome pizza at an amazing price! It took a long time after we sat down at the bar to get menus, have our orders taken, sip our drinks and finally bite into the delicious pizza, but the wait was worth it.

I had the "slice" which dwarfs the size of any "personal pizza" somewhere else.  I ordered it well-done with mushrooms and anchovies. Weird, I know.

My husband on my left sat at the bar staring at the soccer game on the small TV on their wall. (It was the final game of the World Cup.) The man on my right sat swearing softly under his breath, his bad words growing louder and louder as he very impatiently waited for his to-go order, asking the waitress to "check on it" more than once.

You can see the pizza machine moving the pizzas through in the back. Everyone in the place was hard at work and all of the tables were full. Aside from being a large slice, I liked the sauce a lot. Definitely more than I liked the crust, but if you like big, bubbly crust, it's your kind of place! Wasn't bad, just not my style.  Definitely a great value - would love to return to the adorable town of Niles and get another monster slice!

Knowing that we were about to walk into a movie theater, and knowing their usual policy on outside food and drinks, my husband and I decided to split a small, white chocolate mocha. The attendant working was very nice and polite and he even ID'ed me when I pulled out my Visa.

Yes, I used my Visa for a $3.55 purchase. And Yes! A small coffee was $3.55!!

He asked if we wanted whipped cream and we said, "of course!" :)  The drink was prepared quickly and there was no line ahead of us so we were in and out in just a couple of minutes.

I visited the women's restroom which was a bit untidy but overall clean with lots of paper on the floor. Hand driers are so much nicer than paper towels. Cleaner and environmentally more friendly. But oh well.

We snuck in the coffee and he hid it under his seat for most of the movie. By the time I remembered it, I had a cold sip and all the whipped cream was gone, but it was still good :)

text:
As I walked in, the temperature seemed around 65°at 8:00pm. The cashier was somewhat friendly and attentive.  It took about 10 minutes for the food to be ready.
Take it, at least 5 cars passed by in drive thru. I was the ONLY customer inside at the time. A few other customers came in the restaurant to order to go while I was eating,  2 of which complained about how cold it was.
As I sat there, somewhat enjoying my food, a second cashier clocked in to work. Within a few minutes he proceeded to use the restroom. Upon returning as cashier, he began a lengthy conversation with the girl cashier. My issue with that was the use of foul language in EVERY sentence.  "What the f",  "Who the f", "Shut the f up", etc., etc. A few minutes passed by and a guy walked in(apparently an employee who was off that day). The guy cashier stepped outside with his drive thru headset on and had another "break"(take it he arrived about 20 minutes prior). He was admiring the fellow employee's red Camaro.
Out of all this,  I can honestly say it seems as if these employees don't have a care in the world regarding customer service, nor any type of responsibility or respect towards their customers or job whatsoever.
But hey, I've only done every step of customer service in the restaurant industry for 20 years from cashier to franchisee, so who am I to judge.
Good luck with the business, whomever the owner is...but, I sure will not return as a customer.
Oh, btw...the BBQ Mix I ordered, the riblet part seemed to have been sitting there quite some time. It was dry, overcooked tasteless and a bit burned. Just saying.
I did inform the cashier of being unsatisfied with their service towards customers and the use of foul language being disrespectful towards me as I sat there trying to enjoy my food. She seemed to have understood...I hope so, for the good of the business.

In my opinion the prices are high for a pizza place and the atmosphere is bland. The salad bar is small and had no shredded cheese. text:
11/24/14
I visited Pho Saigon (now called Saigon Vietnamese Bistro) right when they opened, but haven't returned since then - only because I have a different Pho noodle place walking distance to my office, so I often visit there instead out of convenience.

I met a friend for lunch at Saigon on a Friday afternoon and struggled to find parking in their lot.  I circled a couple of times before finding a spot and was given a warm, friendly greeting by the host. Much friendlier than my usual place.

I ordered a large bowl of seafood soup ($8.75) - I initially said I wanted shrimp only, but then decided to not be difficult. I wish I had stuck with my custom order, since my large soup only ended up having three small shrimp in it. It was really good though. The fish cake was unlike the thin, floppy ones I'm used to - it was delicious! There was some squid also, but the majority of the seafood was limp, imitation crab pieces floating around, most of which I pulled out. My friend had chicken chow mein ($9.25) that also looked good. It was a lot of food and we both had a lot left-over. Good thing I brought two to-go containers along!

Service was great until the end. My one hour lunch was near over: I had 10 minutes left and still had to fight the downtown Walnut Creek traffic to get back to my office 3 miles away on time. Where was our check? Finally a girl (not our server) brought it to our table, I paid, and we left. I think I enjoyed the soup broth more here than at my usual spot, but the overall experience was a little bit less enjoyable. And only 3 shrimp in a large soup is a little sad. Even still, you can't beat a yummy lunch for two in downtown Walnut Creek for under $20! I'd return!

Note: the receipt still has their former name "Pho Saigon Noodle" - same owners perhaps?

5/8/13

WHERE'S MAH BACON?!

There might just be bacon-vodka at this place, but we don't know for sure. I probably would have given two-stars for our experience at the bar but the restaurant in the front may have great food and service and it's all one yelp page.

Myself and three others walked in through the restaurant and found ourselves at the bar in the back. Just what we were looking for! We sat for a few minutes and ended up just picking up the list of specials (there were 3 drinks on it) since we hadn't yet been even offered a menu. When we placed our order (Bloody Mary's all around) one of us was holding the Specials Menu. It featured a Bacon Bloody Mary and we all wanted one. Long story short, we ended up all getting regular Bloody Marys. To be fair, we had not asked for Bacon, but all of us thought it was pretty obvious, since we hadn't even seen that they had a baconless one (no drink menus before ordering) and we were holding the Specials list in hand.

It was halfway through the drink that we started talking about it. I remember saying I'd ask the bartender how strong the bacon flavor was....if he came back our way.  Service was slow and half-hearted. Our drinks were baconless. $7.25 for an average to small sized Bloody Mary. When we finally did ask about it and got the bad news, no attempt was made to make the situation better even though the bartender could tell we were all disappointed. Yes, it was partially our fault, but a miscommunication works two ways, and it wasn't our job to right the wrong. It was Lucca's.

I would say that in the bars I've previously worked at, most managers (and all owners) want the clients to leave happy. While you can't make everyone happy, it doesn't take much to make bar patrons happy. Had I been bartending, I would have offered a small taste (half shot) of the bacon vodka we all missed out on.  It wouldn't cost the place much and would have given us what we had ultimately hoped to try.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
6/1/2012

It's all about who you know, right? I have an awesome person in my life that has allowed my fiance and I to stay in his room here at Squaw Creek. He's a penthouse owner. Honestly the place is nicer than my own home. I'd probably never, ever have the opportunity to stay in a room like this if not for the generosity and kindness of this person. I'm so grateful to have stayed here more than once.

The staff is amazing. Very helpful and very friendly and many of them have very nice moustaches. :) The bartenders downstairs are nice. Drinks aren't unreasonably priced and they are tasty. I recommend the chocolate martini. There is also a brownie sundae at that bar that's very good. To avoid confusion, it's an actual brownie; not a drink.

In winter there are stations set up for S'mores at certain times. It was awesome - we happened to wander by one of these real fires on our way to the spa. It was surrounded by chairs with a table of marshmallows, full-sized Hershey's bars, roasting sticks, and of course, a bowl of Graham crackers. However, not long after sitting down, first S'more almost perfectly browned, a family with several children came over and the kids were (Surprise!!!) a nightmare. The parents didn't seem concerned by the mess their kids were making - it was gross. No manners.

Once we reached the spa we realized there are 3 spas all scattered closely around the pool.  Unfortunately, once again, parents with no manners were letting their kids go from spa to spa. Mind you, two of these are adults only. Why have an adults only spa? I'd answer this but I have a feeling there is a character limit for these reviews and I could go on and on. Either way, act like a parent and set a good example by following the rules. I think the resort could use a small gate around these two spas. Nothing inconvenient, no key, just something with a sign that maybe states more boldly "adults only".

Getting out of the spa was the hard part. Thankfully all rooms come equipped with big, fluffy robes to wrap in as you walk up the steps back to the rooms. That was nice. Even walking barefoot wasn't so bad with the plush warmth around our bodies.

Speaking of walking, the parking lot is a good walk from the hotel so make sure to get all your stuff in one trip if you're not a fan of walking. Honestly though, it surprises me how many times I heard people complain about this. Bringing it up in my review is not a complaint. Sure, it's inconvenient when if you want to just "run to the car real quick", but honestly, I am so thankful to have the ability to walk that I'd never complain about having to do it. Put on a faux fur lined hooded jacket, some mittens and some boots, and enjoy the breath-taking beauty that surrounds you at this resort.

The parents didn't seem concerned by the mess their kids were making - it was gross. No manners.

Once we reached the spa we realized there are 3 spas all scattered closely around the pool.  Unfortunately, once again, parents with no manners were letting their kids go from spa to spa. Mind you, two of these are adults only. Why have an adults only spa? I'd answer this but I have a feeling there is a character limit for these reviews and I could go on and on. Either way, act like a parent and set a good example by following the rules. I think the resort could use a small gate around these two spas. Nothing inconvenient, no key, just something with a sign that maybe states more boldly "adults only".

Getting out of the spa was the hard part. Thankfully all rooms come equipped with big, fluffy robes to wrap in as you walk up the steps back to the rooms. That was nice. Even walking barefoot wasn't so bad with the plush warmth around our bodies.

Speaking of walking, the parking lot is a good walk from the hotel so make sure to get all your stuff in one trip if you're not a fan of walking. Honestly though, it surprises me how many times I heard people complain about this. Bringing it up in my review is not a complaint. Sure, it's inconvenient when if you want to just "run to the car real quick", but honestly, I am so thankful to have the ability to walk that I'd never complain about having to do it. Put on a faux fur lined hooded jacket, some mittens and some boots, and enjoy the breath-taking beauty that surrounds you at this resort.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
3/16/15

My brother-in-law's cousin is visiting him from Hawaii, so my husband and I drove to Novato to meet her and take them to lunch. After an enthusiastic "yes" from me for Mexican food, Jon suggested La Hacienda. He and my sister used to come here and he said the food was very good.

The food IS very good. The service was really one-two star worthy; but the food makes up for it, and the fact it was a Sunday afternoon and we had nowhere else to be.

It took a couple tries to get drinks delivered to our table. A young man brought chips and salsa (pico de gallo and a hotter one) - I asked him if they had a secret hotter salsa in the back and he said yes, but then just brought another small bowl of the same hot salsa. No comprendo. But the hot salsa was tasty! Especially after our drinks arrived.

I ordered two veggie tacos - Jon's cousin ordered a veggie burrito (they have two types of these also). ONe of the veggie options is beans, lettuce, sour cream, and the other one has roasted vegetables (broccoli, cauliflower, carrots, etc.). I ordered one of each and enjoyed them both. Especially the broccoli one, since that's my favorite food! The veggie burrito comes with a sauce which the waitress said she'd put on the side for Sandy, but even after Sandy reminded her it wasn't brought until the meal was done.

My husband had two carne asada and one carnitas taco. He said carnitas was the best. He had to go inside at one point (we sat out front) to get his drink refilled. He also had to go in when it was time to pay to take the credit card up, since it was really hard to get service at our table. A giant wasp visited us more often than our server. My brother in law ordered a quesadilla that was bigger than his appetite - it looked pretty good!

I would definitely return, but not it I were local and needed a spot for a lunch break - service here definitely made this place a great spot for a weekend meal.

Oh La Bonitas what do I do without you... this is a must try place. Fresh fresh quality food here, prepared by a chef who truly cares. You can taste it. Fresh salsas are a welcomed treat while you wait for your food.
They have a cheese shell taco that YOU MUST TRY. Absolutely delicious
The double shell tacos are my next favorite. The asada is clean and tender, seasoned flavor. Very pure tasting, not too salty like others.
The burritos are delicious
Their beans are delicious, smooth, creamy, rich flavor
Their rice is delicious, cooked pretty much perfectly, I dont like saying perfect because well, we all no that doesn't exist, or does it? Very good flavor, great texture, not over cooked
Chips are prepared in house, not too oily not too salty, very good, A plus
Their flour tortillas are great, chewy, as they should be.
I've said enough, this place is a gem. You can easily pass it by if you're not aware. Just google, best mexican food Palm Springs and follow on IG @Bestfoodpalmsprings

name: Amy Palmer
text:
1/13/15

Veggie Grill opened in the best way I can think of - offering free food! When their man of marketing came into our firm last week with fliers for free lunch today I immediately calendared a date with my mom. We arrived downtown and found that the line was moving quickly with fresh, hot food walking by us to customer tables at a fast pace. The fast-casual environment is perfect for busy office workers who enjoy dining downtown and don't want to order "to-go".

You wouldn't know it's an all-vegan place by the menu - but it is. (I called, I asked - it is!) Don't let this scare you off, carnivies! I think there is something for everyone here as long as your enjoy tasty vegetables and proteins prepared in many different and exciting ways.

A female employee at today's soft opening kept the line moving by answering questions and making menu suggestions - she also explained we'd get an appetizer free with our complimentary entrees. My mom and I reached Amy at the register (it was easy to remember her name) :) and she was a sweet, friendly personality that seemed undaunted by the staggering number of people that were placing ordered. I ordered the Bombay bowl ($9.25) with blackened chickin and my mom had the crispy Santa Fe chickin sandwich ($10.25). We were given two drinks (tea or lemonade) and we picked the crispy Portobello ($6) as our appetizer. The $38 meal was generously comped.

The food was brought out to our table on the dog-friendly front porch. My steaming bowl of roasted veggies, sautéed kale and quinoa was topped with the juicy chickin strips. A slightly-spiced curry sauce lightly covered my bowl - I'll probably never even explore the menu after this. I think I found my favorite item; it was so good that I'll be happy never trying anything else! (Except off my friend's plates!) Mom's chickin sandwich was also good. Outrageous sweet potato fries (the best I've ever had) joined her giant sandwich. The star of our lunch was the crispy Portobello basket with red pepper sauce. Seriously - how did they do this? I can easily say with sincere honesty that this was the best fried dish I've ever eaten. It was a large portion and absolutely delicious.

Can't wait to return with my husband and with my friends (vegan and non-vegan alike)! Thanks for bringing a new restaurant to downtown Walnut Creek that's as delicious as it is kind.

name: Andrew LD
text:
El Cantaro offers good vegan fare but I wouldn't give it the universal praise that other reviews have posted.  The location is quite good with a few dedicated parking spots and good street parking.  Inside, the space is clean and well-kept, although there aren't enough tables to accommodate everyone during busy hours.  The employees are not rude contrary to other reviews, but the restaurant is understaffed, leaving them in a permanent scramble to take phone orders, manage the line of customers, give food to couriers, cook, prep, and clean.  This is what hurts the experience the most, and I really hope El Cantaro can have an extra employee on hand to smooth things out during busy periods.

As for the food, I also didn't find it as good as the glowing reviews would suggest.  When you one of their burritos or tacos, they indeed taste like Mexican food at first brush. If you're not nitpicky you can stop reading at this point and come by.  For the choosier, there are a few flaws in their recipes.  The meat substitutes aren't very flavorful, which can throw off dishes.  The chickn' couldn't balance out the sweet, heavy flavors of the mole sauce nor could it carry the burrito's spices into flavortown.  Some of the dishes rely heavily on flavors from cilantro, onion, etc. to the point that they will make bites taste like nothing else.  And each of the vegan ingredients is still trying to imitate an animal product, so the cheese will taste nutty and the sour cream will taste unsatisfying.  The best dishes avoid these pitfalls, and I enjoyed the potato tacos because they use potatoes instead of meat substitutes and avoided flavors that would dominate the food.

6/20/13

Even though they don't sell pizza-by-the-slice, which is really sad since not a lot of places in WC do, we stop in here from time to time for lunch.

My husband often orders a small pepperoni. ($10). I like the half salami hot sandwich, (light mayo with cheddar cheese, mustard, tomoato, pickles, lettuce, and an add of hot peppers (onions also optional) on sourdough). It comes with a half salad (with everything on it, and ranch dressing).

Sandwich is killer. The bread is awesome. And the amount of everything is great - not overwhelming. They'll give you extra hot peppers on request. The salad is good too, and so is their ranch. It's a fair amount of food for $10. And it comes with a soda which I give to husband.

The employees are all very friendly and helpful. We've had good service and received sincere thank yous as we left. They are all working but take the time to interact with customers, even when the place is crowded.

NICE OUTDOOR SEATING AREA

A few tables out front in the sun, a couple in the shade, and all the seating inside this Starbucks is really a nice perk about this location.  I have always found service to be quick here. I lived a few blocks away for many years (at my parents house).

The biggest inconvenience here is that you can't drive directly from this parking lot into the one with the BevMo next door.  It's hard for me to turn down a cold frappaccino, especially on the hot days. Seriously, I have no self control. Extra whipped cream, please. We had to join a gym recently to counter all the whipped in my life.

I had a friend that worked here years ago and I used to come in from time to time just to say hello. I don't know if they had free wifi then but they definitely do now. Just like most Starbucks, you see people sipping their drinks at tables while pecking away at laptop keys. If this location were closer to home we'd be happy to frequent here, but the smaller Starbucks on Treat is nice too!

text:
Burger Im.... new place in Modesto... well new in 4-8-2019... I love trying new places and seeing new area open up.  If you drive down the road and blink you will miss it. There no might about it.. what dose burger it means??   "Many burgers" in Hebrew.... yes it's a Mediterranean spin on American Burgers.... they have lamb burgers and salmon burgers ... and to my surprise, they have a falafel burger.... hmmm....  best falafel sandwich is San Jose "falafel drive" in on Stevenson... but getting back to the burger im... I ordered a BIG burger. The dry-aged beef... 1/3 burger with bbq sauce, bacon, and onion rings.... something like Burger King has on their menu.....  the burger was 7.99 and 2.99 more you get a choice of something deep fried and a soda... I pick fries and onion rings. To try more that one thing half and a half.... what puzzled me was there were no real french fries..  yeah they have sweet potato fries... but they're always too sweet for me. when you're looking for something salty and crunchy you want fries... I wanted to ask them .... but I went with the flow.... the place was clean and the floor design was beautiful... I saw it done in other places a collage of paints swirled on the floor.. good colors nice design.... they have TVs playing sports ... I was watching tennis at the time .... then my burger was ready .... they call my name as they brought it to me .... bam my meal on a mini metal cookie sheet...  I looked at the burger then the fried Goods.  Onion rings were real onion... I hate those fake process onion rings.... there so nasty.... and then I see the fries... or what they call fries ...more like thick potato chips ... don't get me wrong there were good .... soft but kinda crispy... enjoyable... it looks like there spin on potatoes.... not bad .... but if you wanted French fries you would have to go somewhere else.... and then the burger... I was looking for a whopper size or a size of Nations hamburger... ( Nations hamburger in Tracy is one of the best burgers you can get in California... #2 is in and out talking about chain restaurants)  but the size of the burger was like a big mac... maybe a little bigger ... but not as big as the Quarter Pounder from McDonald's... so I taste it ..... but wait let me look inside  2 onion  rings  one pattie that looks from a frozen box.. not hand pressed .. and bbq sauce with shards of bacon.... yes I have pictures to show you what it looks like.... not big thick bacon hanging from the Sides of the bun... but chips of bacon that placed on the burger that each bite you have a good chance of tasting bacon..... I was not impressed... for calling your self Gourmet Burgers or big burgers ... it was a letdown ... I think Red Robbins ....yum!!! Lol or farmer boys make a better-looking burger then here .... but that looks.... so I try a bite.....the first thought that went through my mind was that little burger from burgers king ... I think there call rodeo burger .... the bbq just tasted like that .... wasn't even bullseye or kc masterpiece.... it was a can bottle or bag bbq sauce.... wow swing and a miss ... it should have been a homemade bbq or a doctor Up BBQ sauce from a bottle.... but threw the whole burger I had that sauce rolling around in my mouth .... don't get me wrong I like the rodeo burger from burgers king.... but I paid 7.99 for a 1 dollar copycat burger .... wasn't happy at all.... maybe I order the wrong burger for me ... maybe so .... but an 8 dollar burger should remind me of a 1 dollar burger from BK.... I like burger king.. the whopper is a good burger ...
So all in all ... no normal French fries.... and the burger was a fancy cheap burger from burgers king. I don't think I will go back ...

Unexpectedly, the shrimp was my favourite part of the dish, due to their high quality, and it was an excellent and humongous dish overall. The raita and naan were excellent as well. As I was indulging in my Biryani,  my work partner had the buffet, but I don't think he enjoyed the experience as much as I, therefore I'd recommend ordering a la carte. I  don't get to go to Indian food often enough and highly recommend Punjab, where the service was friendly and guests are anticipated with and clean, a cozy, well decorated restaurant.

text:
4/10/18 - 3 stars

We were told it would be a 40 minute wait for breakfast so we put our names in and went out to grab some caffeine across the street. We checked back in at Driftwood after getting our drinks, and voila! Only 10 minutes after we'd originally arrived, we were seated. Maybe they're trying to scare off customers with the long wait times they quote, because we really did almost go somewhere else, but regardless, we were seated with steaming coffees in our hands, that we would've just ordered here had we known it would be only 10 minutes.

Yay for our server checking in on us quickly and getting waters to the table and going over the specials (which included corned beef hash, but no green eggs and ham - it was St. Patty's Day!!) I don't usually order steak with breakfast, but after a hard day snowboarding the day before, I think my body was asking me for protein, so I ordered the steak and eggs meal. I asked for the steak to be cooked as rare as possible. I even joked that they didn't really have to cook it at all. So even though I knew we weren't at some fancy steakhouse, imagine my surprise when it was served medium/brown inside. (Sad Amy). I picked at it but I just can't eat my food this way so my share of our $31 breakfast was a little wasted, but Fredie seemed to enjoy his so that's good. Service was great as well.

6/28/2012 - 4 star

We had a very long wait to get in, which is fine unless you're told 10 minutes and you wait an hour. We waited about 25 minutes, just what the hostess quoted!  The hostess finally called our names and walked us to our table. She had a wonderful smile and was friendly, making conversation as we walked. It stands out to me that hostesses at the Cheesecake Factory are very good about this also, but not a lot of other places are.

Once seated we looked over the menu as we waited for a server. And waited. And then finally gave up and asked someone if we had a server assigned to us.  Not sure if we'd been lost in the crowd of customers or if the server was just busy. I'm hoping it was the former, since you should never seat a table if you're too busy to serve them.

We were finally acknowledged and received some water (yay!) and placed our food orders. I ordered French toast. I can't remember the last time I had the delicious bread so no matter what, this would probably be the best French toast I'd had in a long time. It really lived up. I used the entire cup of butter and all the syrup and it was soooo good!

My fiance had eggs and some other stuff.... toast? Bacon? I can't remember. I remember toast because I ate some of his too. I was craving all sorts of stuff so I covered his toast in more butter and jelly and ate what he couldn't finish.  I also ate two of his eggs. He ordered them over-easy but received them over-hard (the yellows were cooked). So he asked for new eggs and I ate his hard ones. Mmmm, eating his hard ones - best breakfast ever!

Our server wasn't bad - service was attentive once we were noticed. Water stayed full, etc. I'd totally go back, next time we're in Tahoe. $22.62 total.

The establishment seemed like a really cool place, the employees were great. This is my first time here and im just grabbing some fish and chips to go. Was told over the phone that my order would be ready at 6:30. Walked in the door at 6:32 and was told that it would be a cpl. more mins.(no problem at all) I was even offered a drink "on the house" while I waited.

Pretty sure it was a solid 20 mins more before  I was out the door , food in hand.
Now, while I was waiting...... the sushi creations being brought out of the kitchen by the servers looked amazing! I'm born and raised in L.A. and have traveled and I know my sushi.
I was kicking myself for only getting the fish and chips, seriously looked that good !

Then... I got to eating my order. Did I mention the LA and traveling things, oh ya..... Well I know my fish and chips !!
I was surprised the fish was not in the shape of little dinosaurs, ya know like the name brand boxed stuff from the supermarket.
Pretty sure it was something similar. To be fair it was not like "van decamp"  bad. More like Gordon's..... And it did not come with malt Vinegar! (I know right)

Not what I was expecting, especially after seeing what was coming out of the kitchen.
But hey, the fries were great !
A generous 4 stars !
I'm not giving up on you Beer Werks, I will be back, to dine in this time, and give you another chance at getting that fifth star. I think you have potential !!
The place was clean, the staff was happy and I even like the rock n roll theme.
Oh and I think they even sold merchandise.

name: Alan Harnett
text:
Came on a weekday for lunch.  It was fairly quiet.  Menu is basic; mac and cheese, fries, wings, and drinks.  They also have beer on tap.  Start by choosing your choice of sauce, then choose your choice of pasta, then choose the items you want stired in, then choose your toppings.  The mac and cheese comes in one size which is enough for a large meal.  You could also share an order of mac and cheese and get an order of wings or fries to share.  I ordered the basic cheese sauce with chicken, bacon, peas inside, with panko bread crumbs on top.  I liked what I ordered, but I wouldn't say it was the best mac and cheese I've ever had.  On the tables is hot sauce and napkins.  The togo boxes, water, napkins, and utensils are self serve.  Interior was neatly decorated.  Service was nice, but not over the top.  They need some AC or fans for the summer days as it gets hot in there.

Order at the counter, then sit down and listen for your name to be called.

Depending when you come, parking is pretty easy on the street within a couple blocks.

name: Martin Torres
text:
I first visited about 7 years ago, when i first heard of a "Bison Burger". I had another burger today (May 30th 2020) and it was just as good as the first time i had it. I don't go as often as i want because i moved out of the area (an hour north) but when i visit family, and friends, I try to make it a point to visit this amazing humble burger joint. Burgers are moist and juicy while the topmost surface isn't too charred or burnt. The condiments are always fresh, and the shakes are just the right thickness without being *too* thick to drink with a straw. The mushrooms are great and you can tell they were clean before being cooked. The cheese is added at the perfect time so its not melted onto their grill but its still melted. The vibe of San Carlos doesn't match the vibe inside Sliders in my opinion. I think being well aged is the only thing Sliders and San Carlos have in common. The rest of the street is somewhat run down with cracked streets, outdated locations, and even a few homeless in the area. But Sliders Burgers screams humble 50s with a modern take on flavor. I spoke to the owner a while back and he's still the same perfect chef with the same perfect knack for customer service.

(If you're reading this, i love what you've done with the place over the years and can't wait for another burger. Hope everyone stays successful and much love to every one of your employees.)

text:
I've been a regular at this location since they opened, but they've lost my business as of today.
I used the app to place a $65 order (with a 15% tip in the anticipation of everything being great, as it once was).
The app stated my order would be ready in 20 minutes. Twenty minutes later I'm standing in line to pick up my order & I receive a notification stating my order was picked up. Huh?
Upon making it to the head of the line, the employee notified me that my order wouldn't be ready for over an hour (it's been 30 minutes at this point for a twenty minute order). He didn't even ask my name, so how did he know when my order would be ready? I told him to cancel the order; he said he could not. I left, intending to call the bank to let them handle it.
Of course there was no one answering the phones on Christmas & since it had been 1.5 hours since placing the order & my family was starving, I went back to Denny's. Wow, it was ready.
Took it home without checking the order. One side of sausage was missing & apparently Denny's doesn't answer their phone on Christmas, either. The Super-Bird & one of the Slam-Burgers had STALE BREAD; we ate the meat because we were all so hungry at this point. The bacon on one of the Slam-Burgers was BURNT. Both of us who are the stale-breaded sandwiches got sick later in the day. Merry Christmas!
So basically, Denny's raked in $65 & a 15% tip for selling food that should have been thrown away & didn't even deliver the sausage that was paid for. I am beyond disgusted with this order & the complete lack of service.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
7/6/14

After a dental appointment with a mouth-numbing shot, a small filling, and a teeth cleaning, I decided to chomp on some crunchy tacos. I stopped in El Molino on Monument, placed an order for two tacos dorado, and took a spot alone at a table by their juice bar.

I watched a man (perhaps the manager) come out and kill the single fly in the place with a swift "SWAT" with his flyswatter.  Keeping it clean! He also sprayed down the tables while another woman swept the floor. They do a good job keeping everything clean, especially with the high volume of foot traffic. There was always someone in line while I waited for my food and while I ate.

I really enjoyed the crunchy tacos while their hot meat-potato filling and crispy, fresh lettuce.  I'm still not a big fan of crispy, crunchy chips, but I do like their hot salsa. And I love how fresh the tortillas are! (of course).

This is definitely one of the nicer taquerias on Monument!

Updated from: 1/25/13 (three star)

I LIKE MY CHIPS THIN AND CRISPY ~ WITH LOTS OF SALT

I came here last nght for dinner #2. What's dinner #2, you ask? It's when you spend all afternoon thinking about what you want for dinner and you can't decide between two places so you eat at them both. I came here after Mercado Del Sol, less than a block away.

For $5-something I ordered one carnitas taco, chips & salsa, and 2 cheese tamales (to go - $1 each). I had some leftover glass-bottled Coke from dinner #1 so no drink here.

The taco was okay - the meat was very good and super tender but there was too much of it for me. Lots of cilantro on top and some salsa verde but the presentation was a little sloppy. Plus, the salsa verde wasn't my favorite. I requested a hotter salsa also and received a chipotle-red. The flavor was smokey and good but not all that hot either.
The tortilla was very good. It was bigger than expected and very fresh. It tasted like a flour tortilla but I imagine was white corn? I don't know...

The chips were disappointing. They were super crispy but much too thick for me. They had a lot of grease, which I like because it makes the salt stick, but lime juice also makes the salt stick and when chips are served in a plastic bag the grease gets all over your hand every time you go to grab one. But I wouldn't have cared if they hadn't been so thick - just too filling. (And not just cuz it was dinner #2 - I always prefer skinny chips).

The tamales were picked at later in the evening but they will be tonight's dinner. I'll definitely be back to this place since I want to try the nachos. And maybe a smoothie from their juice bar. It looked good and several people inside were sipping refreshing parfait-style drinks. Chunks of fruit and thick goodness.  Yum

4/28/13

WELCOME TO MONUMENT, OK CAFE! I LIKE THE NEW LOOK!!!

Oh so much food! What a yummy lunch in Concord. This former donut shop turned Chinese Restaurant is brand spanking new! Go check them out and then thank me. Friendly service and a great experience with surprisingly really low prices. Especially for the amount of food youre getting.

We started our lunch today with Wor Wonton soup. After a large serving of the warm goodness, we moved on to pulled pork sandwiches on fried sweet buns. The slider-like sandwiches had cilantro and cucumber with plum sauce for the pork. Very good! The bread was excellent and the owner told us they are the only sandwiches with this style bread in the East Bay.

For entrees we started with pan fried noodles. The crispy noodles had a nicely flavored sauce and lots of veggies and pork and fresh seafood. The noodles were so good! We'd never ordered this before. Broccoli beef and cashew chicken are dishes typically seen when we dine with my family and they both made an appearance today as well. They were each good in their own way. Not overly seasoned but a nice proportion of flavor. I actually didn't add any hot oil to my dishes like usual, though my mom put some on her steamed rice and enjoyed it.

My favorite dish was the salt and pepper fish. The fish was really nicely breaded with a thin and flavorful breading. On top were crispy, tiny cubes of fried onion bits and jalapeno slices. Holy heaven. I LOVE jalapenos. And I love crispy fried onion bits. The combination with the tender fish was excellent. All of the plates were piled high with food so we were pretty full at the end, but I couldn't stop eating the topping that was on the fish. Definitely my favorite.

They serve shaved ice with fresh fruit flavors (and donuts) but we skipped dessert this time. Good excuse to come back. The brand new kitchen sure looked clean. The owner mentioned they're still so new they're trying to find the right chef. I hope they keep the guy today. He was OK Cafe by me!

This is definitely a good choice for the deep dish lovers. I've never seen a pizza quite this...deep. Layers and layers of sauce, crust, cheese, and toppings; it's really a remarkable sight.

I'm personally not much of a deep dish person, but while on a double date my husband and I split a pizza and decided to go with the deep one we'd heard so much about. The pizza itself was very good, loved the tomato sauce, and it was nice that we could still do half his "topping" (err, filling), and half what I wanted. It's also great that they have vegan options, since our awesome vegan friends were the other couple dining with us!

When my husband and I arrived we had decided to take a seat outside and the hostess led us to a table. We were a little early and waiting for the other two people, but also waiting for water. And waiting for a waiter. And waiting.... until we decided we didn't want to be the forgotten table out front and asked to be moved inside...  Where it was unfortunately uncomfortably warm. It's hard to eat pizza when youre hot. It's hard to eat anything!

I started with a fresh salad. I definitely shouldn't have ordered this since the pizza was so much food but it was good. A large block of cheese to crumble myself sat on top, and it made a huge mess on the table and my hands as the over-filled bowl spilled with crumbly cheese. But overall food was good, and service was good once we moved back inside.  It is an expensive pizza though. Since I prefer a thinner price tag on a thinner slice anyhow, I'd prob only come back if we were going out with friends again.

text:
12/12/14

Not long after our first experience on a Sunday evening, Derek (the owner/manager) contacted me about my review. He insisted that their business deserved a second chance, and sincerely apologized for everything that happened. I thanked him, and a couple weeks later he followed up and contacted me again, inviting me back and telling me a little bit more about deals on their website.

We called for delivery on another Sunday. They had lots of specials online - definitely check out their deals before ordering off the menu. This gave us the opportunity to try their parmesan breadsticks, in addition to a pepperoni and sun-dried tomato pizza, and 6 more chicken wings. I love the spicy garlic sauce on the wings - they were still too hot for my husband.

Our food arrived really quickly - faster than the estimated time we'd received on the phone.  We ordered thin-crust this time (but perhaps we'll just order well-done next time we call in with the regular crust.)  The thin crust was delicious - the dough is nicely seasoned and we liked our choice of toppings together with their yummy sauce. I believe that same marinara is what was served with the breadsticks. I'm going to need extra sauce next time - it's really good! I want to dip my pizza in it too.

I'm glad to know that this small business actually cared about our experience.  Derek really did care. And he was so nice in his messages - I hope that he does really well. He has two new loyal fans!

Previous review
11/11/14 - 3 stars

On Sunday night at 9:30 we decided to call around for a pizza.  I wasn't really hungry but my husband wanted one for delivery.  We called Pizza My Way but they said they weren't still delivering, even though they weren't closed.  Eat 24 was available though so we placed the order of a medium meat pizza and 6 garlic chicken wings for delivery.  It totaled about $30.

I guess the person making the pizza was in a hurry because our pizza was really undercooked.  Really, really doughy inside. It took 75 minutes to get to us, and arrived hot, so that couldn't be all Eat 24's fault. I liked the sauce on the pizza but we only each ate one piece.  The wings were really fatty and too spicy for my husband. We were really disappointed.

However, two days later we baked the pizza for a while, and then broiled it afterward.  it was a lot better with the dough completely cooked.  The cheese still tasted kind of cheap, but the pizza itself was a lot better.  It sucks that someone rushed our $30 pizza the night we originally ordered it and it was more or less inedible then, since it was noticeably better once it fully cooked. I'll stick with Domino's delivery for half the price.

Big parking lot, though, it does get crowded.

HELLO, HOT SALSA

So the hot salsa here isn't even very hot. And sometimes the medium salsa is more spicy than hot. But the bright red, "hot" salsa of Chipotle is tasty! I love it!! And in combination with the chips and lime salt it's one of the things I get random cravings for. Luckily, I live nearby this location.  We can walk over and pick up our salsa and soft tacos whenever we want.

The soft tacos are pretty good. That's the only thing I'll get if I come here.  Though sometimes they can be made very messily and it's definitely something I want to eat with a fork. This location gets pretty crowded but I rarely visit Chipotle anywhere and stand in line. It's too easy to call in your order and we haven't had problems with accuracy. (*knock on wood*)

I believe Chipotle is one of the companies that advocates for humane animal treatment from the businesses they buy from. So that's a good thing! They also offer delicious sofritas for the vegans.

Keep up the good salsa, guys!

text:
6/17/13

LET US EAT LETTUCE

Hoping for a nice FAther's Day lunch we met my husband's parents in downtown Walnut Creek. Stelle Bistro was closed without announcement. Katy's Kreek was so packed the area outside was saturated with people waiting. And then there we were, at Lettuce. I'd never been inside before but knew to expect the deli style atmosphere. Service is at a counter, rather than tableside. A large menu hangs on the wall but you can also look at the ingredients in front of you if you want to change or add something.

I ordered the Farmer's Salad and enjoyed asparagus, beets, mixed greens and croutons (ask for extra if you like croutons - they're big, but they're good, and I didn't get many to start). It was nicely dressed. The guy who prepared it for me was very friendly and made conversation as he worked.

My husband and his dad both had a BLT on focaccia. His dad added a corn chowder to his order, after reading "clam chowder" by accident. We were all surprised how little clam there was, until we looked at the menu again and realized our mistake. The sandwich was very good. I finished what he couldn't eat. There was an herbed mayo in the bread and the flavor really stood out. The bacon was crispy. It could have used an extra slice of tomato, but overall was really tasty!

Mom and her Mom fared the least well. Neither of them loving their dish. Mom had a salad that was somewhat overwhelmed by gorgonzola, making it just a little too bitter for her (and my) liking. There was a TON of avocado in it and I even ate some huge chunks of it in the couple bites I had. It was wonderful! My husband's grandmother ordered a small bowl of angelhair pasta. The chicken pieces in it were very dry so even though it had good flavor, it wasn't nearly as good as everyone else's dishes.

The bruschetta and garlic bread looked great but I wasn't about to pay that much extra for each piece. I think it was $3 and $1.50, respectively. I had water to drink (oh how I love the cucumber water!) and husband had a can of soda. Our table total was around $60. The food was really good but $10 is a lot for a bowl of salad that I was just about able to finish. A couple bites of it went home with me in my reuseable to-go container.  :) But they didn't make it all the home. Yum.

5/21/13

LETTUCE EAT TACOS!

Awww Tuesday. My favorite day of the week and the most appropriate one for another taco review.

Honestly, this JITB location is as close to five star as fast food can get. The parking here is a nightmare though. If the drive-thru line is more than a few cars long, it makes parking for us dine-in people a nightmare. The drive-thru cars block the spots and the way to the exit. During prime fast food hours I've also seen the line of cars reach the end of the parking lot, spilling onto N. Main Street. Not fun.

BUT... at the end of the day (literally) when all the other establishments have locked their doors and turned off their lights, Jack is waiting for you. "Come eat here" his voice calls somewhere in the back of your hungry mind. You can even dine-in at a clean table - 24 hrs a day! Pretty awesome.

They used to have a great (healthy-ish) teriyaki bowl. I liked that a lot. And the curly fries are pretty good. My favorite menu item is ultimately the taco (2 for $1.00!!).  It wasn't always my favorite. An ultra-greasy shell with oily, wilted lettuce and a fried cheese slice over the meat-product inside... hmmm, not so much. But if you ask for extra lettuce they throw it on after cooking the taco. So you get your hot taco and crunchy shell with fresh, crispy lettuce. It totally changes the taco. Learning to ask for this has renewed my love for this killer deal on the JITB Value Menu. And this is the best location to order it from!

PS - I'd love to see more vegetarian options. Can you please make potato tacos??

text: The Habit is arguably just as good and some might even say better than In n Out. The burgers are excellent and unlike In n Out they have more than just beef and potatoes. The chicken sandwiches are delicious if you're looking for a healthier alternative and their onion rings are as good as they get if you're tired of the typical side of french fries. This location has parking directly in front or two parking structures that are easily accessed. Wait time varies but don't expect a quick visit if you're there during lunch or dinner as this location is very popular with local residents. The sitting area is always kept clean and trash free, the employees are always very friendly and efficient. Overall you won't be disappointed if you're looking for a reasonably priced all American meal!

Let's see, when was the last time someone thanked you for eating at their fast food restaurant? I got my two medium two topping pizzas, that have never tasted that good ever before, and left with a good feeling.  I always order online, there never is that human face to face, next time you want a pizza in Mira Mesa take 15 busy minutes and visit this restaurant. name: Endless Possibles
text:
You're buying everything but quality sushi here. It's not a terrible thing really but if you're looking for really great sushi this is not the place. The chefs signatures are worth trying if you do still decide to come here, some with a unique flavor. The micro greens really are not a welcome addition to the sushi, that's just my opinion though, the ratio simply isn't right for taste, but it does look cool I guess. The fatty tuna was disappointing, which is highly disappointing for a favorite that we all drop big dollars on, $22 for 2 pieces. Clearly not "Otoro" This same $11 slice of fish had a piece of unchewable tissue in it, very gross.
Whiskey: The gals whiskey knowledge was completely fabricated which was really bad.. as a savior, their whiskey selection is definitely the best in the entire Coachella Valley when it comes to Japanese whiskeys. Absolutely come here if you're looking for some very very rare (Yamazaki 25yr, and more) whiskeys with your fish.
The gyoza was great! Crispy outsides, chewy center.
The drinks were also very very good.
If you want a fun dining experience with top notch drinks and typical tasting sushi, I absolutely encourage you to come here. The crowd is very trendy, almost hipster status really.
If you're looking for epic sushi, this places reputation will absolutely mislead you, unless you have zero experience with high quality sushi, then you'll like it.

text: My wife & I have been coming here for years. This is one of the best Indian restaurant in the San Francisco bay area. It has a variety of Indian cuisine including Punjabi, Gujarati & South Indian items - but not dosas. This is the place for Punjabi/North Indian vegetarian food. The service is always quick & fast. Thalis are a good item to order - you get a little bit of everything & the items in the thali change regularly. I like the sag paneer & my wife likes the bhindi masala, along with paratha & methi paratha. The palak pakora is a good appetizer. For lighter fare, have the dahi papdi chaat & hara bhara bhel. For a light refreshing cool & healthy drink, have the chaas. The lassi is a thicker yogurt drink. There can be a short line during peak dining times. Parking can be tight with Starbucks in the same shopping center.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
11/9/17

I've been to all sorts of D&B locations across the US and I always enjoy Milpitas, which is the one now closest to my home. Usually have a really great time playing games, getting drinks and food, and watching sports on the bar screens as we walk around. I've even gone home with some really cute 18+ prizes from my ticket wins.

Our last visit was kind of irregular. We had my boyfriend's sons with us and it was their first time at a Dave and Busters. Some locations don't allow under 21, but this one does! We had a killer time but a few of the games weren't working properly and it was frustrating trying to find a staff person.

At the end of our gaming we sat in the restaurant area to eat and shared some delicious nachos (only $5 during games), lobster alfredo ($19.99), All Fives appetizer sampler ($23.99), a Mac Stack ($12.99) and a burger ($13.99) (Bud Lights -- $5.99, Cokes $3.29). Everything tasted outstanding but service was a little slow and again, it wasn't the usual standard D&B typically lives up to.

However, I mentioned the issues I came across and felt like their customer service department really cares and listens and wants you to have a better-than-great visit. Angel in customer service was genuinely nice and really made us feel like valued customers.

We can't wait to return - with or without the kids. It's definitely a fun adults-only outing, but you can have fun here at any age because they really have games to offer for everyone's likes and interests.

7/25/14 - 3 stars

I'm a pretty big fan of D&Bs, some more than others. I like the games, the bar, and the food. This is not my favorite D&B location. The age requirement varies by location, and unfortunately children are allowed inside this particular barcade. I'm not trying to offend all the parents that bring their kids, so I'll leave it at that, but there are more awesome locations that don't allow children.

We came in for dinner and games on Sunday night and it was more crowded than I expected, even though I've never really seen this place not busy.  Husband and I ordered from the Eat & Play Combo menu. I had a Caesar and he had pretzel dogs.  Two beers and a $20 play card all for $50!

The food took forever to arrive but we expected that. It's not really understandable since I had cold food and pretzel dogs can't take that long, but it wasn't a big deal.  Our server (Marilyn) was awesome. Girl was hustling! From table to table, she was getting her job done! Even with annoying customers like me ("May I have some lemon?" *Ten minutes later* "May I have some more lemon?") I got sort of citrus crazy and yet she kept returning to check on us. Superior service! Even got a sweet note on our receipt wishing us fun with the gaming!

Tons of the games happened to be dark or out of service last weekend. Another terrific employee we encountered was Justin, who was the only technician working Sunday night. We waited patiently as the nice security guard brought Justin over to our game where the tickets had jammed in the machine. It was the polar bear baseball game, totally fun! Justin was smiling even though he had two more repairs lined up before he was even done helping us. Super busy and a positive worker. That's always nice to see.

Coolest thing we noticed were several of the new games could be played once for FREE if you had a new power card or recharged it that day. We played some fun games that we would have never played if not for that!

name: Amy Palmer
text:
5/17/13
SPECIAL OCCASIONS

By chance, I feel like I've ended up here on two special occasions. A few years ago we spontaneous ate here as a large group the night before my sister's wedding. Then yesterday I walked over and lunched with my boss and two other attorneys to discuss a shift in responsibilities (which was a good thing for my position). Both very special events. I've called in orders of rice (to-go) more than once and picked them up without problem, but the real experience here is dining in.

I love the decorations and dim lighting. Even the staff's traditional dresscode make the lunch experience a little nicer. Yesterday we sat in a private booth in the back. The four of us fit very comfortably and it was private. Steamed edamame was brought without asking and a delicious hot tea in a beautiful teapot arrived upon reuqest.

I ordered a lunch special of chicken teriyaki and calimari katsu. It came with several rice rolls, pickled ginger in thick slices, miso soup, house salad, and a dipping sauce. I asked for hot sauce and received two different ones (a generic 'red' sauce and a creamy pink-colored hot sauce). Both were great.  The portions (meat) were just a little smaller than other places around here but I think the quality was better than I remembered. I espiecially enjoyed the crunchy calamari strips. Very nice flavor on the light breading. The miso was also very good and the bowl was a good size. Salad was slightly over-dressed.

I'll have to remember to walk over here more often. I can't believe it'd been years since I'd sat down here for lunch.

Considering I get fast food more than once a month, I think that this place is worth a visit...be it late night box or regular menu item, they consistently get my order right.  The price you pay is higher than other fast food joints, but it's because they will serve you anything and everything off the menu 24/7.  I can't say this place had its downsides, like when the card transactions aren't available(hasn't happened to me in forever tho), but it seems it's been fixed I guess. It would only happen after midnight, but I don't visit around that time anymore(since covid), so no stars off for that.  I've visited the Mc Donald's and the BK and even the Wendy's near by and they sometimes forget to get check my order, or don't add enough of one item, and I'm pretty sure I talk the same at all the drive through order mics.

I would suggest this place for the box meal or anything else your craving over the other places.

text:
Wonderful lunch experience. Lunch is busy with a good atmosphere. It has a great business lunch vibe. It’s easy to get a table without a wait. Parking is challenging on the street.

Cockscomb (as the name implies) is a meat focused restaurant. They also have a few seafood dishes. The menu is a mix of classic with an innovative spin.

I started out with the chicharones which were dusted with a cheese powder. My burger was reasonably priced and delicious! It came with fries. The dessert was a seasonal panna cotta which again was outstanding and I could tell was created by a pastry chef.

The service was wonderful. Attentive, passionate, friendly, and very knowledgeable. This is a must if your in San Francisco.
