name: Mihir Meghani
text: This is one of San Francisco's best gourmet vegetarian restaurants. We have been coming here for years. The menu changes regularly. Most recently we had some of their non alcoholic wine, the mushroom farro risotto, a side of artichokes, asparagus pizza, soup (kale or chard), & avocado salad. The appetizers were better than the entrees, which at Greens I have found to be slightly bland. I rate the food as being slightly lower than Millenium (the other high end gourmet restaurant in San Francisco), but Greens has the San Francisco Bay & Golden Gate Bridge view (Millenium has no view) & is cheaper. All in all, a place you should eat at. The food is creative & my comments are more subtleties from a self-appointed vegetarian food connoisseur. Be sure to reserve your table in advance, as they are booked months in advance for prime time, & weeks in advance for other dates. They are located in Fort Mason. You can park for free just outside Fort Mason or pay $2 per  hour to park in the Fort Mason parking lot.

name: Susan Pearson
text:
Great old school diner serving a variety of food.  Everything from breakfast through dinner.  Pancakes and crepes to sandwiches and steaks.  They also have some house wines and beer.

I went here for an event and was very impressed with how they had transformed the space.  I remember when this was a Bob's Big Boy.  Now it is decorated like a 50s diner.  Very clean and fun.  They have lots of indoor seating both public and private and an outside patio area as well.

I sampled the minestrone soup, seasoned fries and California Melt.  All were quite good.  My companions had a veggie burger and the pastrami melt and said they were good.

I think this could once again be a hangout for teens like it was back in the day, as well as a nice place to take family or just get some good comfort food.

If this is your only option for Chinese then go for it.

text: This restaurant (owned by the wife) & the sibling restaurant Palo Alto Sol (owned by the husband) are great. They have great vegetarian options & the staff are familiar with what is truly vegetarian. Enchiladas are my favorite. In the past, we have had enfrijolades which is a set of 3 corn tortillas covered with beans & some vegetables & is very light on cheese - if you want this spicy be sure to ask for chipotle sauce. The enchiladas mexicanas had some sour cream - we got cheese inside & red sauce on top which was not spicy. The enchiladas guajillo we got with cheese & spinach inside, & this sauce was creamy with a slight spicy (but not hot) tinge. I had De La Plaza before & that was good. The complimentary chips & sauces are good but filling. If you order a la carte, it is $3 less than the full entree with beans & rice. They charge for sharing. Get Mexican Coca Cola. Service is good. The restaurant is colorful but small, & they don't take reservations.

text:
I kept walking by this place while shopping for groceries but it always seemed closed but I made a mental bookmark in my head. Wanting to try a new option for lunch and Tony wanting to watch the Warrior game, we decided to walk down the few blocks from our house to check it out.
The inside is very simple and no frills. We grabbed a seat by the bar but in a view of a large screen tv to catch the game. The menu seemed very minimal so I was a bit worried at first. We were hoping to try their burger but that was not on the menu (even though it is listed on their website) so that was disappointing. We decided to split the Chicken Tenders, French Fries and Caesar Salad.
This may all seem like typical bar food but alas it was not! Each dish came out and tasted like an upscale version of themselves. The fries were thick and moist and had a house aioli it came with that was amazing. The tenders were tender (PUN INTENDED!) and had a rosemary coating which brought out a really nice flavor. I was extremely surprised because I would see this type of food quality at the higher end restaurants that we go to. The caesar salad was actually a large portion and perfectly dressed.

name: Mihir Meghani
text: Absolutely great service. There is seating in their heated patio that is open to the outside, as well as inside the restaurant. From the outside, this restaurant in the Mission area seems like a hole in the wall, but it is a nice restaurant from inside. The food came quickly & the servers were very friendly & helpful. This time, we had a virgin mojito, tangerine aqua fresca, chilaquiles, tacos (one each of RAJAS- roasted poblano chilies and onions, HONGOS – sauteed mushrooms with garlic, & GREENS – seasonal greens sautéed with fresh garlic and chile), & flan. We added salsa on the side. We love the food. It is all vegetarian & vegan.

This was our first experience dining @ Khunying Thai and it was satisfying.

We started with the Roti, which was perfect. It was still hot when it arrived, sliced into 10-12 triangles, wasn't oily and the egdes we're crisp and flakey. The dipping curry sauce tasty as well.

Our kids wanted the bbq chicken but they didn't have any chicken.  Not a good first impression but they did have the chicken satay.  They said it was "yummy" and the portions seemed larger than what they're used to eating.

My go to dish to sample a new Thai restaurant is Pad Thai.  I've been to Thailand twice so I know what traditional Phad Thai should taste like.

I first noticed the noodles, it was thinner than the typical rice noodles. It looked almost like a ramen noodle. It didn't contain eggs or the garnishes like the cilantro, peanuts, carrots, or even the lime wedge.  Besides the noodles, it did have large pieces of tofu, strips of chicken green onions, and bean sprouts.

Except for the missing items, the Pad Thai was still delicious. I was able to taste the tamarind, which has a sweet and sour flavor. The portion size was comparable to Thai Grata or Oros servings.

Also, we tried the Tom Yum soup, the broth was pleasing. Plenty of shrimp, mushrooms, tomatoes, and chile's.

The service was quick since we were the only customers on a Friday night. The prices are expensive compared to other Thai restaurants in the area.

We'll try this restaurant again, we haven't decided if we will be faithful customers yet.

Update- after several months have pasted. We decided to give this restaurant another chance.

We ordered the BBQ chicken again,  It was delicious.  However, part of the drum stick was COLD! But it wasn't pink  maybe it was refrigerated and they just reheated it. Also,  normally when a half a chicken is served.its only split in half. I was given a whole leg  but the breast was cut into 3 parts. Maybe it was  intended for another dish.

Also, we ordered the the grilled prawns with glass noodles or Goong Ob Woonsen. The noodles was delicious but the prawns had no flavor at all.

We gave this restaurant a second chance  and the food  being served here is a hit or miss! We won't be returning.

text:
Great Ambiance Poor Food Poor Drinks

We went here for Dine Downtown, the week in San Jose where restaurants give fixed price menus for discounted rate. Unfortunately, this place provided all lack luster food fare.

We ordered old fashions at the table, we received a glass of whisky with water and a maraschino cherry at the bottom. It was not an old fashion, it was just bad.

Three of us ordered off the fixed menu, one ordered off the standard menu.  The fixed menu items were poor.  Soup was bland, having no flavor and served warm.  The tomato mozzarella salad, was just sliced roma tomatoes with slices of mozzarella and strips of basil.  It was a disappointment with under ripe tomatoes.

The entrees continued in the train of the meal. The pasta with chicken and shrimp, was bland, lacking any flavor to an overly buttered and oiled dish.  Luckily, the table did come with salt.  The mashed potatoes had an odd sticky texture, but missed one of the great joys of mashed potatoes, the flavor of a potato mixed with creamy butter.  They were just sticky bland mash.

But, maybe there was hope with desserts.  Yet, there was none.  The berries with grand marnier cream, was a little cup of berries with non sugared whip cream.  The berries weren't macerated, they weren't even ripe! If you went to the grocery store, bought some berries, threw them in a glass, whipped up some heavy cream and gave it to your significant other, they'd wonder why you decided to put them on a bland diet.  Maybe you did something wrong to offend them, or maybe you just decided that taking a page from the chef at the Loft was a good idea.

The creme brulee was curdled, making it and oddly textured sweet caramel covered scrambled egg.

Why not 1 star you ask?  Why give them two stars? Well, the service was nice and attentive.  The roof top porch was open and perfect for a summer night.  The experience  is fun, you keep eating bland bad food, but then you look at the people you are around, laugh and say, "there's great ambiance."  So, the saving grace of this place is the location.

If you want good food, go somewhere else
If you want good drinks, go somewhere else
If you want good desserts, go somewhere else
If you want to enjoy the company of friends on a summer evening, try somewhere else, if you can't find anywhere else to go, go to the Loft.

On my 2nd time here visiting from LA; I was again very impressed with this restaurant.

The food is superb. I had their signature Angus steak(cooked perfectly medium rare just as I requested), salad with anchovies, meat cheese board with jam and their famous bloody mary.

The steak was the best I've had so far this year; the quality of the lean, flavorful Angus meat really shined.

I had a nice booth outdoors with heater. This is a large spacious restaurant with all types of comfortable seating.

Service by Jose and Scott was impeccable and 1st class.

Davanti is very consistent with the highest levels of quality food and service.

A top 10 san diego restaurant in my book.

Davanti is in the center of Little Italy on restaurant row.  The interior is spacious showcasing attractive, traditional wood furnishings.

I started out with the Manager recommended Focaccia Di Recco(flat bread filled with soft cheese) with a honeycomb on top to spread on the bread.  In one word:  PHENOMENAL!
One of the best bread starters I ever tasted.

My Antipasto salad was very fresh with delicious meats and cheeses.

The entree, Chitarra Con Scampi(pasta, large prawns and scallops) was superb and perfectly seasoned.

I also has the Manager recommended 2015 Complicated Pinot Noir Sonoma Coast red wine-again a true winner.  The flavor was subtle yet compelling.

The server Dustin was quite frankly one of the best in my experience.  He followed up perfectly on each order and was great at suggestions with extra points for his solid demeanor on a very busy night.

Overall, Davanti LI, San Diego rates in my top ten ever been for Italian fine dining.

Overall a decent dim sum restaurant with tons of good options. Polite efficient staff.
• the stuffed eggplant with shrimp is perfection. Large juicy eggplant marinated in sweet savory sauce with pan fried prawn inside. A 💯 combination
• stuffed crab claw is a wonderful medley of crispy perfectly fried thin breading and juicy crab and shrimp filling
• siew mai is okay, big and juicy but there were some unchewable fat parts, nothing big though
• I wouldn't recommend the scallop rice roll, though the rice roll is thick and mochi like, there's too much rice and too little scallop
• the lotus leaf rice (lor mai kai) is white yummy with decent rice to meat ratio
• the sweet tofu gives you unlimited syrup! The tofu itself is soft and aromatic.

text: Went in Xmas Day 2017 on the fly with a date for lunch and had some fantastic dim sum. The dim sum was of the highest quality and I felt like I was in Chinese Food Heaven - many, many varieties of offerings served by staff members rolling carts or carrying trays laden with goodies. I had some of the shrimp offerings that were crunchy deep fried and soft that were excellent. There was plenty of desert offerings too that my date enjoyed. The dining room is large and was extremely busy, the service was friendly, and fast. I would challenge that China Village is the best Chinese Food in the area for not few miles, and I look forward to going back sometime soon. name: Jonathan Adler
text:
This place is a few years old and is really popular.  I walked in around 5pm and it was already packed with groups of people.  Fortunately, I found a nice table near the bar.

As others have noted, they are not just about Lobster and Beer.  The menu had alot listed including crabcakes, shrimp cocktail, buckets of clams special and a wide array of drinks besides beer!  It was very tough deciding because it all looked so good and I love seafood.

I decided on the lobster/shrimp bowl with edamame, avocado and brown rice, grilled cheese with lobster chunks and lobster tacos!

The bowl was fantastic-large shrimp and hunks of lobster and the herb butter and old bay spices made it a masterpiece.  The ingredients tasted very fresh and healthy.

My bloody mary was very tasty giving me a really nice buzz.

The atmosphere is very enjoyable with basketball, winter olympics and other events on the TV screens.  The crowd was upscale, yet relaxed and casual.

They also have some outdoor seating with heaters.

Service was excellent-my orders brought out rapidly with friendly and professional demeanors.

Lobster and Beer is now my #1 choice for lobster in LA and top 10 for seafood.  I'll have to try the crabcakes and clams next visit!

text:
6/7/13

AT LEAST THE VIEW WAS NICE

The view is amazing. That alone is worth the stop here for a bite; thought it might not be a quick bite.  We ordered breakfast items and while they were good, it took close to an hour to get our food. An omelette. Almost one hour. Ugh.

Normally I would love to spend an hour staring at the water and enjoying a meal, but we were on a road trip, driving up the coast. There are lots of pretty places to see, and we had a certain amount of time to get to some of these spots before they closed. So breakfast was supposed to be quick and easy.

We walked in and the place was packed. A waitress saw us and casually motioned for us to go to the front of the place. I guess the stairs outside took us to the back/side entrance. A hostess ran into us half way and pointed to a table by the window back in the room we came from. Several minutes later we were greeted and finally placed our order. Unfortunately, service wasn't as good as the food. Once it finally arrived, she never checked back with our table until we were just about done eating. The room isn't all the big, so even though I mentioned it was crowded, it wasn't an unmanageable  number of diners demanding her attention.

I really enjoyed my food and even with my coffee and his soda we only spent about $20. For the view, that's awesome. It's sad though because a place like this should leave everyone with a five-star experience. Service is part of that. The food is good and the view is great. And prices are spot-on for the travelers. Glad we stopped but wish it hadn't taken so long to get back on the road.

text: I enjoy the freshness of Panera.  Is it always worth the price to me...not enough to put it in regular rotation. I consider it a nice splurge. I do like the 1/2 and half option, opting for the combo of salad, soup or sandwich based on the weather and my mood. In Tracy, this location has a nice outdoor option (as I am still not too comfortable with indoor dining) where you can enjoy your meal, if you don't hit the drive thru. Service is usually quick, even with a group. The staff is always friendly and knowledgable of the menu. Since it not one of my usual places, I try different things each time. So I tend to ask a few questions (lol). But what I can say is that most of what I have tried is a hit. Nothing stands out as a no-go and I would highly recommend this to all that enjoy soup, salad and sandwich options. Today I enjoyed the Fuji Apple salad with Chicken. So far its my favorite salad. I initially got hooked on this salad  (and Panera as a whole) from work lunches, but have found myself venturing across town to grab a bite on a whim. If you never tried Panera, its great to get in the drive through and not have to get out and go though a mega list of veggies to distract you from the 3 slices of meat on your sandwich you get at that "other" sub place. You get a good serving of meat and veggies. But this is not the place to go with a picky eater, that always wants to alter the menu...or enjoys that 3 slices of meat sub place.

name: Jonathan Adler
text:
When I walked in here I was immediately piqued by the atmosphere and attractive decor of this Restaurant.  I felt like I was going to Italy even though this is in the heart of Santa Monica, well located on the Promenade.

I was greeted by the Manager who is from Italy(very well dressed and professional I might add) and seated at a nice table in the main dining area.

The menu is very extensive with many California farm to table offerings and direct from Italy.

The Server was very helpful with answering my questions and I decided on the Antipasto Misto and their signature Angus beef lasagna.

The Misto consisted of Gorgonzola, Bresaola(beef), Speck, Prosciutto Parma and Fiore Sardo(firm sheep milk cheese fr island of Sardinia).

It was delicious...what else can I say...especially the Gorgonzola on the bread dipped in olive oil.

The Angus meat Lasagna was also superb with just the right texture and flavor.

For a drink I had the Raspberry Lemon drop which had great quality ingredients and tasted it.

I also appreciated the chalkboards in the restaurant explaining the food origins from Italy and California.

So far this year, Locanda is the best Italian fine dining restaurant I have patronized in Santa Monica and places in my top 10 for LA.

They are very worthy of a repeat visit to try their many other classic Italian offerings.

Walked in and quickly greeted and seated. Fast service was provided by our waitress Diana. She was really polite and prompt with service.

Why did we pick Denny's in a low traffic area? Gotta be careful when traveling on Thanksgiving day (holiday). We searched for a breakfast restaurant on Google maps while driving to Oxnard from San Francisco and found Denny's to be a good spot in Kings city to stop for food and take a break from driving. There is a gas station right next to Denny's which is super low key and easy to fill up and take off after eating. The five stars are for clean restrooms.

The food was as expected and good coffee. I picked up the All American Grand Slam, but wanted to order from the Hobbit menu too. Enjoy Denny's for all the creative breakfast options. Sometimes making a decision can be very difficult. I like options and Denny's definitely exceeded my expectations + I learned about the new hobbit movie coming out soon from the special menu.

text:
The Waffle Experience has great food but inconsistent service.  I went with a friend for Saturday brunch at 11:00.  As expected, it was quite busy, but we sat down with an estimated wait of 20 minutes.  It took about 40 minutes for a table to open up and be cleaned, but oddly another 10 before we were led to it.

Two different servers tried to take our drink orders, and an order of a small pineapple juice was charged as a large (they later said they now only serve large juices, but didn't say anything when we were ordering).

My ham and cheeses sandwich was delicious - the mustard and arugula went excellently with the orange marmalade, and the sandwich was the right size to be filling without being excessive.  My friend's country fried steak was solid but not special.

We were asked multiple times if we liked out food, but once it was time to pay the bill ($25 each after a smallish tip) it took a while to get a server's attention.

Overall, I appreciate the good food, but I'd like more consistent service.  Maybe it would be best as a food truck?

name: Amy Palmer
text:
6/15/18

My grandfather's 90th birthday was a couple of weeks ago. Most of my family lives in Southern CA, but my parents and I are up in the Bay Area, so it was a little tricky finding a weekend we could all be down there together. Luckily, the weekend after his big day worked for everybody, and the whole family gathered together at Zov's, since he said he really wanted to eat lamb chops!

He is an incredible man - he still works one day a week and takes care of my grandmother at home - so we wanted to make the dinner just as special as he is. My Aunt and I went early on the night of the dinner and set up decorations in the private room with the help of Nicole and Justin. Another friendly Nicole working behind the bar made the night special too - she was very attentive and friendly.

I have to say service throughout the evening by our server Justin was top 3 of best service I've received ANYWHERE (and this is not my first review). If you were having a large group party, I would recommend Zov's for the venue and Justin for your server. The food was just outstanding. My lamb chops were perfect (a little on the rare side, which I love) and my boyfriend's scallop and filet mignon dinner was excellent too. The sides they served and even salads were great, and the crème brulee bomb for dessert was worth eating, even though everyone was so full! Our glasses stayed filled (both water and wine - and champagne for my toast). And through the entire meal was Justin with his sweet personality, making sure everyone was happy and comfortable, and taking extra good care of my grandmother, who suffers from alzheimers and sometimes the littlest thing can set her off. Thankfully, she was happy all night long.

Dear Zov's - please open a Walnut Creek location! I miss you already.

text:
I was walking down Overland Ave to Culver City and found this super cute & cozy Cafe at Woodbine St. In the small Overland Plaza center with parking.

C & M stands for "Chicken" and "Monkey" which are the nicknames for the Owner's kids.

The interior is very nice and cozy with very well done paintings, mixed media by local artists(nice to promote local talent).  There is ample seating for groups and singles working on the laptops as well as some convenient stool seating along the window.

The food is very healthy and fresh.  I had the Chori Burrito(local & artisan chorizo, scram. eggs, potatoes, farmers' cheese, avocado, jalapeno and chili aioli).

This burrito knocked it out of the park for me aka HOMERUN....I treasured every bite...it was the best I've had in years(compliments to Chef/Owner Klarissa).  I wanted to eat 2 more after that but since it packed alot of food I was stuffed.

For dessert, I had a Blueberry coffee cake which was superb as well.  It was sweet and fruity/crispy without being too heavy and sugary.

Their single origin(Columbia) coffee from local roaster, New Frontier, was great.

The Staff(shout out to Barista Adam for excellent and friendly service) and Owner/Chef Klarissa are outstanding and on point...could not find any negatives and I'm picky about service.

The atmosphere is relaxed, pleasant with chill, low key music how I like it.

C & M ranks as one of my top 10 picks for breakfast and coffee in LA.

Met the girlfriend after work there for dinner.  The place was packed, there was a large group be entertained in a separate location, which was nice for all parties. They even had a old drive-in pole with the two metal speakers that hung from the door windows of the car.  That brought back some memories.  The gal brought us our order, at the time she thought it was our order, but the food was all wrong.  I am pawing threw my burger and this was not my order.  The girlfriend she's putting ketchup on hers and pulling out the pickles, then we get the servers attention, tell her this isn't our order.  She grabs the plates and back to the kitchen with them, a minute later out she goes to another couples table with the same two plates and sets them down as if nothing had happened to their food.  I had my hand all over the burger and had eaten a few fries. The girlfriend did the same, I was kinda blown away that the server would do something like that.  I hope the restaurant reads this review and changes their practice of serving food that customers have handled or touched, to other unsuspecting customers.  Had I not seen it with my own  eyes,  I am not to sure if I'm going back anytime too soon.
The food was pretty good, nothing to spectacular to brag about, I eat the burger wondering who had my burger first and did they wash their hands first?  OH BOY

The location is great across from the Coaster train stop on the corner of PCH 101 and "E" St.

I was taking the Coaster( commuter train from San Diego to LA) and made a pitstop in Encinitas.

Angelo's is just a short walk from the train/bus stop on the 101(cross st "E"). When I walked in I immediately appreciated the warm, professional welcome by the Manager Stathi who also made my pastrami burger with onion rings and fries.  First off, it was made fast and superfresh. I was really impressed with the huge portions and for the money one of the best values in southern cal.

The onion rings are exactly how I like 'em-big fat with flaky breading. The fries are thick, fresh with nice fluffy insides.

The burger with pastrami makes my top ten list for southern cal-great meat, crunchy lettuce and fixin's=very happy camper!

For service, atmosphere and food, Angelo's is by far my favorite in Northern San Diego County.

Just ate here for the first time and was very glad we stopped. We had the Hula Burger with Pepper Jack Cheese and Fries which i asked for extra crispy. The burger to go, is in a foam to go box, and they don't put it all together. They put the lettuce, tomato, onion, and pickle, or whatever fixing you ordered with your burger on the side, which i really like. It keeps the bun from getting too soggy. They do have a little fountain in the seating area that looks as if it is in need of repair, because there was  a puddle of water near the base of it. I highly recommend this place. Will be back for more!

name: Amy Palmer
text:
7/24/14

A few months ago I returned home to find a brown paper bag on my front porch.  Inside was an orange bottle of sauce and a greeting card (with an awesome picture of a cat) from my friend Leyanne A. Curious, I immediately opened the sauce and found some fridge items to eat with it. Holy yum yum sauce!

I quickly went through my bottle, gone in less than a week! I added it to everything. Outstanding flavor and a little kick - perfect on raw veggies! When it was gone, I contacted La Vic by phone and ordered more. My $6 bottle doubled in price (with shipping) but soon arrived and was once again finished too quickly.

A couple months later, after an afternoon in Niles, we drove a little ways further south and spent the day with my sweet Leyanne. After hanging out, we headed to La Vic where I consumed copious amounts of Orange (and Green) Sauce, atop two tacos and some chips.  The crispy veggie taco I ordered wasn't really crispy at all, but the sauce saved it. We also ordered a soda, some tacos for my husband, plus, two bottles of sauce to-go.

It says "It's Vegan" on the bottle, and I believe it is. We've tried to replicate it and can't, but I highly doubt they'd falsely advertise something like this. However, this remains a orange-hot debate topic online on several forums and sites, being questioned because it's richness and creaminess make it hard to believe it's animal free, but either way, it's delicious!

I ordered online at 9pm receipt said food would be ready in 18 mins. Showed up at 9:24 to pickup my order.

The employee (no name badge) told me my order had only just came in and the food wasn't ready. I asked for a refund since it was late and I needed to bring food home to my family. Employee told me I couldn't get a refund. Insisted so a Manger came, And told me I couldn't get a refund. I continued to persist and the manager started telling me I was making things up, basically calling me a liar.

Come to find out there was another order placed under Justin as I walked in and my order was sitting arms reach behind the counter getting cold after the 20 min argument they forced me into.

I was given 2 large drinks as compensation for my time lost. Yeah that may make up for the mix up, but doesn't come close to making up for calling me a liar and making me wait an extra 20 minutes of frustration to get my meal. My meal that was cold when I got home. I live less than 2 minutes away. Literally less than a block. Which means my food got cold while I was being told I was a liar.

Oh and they never even apologized after figuring out they were wrong.

I hate to give such a poor rating since the wings are actually decent, but you don't call me a liar.

The first thing to arrive was a salad I typically will finish off most of my first beer during my salad or a second one for my meal and if time permits enjoy a third one I reminded her about the butter and my drinks that once again is what normally one starts off with they arrive when my steak arrives but just the drinks the special request that I made for butter fell to the wayside which is understandable it's not a common request she offered to bring me fresh bread because by that time the bread that you get right in the beginning of the meal is ice cold, she brings the butter but it's no use because the bread did not arrive a reminder next time she comes around to check on me so I get to enjoy my bread that comes in the beginning of the as I am done with my steak The last time I gave a review that was a tad more negative than this I was called by the management or corporate office and I was asked to call them back I left them a message I never received any communication after that It seems like they begin with good intentions but never follow through I love eating here I love the quality of the food and the service was fantastic until about a year ago I come here for the experience making a steak is not very difficult to an experienced individual but it's the ambience that people enjoy, I do understand that the pandemic has restricted a lot of ability to experience the ambiance that is this restaurant but it seems like a lot of people are becoming complacent and I don't feel I should have to if I'm trying to experience a sense of normality in the small window that our government has offered for restaurants to operate like they used to

Perhaps the best Indian food I've had in a while.

A very good layout of traditional dishes. The tandoori chicken was nicely grilled but not over done; tikka masala was very fresh and all the dishes weren't mushy (which I've encountered frequently at other restaurants).

The interior decor is contemporary with Indian art accents; spacious, without being overly decorated or crowded with tables.

The seafood was unexpectedly good, the name sounds like a short order cafe but its definitely seafood. Their oysters on half shell are cheap, fresh, and good! They have wine and beer but not cocktails or hard liquors. I had one of the specials of the day which was halibut. The waitress was really nice and she said that it was a healthy portion of halibut and she wasn't kidding. I was very full, didnt even eat all my steamed spinach and I like steamed spinach and theres was good. The scallop potatoes that came with my dish were also really good. The halibut was very good. No bones and came with a capers white sauce, so good. My girlfriends smoked salmon pasta was really good, it had a lot of smoked salmon flavor. If you want a traditional slice of pizza (pepperoni, supreme, etc.) You ca absolutely get that here with dough, sauce, cheese, and ingredients that outshine just about everyone else outside of NY. However, if you want to taste some really fantastic combinations of flavors, look no further than their main menu of signature pizzas. Today I had the

Now, they're getting ready for pride parade and a big party tonight which is why I assume my slice was just a bit over done. But typically theyre perfect and will make things right regardless.
Enjoy this wonderful pizza place that puts passion into their food, the sugar levels in the dough are perfect, it's a great tasting dough!

text:
Could you really use another 5 star review? The answer is yes yes and another yes.
Kraken bowl is the wizardry here. Their teriyaki or "Tiki"yaki chicken bowl is amazing as well. The place is constantly busy so you can be assured the food is fresh. The fish is fresh and delicious. The chicken is pure, lean and delicious. I will venture to eat more on my next visit but for now I cannot say enough positive things about the absolutely incredible food here. The rice is sticky and flavorful too! I also had an Acai Berry freeze, delicious. As well as their tea which was a tropical flavor with plenty of full bodied rich brewed taste. How in the world can one place ve so good at everything? Try Tropicali and find out. Not to mention the incredibly fun almost Disney like atmosphere. Being a hardcore Disneyland it was immediately apparent. What's more, on 2 separate occasions during this one visit, guests were making remarks of and comparing to Disneyland.
Then you've got the 2 gents that made right there at the counter, one taking orders and the other serving them up. They both do a great job of making you feel welcome and part of the family. You immediately feel like you just know them and your amongst family, I know that sounded redundant but it worth a double mention. You'll see why when you visit. Do yourself a favor and see why this place has the reputation it does, it delivers, in every way.

text: Not much special here... I assumed being the owners of Okura that the same quality would translate over but it simply doesnt. The salmon is good, but the ahi not so much. Some stringy pieces make it less than satisfying. Also, the rice is fairly bland. Most places if they have decent food like this, not terrible but also not noteworthy, I end up gauging their service... the man who rung me up, the same guy running on their TV screen, seemed somewhat disgruntled. I'm unsure if it was the group ahead of me or what but he just wasn't friendly. I'm used to local places being engaged and caring about their customers. Those are the ones I prefer to patron anyway, this just wasn't the case here. The employees could care less if you come back or not (maybe an assumption but definitely the vibe). The pros, good protein to rice ratio, actually could use a little bit more rice but still, means good portions of protein. Decent quality ingredients, again not noteworthy or extremely fresh like expected but also not bad by any means. Anyway, if you're look to get a par poke fix, feel free to come here, otherwise their are several others nearby that will serve you better tasting, more fresh ingredients with higher quality proteins and actually enjoy doing it. I will absolutely give this place a second chance but the gentlemans attitude was most definitely a turn off.Hope this helps! Enjoy

text: Gosh I'm so confused with this. Reviews are great but wow was this place a miss on most fronts. Everything was fine, even when they placed my "Efrain burger" in front of me I was excited, I mean look at the photo!. That's when things took a turn for the worst. I'll back up and mention that the server never asked how I wanted my burger prepared , which to me personally is typically a great sign. I always answer with "Whatever the chef prefers" anyway. Whelp, the burger was basically burned. Quality of the meat did taste fresh outside of being way way over cooked (yes, 2 ways is justifiable here). The brioche bun was stale, yes stale. I'm not being a princess here but at the price point of 12.95 the bun being stale is a huge let down. Not to mention all typical diner ordered condiments which I'm not really complaining about but okay, we have all tasted these pickles before and absolutely take away from any unique flavors like the cilantro chipotle mayo (which was a determining factor in my ordering of this burger). Nope, the entire burger tasted of stale bun, burnt meat, and the same (insert food vendor name here) pickles. I'm sorry it seems like I'm beating the place up but this was absolutely what happened here. What's more, it took me flagging down someone in order to get an extra side of the cilantro chipotle mayo, the waiter actually sat down my check at that same time. At this point I was halfway through the burger and was never once asked how everything was or if I needed anything, nope, straight to "here's your check now so get out". Obviouslt I'm being dramatic with my words but that is exactly what happened. The fries, looked great but needed to be in the fryer a bit longer. Soggy for the most part. Anyway, what a sad sad place that suffers from mediocrity and a lack of caring. Based on the previous reviews I was under the impression this would be a place with a chef or chefs that cared about what they serve, I was strongly mistaken. If you want a very common place diner meal, by all means eat here. Otherwise there are a plethora of far superior options at even a couple of bucks less. Would like to try their breakfast though.

name: Endless Possibles
text:
So I experienced a little racism while here... that's a first. Also, I was charged for 2 different things that weren't disclosed. I will actually be disputing the charge with my credit card company which I have never done before. The 2 Hispanics in front of me were greeted with smiles, when it was my turn, her demeanor changed. She wasnt necessarily rude but the mood was very different. Now here are the important parts...
She asked, "would you like hard shell, or soft shell for your taco"? I replied, "hard shell". She moved on to ask if I wanted a drink. She rattled my total very quickly, almost intentionally, at least that was the feeling I got.
After looking at my receipt, I was actually charged .59 for the hard shell, nothing was ever mentioned about that. Onw could argue shes being a clever sales person, which I'm all for a good up seller, but no, this is sneaky. I also received a charge saying "convenience fee"! Zero explanation or heads up! I had cash in my pocket and would have paid cash had it been posted or quite honestly mentioned to me, that should be the law actually. So yes, here I am with over a dollar of un stated charges.
Now for the food, it was good. Not wow you need to eat here, but not bad dont go here  it was good. Green salsa was hotter than expected which I actually liked. Their house salsa tastes like many of the other local Mexican places, la casita, Las casuelas, flor de jalisco etc etc. Their roasted salsa was bland, watery like.
Enchilada sauce was good, not sweet like I've had in some places. Not really that rich in flavor either but still good. Cheese was bland, may even be fake cheese (soy)?
Chips are okay, crispy and light. Cant tell if made in house but decent.
Not a lot of shredded beef in the taco, very minimal. Was primarily shell and dressings, lettuce, pico de gallo, cheese.
All in all I wouldnt go here if I were you, nothing stands out in a positive way, and the charges without saying is really terrible. 1 star.

text:
This place has great food. Great happy hour. I used to come here everyday after work and they were nothing but friendly. I changed jobs several months ago so hadn't been back in a while. Came for dinner and sat at the bar. Had a new bartender that I had never had before. He was nice but I must complain about the communication issues.
I attempted to order a classic margarita and my wife wanted a spicy Moscow mule. When trying to order, we pointed out the pictures on the drink menu. He said ok and we got our drinks rather quickly. As we were sitting at the bar we were watching as he made the drinks. (Made sure we weren't getting cheated). He made us a regular Moscow mule using a ginger beer that contained no alcohol. The big issues here are that not only did we not get the drink that we ordered but they are serving a drink on the drink menu that doesn't even contain alcohol. Back to my classic margarita that I ordered. He had talked me into the locos margarita which was fine, I agreed and it was good. The point being on both drinks I had ordered they were not what I had originally wanted. I had asked him to fill up the Moscow mule with a pacifico that it said it was made out of on the menu and all he did was poor in more ginger beer. After not getting what I had requested yet again I asked to see a manager. They eventually brought me someone that could speak English and it was told to him what I was requesting. after the two drinks that we had ordered we did get a free pacifico to make up for the lack of alcohol in our Moscow mule.
They work hard to make their customers happy and I understand that when I don't speak Spanish it becomes very difficult in authentic Mexican restaurants. Overall I really enjoy this place.

text:
This is a pretty unique Taco Bell, purely in the sense that I generally walk into TB and have a consistent experience: fast, friendly service, helpful employees, and a clean environment. Not so much here in Livermore. I had come to Livermore straight from work in Walnut Creek, and the hour-long drive in traffic made me think that I should stop for a bite before the next one-hour stretch in the car as I made my way to Oakley.

There were only 2 people in line ahead of me but they both seemed to analyze the menu like it was their first time ever in a Taco Bell, and the employee didn't speed up the process at all as she had to stop and ask questions about how to customize the first order. I was patient though, but this gave me plenty of time to look around and notice how dirty the dining area was. (The bathroom was pretty clean though, which is important!)

I finally ordered my 3 crunchy taco and drink meal (#8 for $6.22), then waited again to ask an employee if they had unsweetened iced tea behind the counter. Eventually someone asked if I needed something and he kindly filled my cup, but that was after several staff persons walked by without acknowledging me at all.

Food was good - typical TB tacos - so that was satisfying, but I probably would have saved time in the drive thru, and would have avoided seeing the mess they allow in their restaurant.

Very tiny restaurant, about 14-16 customers can sit and eat comfortably without elbowing your neighbor. Also, they have a few tables outside too.

But if you have some one sitting next to you, who is loud and talks nonstop, it will be annoying! Like what we experienced.

Anyway, we dined here about 6 pm during the week and we were seated right away.  We ordered roti, chicken satay, tom yum soup and pad thai.

Everything was delicious and authentic. We've visited Thailand twice so we can speak from experience.

The roti was crunchy and crisp paired with the dipping sauce. The satay was tender and juicy. The tom yup soup was spicy with tons of flavor. The pad thai was sweet, spicy and sour.

The portions and price is reasonable. We would definitely return, great neighborhood find.

text: I would like to rate this place higher, as i have always been a big fan of Marie Calendars but unfortunately I'm afraid this trip was a little disappointing. I was in Modesto to pick up my taxes and took my dad to lunch afterwards. We met a friend there and ordered breakfast instead of lunch. My dad is a big fan of biscuits and gravy and imagine the disappointment when the server said they don't make that. I thought she meant for lunch but she said no they don't make it at all any time of the day. I do believe that is the first place i have been to that has a breakfast menu that does not serve biscuits and gravy. Well my friend ordered breakfast and Dad and i decided to share a vegetable omelet which we would end up leaving most of it on the plate because it was not very good. It was runny and had very little flavor and even adding pepper did not change the fact it was so runny as to just be gross. Ok well it's Marie Calendars most known for her pies, so i asked the server if they had anything sugar free because my dad is diabetic, she said no, that surprised me but ok we would just share a piece, that we when she informed us that we get a piece of pie with our orders that day. Well great i wonder why she didn't mention that when taking our order, or after we were done eating. I wonder if she would have mentioned that at all had we not decided to order a piece. So since we had two meals that meant 2 free pieces of pie. My friend did not want one so she told Dad and me to get whatever kind we wanted. Dad ordered apple which he ate there and i ordered chocolate to go as i had lost appetite over the omelet and i have always loved the pies from Marie Calendars and would enjoy it on the ride home. Imagine my surprise when on the way home i reach for it anticipating a delicious piece of chocolate pie only to discover a piece of coconut pie instead. I guess it's easy to mistake the word coconut and chocolate after all they both start with the letter C. I said that last sentence with sarcasm and believe me i take writing these reviews seriously and that may be the first time i was sarcastic in a review. I don't like to rate anyplace after just one visit so low because i understand that everyone has a bad day and maybe the one time i was there it was a bad day. But i got to me honest nothing about this visit warrants anything more than 2 stars and i feel that is being generous. The server was not that friendly and there was very few customers in the place. We were there on April 15, 2019 so the lack of customers is not a surprise as it is tax day and people are in crunch and mail mode as to make the IRS deadline. Maybe this even explains the poor service and wrong pie and even the unedible omlett, but as i said i take these reviews serious and 2 stars is best i can fairly give for our experience. If you decide to give it a try which to be fair i will again someday and if anything changes i will update my review but if you go i do hope your experience was better than ours.

text:
5/15/17

Before last weekend's flight to Seattle, boyfriend and I stopped here for a fast bite since Southwest had an hour delay and we had time to kill. We had Bloody Mary's and shrimp nachos ($14.71 for the food). The nachos were delicious with plenty of cheese and shrimp baked over crispy tortilla chips. Unfortunately they ran out of salsa at the bar but the service and food was otherwise great.

5/25/14 (3-star)

All I wanted before my one-hour flight to Orange County was a quick bite, so I stopped at Oakland Airport's Andale for a couple of veggie tacos ($10.25) and some chips for the salsa bar.

Darling at the register asked if I wanted them fajita style or ranchera. I asked what the difference was and she said fajita had vegetables and ranchera had sauce. I couldn't picture what crispy tacos full of sauce would look like, so I ordered the fajita-style grilled veggies. (I later looked up ranchera on their online menu and it described that style as tofu sautéed with Serrano salsa - sounds awesome!)

A huge basket of chips arrived ($4.50). I had only wanted enough for one person so I was a little upset that she hadn't told me the plate COMES with chips for the salsa bar. My plate had a lot of chips on it so the big extra basket was just wasted. I wasn't about to pack it up to carry onto the plane. The chips were pretty good I guess but I think an employee should ask if someone means a giant basket full. She did ask me if I wanted the chips and guacamole option when she was ringing me up, and since I had seen this on their menu I guess I thought that by declining that I was declining actually purchasing chips. I wasn't given my receipt after my purchase, and since I wanted to see how much I'd paid for these I had to ask for it when the food was brought out. Twice!

A small Mexican Coke for $3.25 brought my lunch to over $20, after taxes and the airport fee for health care (2%). I'd eat here  - the food wasn't bad - but I'd definitely pay more attention to what I was ordering and paying for next time.

name: Jack Flynn
text:
Unique Food Experience

When I think about great food, I tend to remember my mothers cooking, then I think about restaurants that have wowed me with their explosive flavors and wondrous environments. I have had meals which stopped me cold mid bite to remember that having taste buds is one of the greatest joys of being a human.  Plaj has given me one of these experience.

As a group of four we had appetizers, oysters, soup, salad, entrees, and desserts and all of us found ourselves struck dumb lacking words to describe how we felt at different times throughout the night. A crawdad soup, features the best lobster bisque you could imagine, but light, silken texturally perfect. Croutons, which added the crunch and sour salty bread, then a rich wonderful cognac whipped cream. And, as almost an afterthought, a dill oil.  Why would all this work, I don't know, but it is amazing and made all of us forget that we had even ordered other food.

Every dish is a reminder that there are people in this world, wonderful people, Chefs that care about food and care that it is presented in a form that makes you fall in love all over again. The dishes look like real food, they taste like the memories of childhood and loves lost, they exhibit the wondrous feeling of being a human being and enjoying life.

The staff are wonderful and the represent people that are actually happy to go into work.  They have tasted the dishes, they know the menu, they even know which drinks you might like throughout the night.  They are well trained, but more importantly they treat you as a person and are just as excited to share your excitement at the wonderful meal.

If you are in the City, and find yourself wanting something worth your dollars, stop by.  Have a drink, have some oysters, ask an employee what the best dish is of the day, and then enjoy a ride to food greatness.

text:
Had heard good things about this bbq restaurant so gave it a try.  Although its not bad I was disappointed.  The order taker was nice and informative.  The wait was reasonable and I was offered a water while I waited but not until after I had been seated for a bit and my order was ready shortly after it arrived. Perhaps it should be offered at time of order.  The ribs and chicken were cooked fine but they're served on a pool of liquidy sauce which makes them soggy. The chicken on the combo meal was a thigh/leg and very small.  Potato salad was fine but I doubt its house made.   It comes with house made cornbread which is pretty good but was somewhat flat. The mac and cheese was the worst part.  It was not cheesy at all and the sauce was both watery and grainy.  In other words not cheesy.  It was like they used a powdered cheese mixed in water and it wasn't mixed/heated good enough to blend it in, this I got this grainy taste.  Not good.  I had my order to or otherwise would have returned the mac and cheese.  I would also ask for no sauce but rather have it served on the side.
I had heard how friendly the owner is and how he greets people often remembering their name.  But I never got any such recognition.  Maybe because. well, no I won't go there.

name: Jonathan Adler
text:
Dublin Square is a fun Irish Pub serving authentic Irish grub.

I started out with an Irish Mule(Irish whiskey, ginger and lime) in a copper cup which was excellent.  I also tried out the Irish Smithwick's beer which tasted good but not great like some of the products from the local San Diego breweries.

My starter was smoked salmon boxty(on potato pancake) which was too warm, not very smoky and the pancake was too flat and flavorless.

My entree of Irish Lamb stew was tasty and filling with very large chunks of lamb meat.

So the food I had was decent but if I visit again I would go with a burger, fish and chips or the breakfast perhaps.

The traditional Irish music was nice but would have liked to hear some more contemporary Irish sounds as well.  Also, when I lived in Amsterdam I went to some very cool Irish pubs with the live, authentic Irish bands.  Apparently, Dublin Square offers that but not the night I was there...too bad.

Lyndsay the bartender is the best bartender I have met so far in San Diego.  She didn't mind bringing the food/drinks out to me, gave me some great suggestions and has an awesome energy and helpful attitude...nice job Lyndsay. This does really set the tone for having a fun and pleasant pub/dining experience.

Dublin Square is certainly a good time to be had by all.

6/5/13

TOO MUCH SECURITY

This casino was soooo much nicer than we expected! We picked this over another one that came recommended, even though we were pretty sure the other local one was nearby and much nicer; long story but we mostly wanted to check up the less nice one. So we decided to go with the one that had four pictures on yelp (two of which are gross onion rings). The other casino has TONS of beautiful pictures!! Well, that's because the security here won't allow you to take pictures. Of anything. And they are everywhere!

I asked if I could take a couple of the slots gaming room and one security guy said "no, they want everything (machines) kept secret", which is silly, because some people will go to a certain casino, just to play a specific game. I know that you can't take pictures of tables because you can't do that anywhere, but someone needs to call the marketing department at this casino and telll them to have an employee take some pictures or something. They must lose so much tourist/driving-thru business.

The place was pretty empty for a holiday weekend. It was nice to not have to fight over the machines we wanted, and drink service was attentive (free hot chocolate!) But I think there were more security than players.  It just felt like they were breathing down my neck. And I promise I'm not trying to cheat on the penny slots, just have a good time. It made it hard to have fun when you're being watched constantly from someone so close by.

We would definitely check out the other nearby casino if we were back in town, but this one really surprised us with how nice it was, so don't let the lack of yelp pictures scare you off.  You do have to pay for your beer though - no complimentary drinks while gambling.

I asked if I could take a couple of the slots gaming room and one security guy said "no, they want everything (machines) kept secret", which is silly, because some people will go to a certain casino, just to play a specific game. I know that you can't take pictures of tables because you can't do that anywhere, but someone needs to call the marketing department at this casino and telll them to have an employee take some pictures or something. They must lose so much tourist/driving-thru business.

The place was pretty empty for a holiday weekend. It was nice to not have to fight over the machines we wanted, and drink service was attentive (free hot chocolate!) But I think there were more security than players.  It just felt like they were breathing down my neck. And I promise I'm not trying to cheat on the penny slots, just have a good time. It made it hard to have fun when you're being watched constantly from someone so close by.

We would definitely check out the other nearby casino if we were back in town, but this one really surprised us with how nice it was, so don't let the lack of yelp pictures scare you off.  You do have to pay for your beer though - no complimentary drinks while gambling.

name: Rich Garcia
text: Chez Loma is just off the main drag, I was vacationing in Coronado the first week of the year 2018, I found it walking around exploring late at night, closed, I peered through the windows, and knew I had to try it asap. The restaurant esthetically, is one of the cutest atmospheres I've ever come across. Heavily frequented by the locals, with delicious French cuisine, that incredibly, is reasonably priced, I was anomored there. I went about 4 or 5 times -I enjoyed duck l"arange, a real nice pate, bouillabaisse, and onion soup. I would have liked to see though, a more French focus on the wines they have by the glass, I would have killed for a nice glass of Bordeaux or Bergundy, I felt it a travesty, neither were available BTG, given the fine effort by the kitchen and their high quality food. The wines  BTG were all warm climate, low acidity wines, that were poorly inadequate, but being in a touristy area and having to placate to  touristy palates is probably why, I'd guess. Chez should stick to the concept, offering only French wines BTG, educating and giving guests a more complete experience. Enough ranting about the wine - I opted for beer and made do! The restaurant is supremely cozy, has great service, and I think is one of the best restaurants in the area - don't miss out on Chez Loma and make sure to go out of your way to try them!

name: Jack Flynn
text:
Solid San Jose Upscale BBQ

This is solid food.  Nothing you'd rhapsodically praise, but you will leave feeling satisfied and money well spent. The drinks are wonderful and the service excellent.

Our waitress was attentive, suggested the dishes she actually enjoyed the most, and cared about how much we enjoyed the meal. We sent back one drink for being too medicinal, she took it without a second thought and offered her favorite as a suggestion.

The brisket was tender and well caramelized.  The meatloaf was moist and stuffed with flavor, short rib fell apart with a slight touch from a fork.  The swordfish, tasted like swordfish, nothing amazing, just ok.

The portions were large and the sides were a good accompaniment to the main courses.

Overall, this is a nice place to have a dinner, is it a fun upscale splurge? No.  Its a nice place with great service and a welcoming atmosphere.

8/2/15

This little gem is hidden in the corner of the Kinko's plaza and is worth checking out. It's next door to a laundry-mat and Star Thrift Store. My husband and I ran in the other day for a quick bite. You order at a counter and they bring the food to your table. They have two rooms for dining and lots of seats were full on the Friday afternoon we were there. Also, the phone didn't stop ringing the entire time we were sat and we watched order after order of food being picked up to-go.

We ate chips and salsa while we waited. The salsa they serve with the chips is pretty tasty, but very mild - there is also a salsa bar with 3 other salsas to choose from. Unfortunately, the hot salsa option is so watered down it's hard to get on your chip, and not very hot. The salsa verde was a little bland, and we didn't try the pico de gallo.

I had a ceviche tostada with fish and a shrimp taco. Both were very good! Husband had 3 carne tacos with the meat cooked well done - and they got it right, serving up extra crispy little chunks of beef. Our total was $12 and it was a lot of food.

The place is pretty clean. One big negative is that their salsa is served in Styrofoam. They have Styrofoam containers for some of the food they serve (we saw another table eating their nachos from this). Their drink cups are Styrofoam too. Incredibly environmentally unfriendly. But food was good and so was the service. Also, there was a woman working who was singing along to the music and her voice was awesome. We meant to tell her she should sing louder - customers in the other room should get to enjoy her pretty voice also. It was honestly really fun listening to her while we ate.

Harbor House is a upscale seafood restaurant next to or in Seaport Village. Currently only the upper level is open due to Covid. The views are ok, but not breathtaking. The menu features traditional waterside seafood dishes. Nothing special.

The atmosphere was good. Understandably the tables were spread out so it appeared more empty. Service was ok but not great. The staff couldn’t bother to clean up the fruit Simone dropped on the floor before me.

I ordered a shrimp cocktail for an appetizer. It was standard.

I got the mango margarita. It was the kind of frozen margarita I would expect at a taqueria or nightclub. Definitely not worth the $16 price. The old dry and brown lime wedge was the garnish. For not being busy you would think they could cut a fresh lime slice.

My fish tacos were ok. $20 for 2 fish tacos. A bit overfilled so there is no way to eat them. Again garnished with week old lime slices.

I personally wouldn’t go back here. There are many other seafood places in San Diego, many with better views and better food, that I’d go to.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
6/20/18

We went rafting on the Stanislaus River a couple weekends ago and after several hours of fun and sun, we found ourselves in the small town of Knights Ferry. Everyone was ready for a bite in town before setting up our campsite on nearby Lake Tulloch.

The River's Edge Restaurant surprised us as we walked in. It's very pretty inside and opens up to a great back patio and even a beachfront area on the river. The portions were great; even the kids menu sized plate was huge. We had lots of drinks and tons of drink refills. Receipt said Chandler was our server - she did a great job!

Their house-made Bloody Mary mix was delicious. Strangely, their menu boasts of house-made mustard too, but when we asked for it a bottle of store-bought was brought out with no explanation. That was actually pretty disappointing. My chicken strips were still good though, as were the fries. My boyfriend and his boys all ordered the Reuben, and I enjoyed some of their leftover sandwiches the next day at the lake!

Restrooms were clean and it was nice and cool on the patio in the shade - and crazy hot a few feet away in the sun! We really enjoyed the restful, peaceful atmosphere and good food and service.

name: Jonathan Adler
text:
I was walking down the popular India st. very hungry looking for an Asian lunch and found RakiRaki.

First thing I noticed was the spacious interior, high ceiling and psychedelic wall image of rock icon John Lennon.  So far I'm really liking the vibe here.

The manager was very friendly and informative so I went with the Red Edition ramen chicken with eggs and spices.  The bowl was huge, piping hot and so tasty.

I also went with the Kali salad w Tuna poke which was also gigantic requiring me to save about half for later.

My drink was a strong/sweet premium ozeki nigori cloudy sake-unique flavor and at 14 % alc w a nice effect.

There was a busy crowd of locals, businesspeople and tourists.  Raki is not far from the airport and worth saving your appetite if your flying in and want great asian fusion.

Everything is brand new and looks phenomenal decor wise.  Service was superfast so this would be my #1 choice for asian lunch in the area especially as India st is full of Italian rest obviously aka Little Italy.

Raki appeared very well organized and run and the results are very impressive.

They also do alot of dinner takeout.

text:
After eating sushi for many years I would categorize sushi restaurants into 3 main categories. 1) very high end - $200/person or more, 2) nice $70-200/person, 1) budget <$70. Budget also includes buffets and sushi boat.

Live is a “nice” sushi restaurant. It’s busy most nights so make a reservation. The menu is expansive and features a lot of classics but also some unique items. I really enjoyed the short ribs. They came out hot. They were well flavored and very tender.

My sushi rolls were innovative and well prepared. The fish was very fresh.

Service is good and attentive. They have a couple unfiltered sake options which are my favorite!

I wouldn’t recommend this wine bar to my worst enemy. They were incredibly disorganized and the service was outright bad.

They had multiple tables “reserved”. But as we sat throughout the evening none of these tables were used. The servers need new careers. They were rude, were inconsistent, moody, not knowledgeable, and slow. At no point did they apologize for issues and instead blamed it on us. I’ve worked for years in the service industry.

The kitchen was not able to keep up with food service. The food took anywhere from 10 minutes to 45 minutes to come out of the kitchen. The food was ok, but not great.

When coming to a wine bar I expect a certain elegance, and level of service. The service here was better suited for a fast food restaurant. If the staff is new or not trained, then add better written descriptions of the wines and food.

This little El Pollo Loco establishment is located right next to a big AT&T retail store.  When we got there at around 1pm, the restaurant didn't have any customer there.  Since we were all senior, we should be getting the 10% senior discount.  At the time the server person ringing up our bill, he only gave us 10% discount on one order so we asked him why,  then he told us that they only give discount if we pay for our food individually and not collectively! We were just told of this fact when we were paying for our order. He could have just told us before we were paying our bill so that led me to believe that he purposely misleading us into believing that we can pay collectively and still be able to get the 10% discount for all 4 of us seniors.  Needless to say, we're never going to be in this establishment again.
The food in this restaurant were just so so.  The burrito wrap skin was dry and the ingredients inside were dry also. Others in the party were not  impressed with the food either.   All in all,  we weren't too happy with our food nor our experiences at this establishment.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
6/28/15

My husband and his family are members of a French Club who take a lot of awesome annual trips, including a destination trip to Wine Country Napa. For the last two years Brix has been the destination-of-choice for Les Faneurs' wine trip. We begin the day with hor d'oeuvres and champagne at Domaine Carneros and then complete the event with a fancy lunch in the beautiful garden at the back of Brix.

The staff is nothing but warm and welcoming and gracious in every way. They professionally serve food to our group of 100+ as simultaneously as imaginable. Which leads me to the food! We have a multi-course prix fixe menu beginning with butter lettuce salad, then entrees including both tender grilled salmon and juicy, rare filet mignon (perfectly cooked!). I'm a seafood lover so to no fault of the steak the salmon is always my favorite of the two dishes - it's outstanding! Last to join the party is our dessert (buttercream cupcakes are terrific - the crème brulee is my favorite though!) The wine glasses are kept full through the entire lunch and the servers are really attentive to keeping water glasses full too. And of course, coffee and cream at the end of the meal.

The outdoor seating here has always been set up nicely with beautiful tables in three long rows. They also put umbrellas out and so even though there are lots of spots in the sun, we get plenty of shade for part of the lunch also. It's really nicely done. We are also welcome to walk through their gardens and grapes - and at the back of the property are the railroad tracks where the wine train slowly strolls by from time to time. This is a really lovely place to lunch outdoors.

text:
Besides the racist servers at Buena Park Friday's...this is the second worst experience we've had at this chain. I would actually give it ZERO STARS, but there's NO OPTION for that.
Let's see, we arrived at 5:30pm...walked right up to hostess station and gave our name...was informed wait was about 20 minutes. Ok, no problem.
2 ladies and 1 couple were already waiting on benches.
5:35ish two gentlemen walked in
5:40pm ladies sat at a table
5:45ish couple sat at a table.
5:47 party of 5 walked in.
5:53ish pm two gentlemen sat at a table.
5:55ish pm party of 5 sat at table.

I walked up to hostess, asked if we were next...she stated "a couple of minutes".
She did not even make eye contact...???
2 minutes later...we were called in...ok...no problem...but come on!!!
We were offered a table AT THE BAR!!!
I was there with my 7(SEVEN) year old daughter...REALLY!!! THE BAR!!!
I denied the table...was quickly informed: "the wait will be about 30 MINUTES".
Seriously!!!
There were 5 EMPTY TABLES I pointed to that were very OBVIOUSLY EMPTY and CLEAN!!! But, the wait (because I REFUSED a BAR TABLE with my 7 year old daughter was 30 minutes!!!
I turned around, and started walking away...the second hostess(who kept texting on her cell phone, but FINALLY started to do her job)called us in and immediately walked us to one of the EMPTY TABLES.
At 5:59pm...I took pictures of the EMPTY TABLES...from the far side of the restaurant.
There were ACTUALLY 10 EMPTY TABLES!!
5 with 4 chairs each
and
5 with 2 chairs each
"Ok, ok, RELAX, RELAX I'm here with my (7 year old )daughter. Don't make a BIG DEAL" I kept thinking.
Let it go!
So...we receive ONE REGULAR MENU and ONE ALCOHOL MENU!
WAIT...did I mention my daughter is SEVEN??
As we sat there, I tried WAVING DOWN 3 servers.
FINALLY a hostess who had JUST ARRIVED...(6:10pm) came by. I asked her for a "KID'S MENU".
SHE was REALLY NICE and quickly came back with one. (YEY!! THERE IS HOPE AFTER ALL!!!).
I tried logging into my app account, but it would not allow me.
I RESET my PASSWORD twice.
Shift Manager came by to help..."to make sure I was using the app correctly".
I informed him I knew how to use it...he said: "I'll help you through the process."
So, after trying to make me feel stupid...step by step by step...same thing...it did NOT WORK.
He offered some Chips and Salsa for the hassle.
Btw...Chips and Salsa are ALWAYS FREE if you have a WORKING APP!!
BTW...you can get your REWARDS POINTS by using your phone number on the TABLET that is ON EVERY TABLE.
I was not informed of that while I was trying to log in.

6:30pm our order was taken(FINALLY).

6:49pm our food arrives...YEY!
Wait...I ordered BBQ Ribs and Chicken Parmesan, Baked Potato...
NO NAPKINS...NO CUTLERY!!!
3 minutes go by...I FLAG DOWN the server...
Keep in mind...I'm there with my loving 7 year old daughter..."DON'T MAKE A BIG DEAL OUT OF IT...RELAX, RELAX...BREATHE!".........
Ok...finally...it's time to go.
I ask the server if we pay her or at the front...she says me...and walks away!
Not with the bill...just walks away(and starts talking to the hostess at front door once again).
I flag someone else down, I ask about "Military Discount"...she says: "Yes...I'll let them know".
She comes back with the bill...no "Military Discount"...same price.
Ok...you know what...it's time to go and NEVER GO BACK to FRIDAY'S.
Apparently, it's WAY MORE than a TRAINING ISSUE!!

This review is being provided as a Door Dash Dasher.... Although I have not eaten there personally, I still will say that for a small business, their service is to die for and the food looks and smells amazing.

They're located off Convoy in Kearny Mesa is the Southwest corner side of the shopping center they're located in.

Since I'm usually picking up orders to deliver to my customers, I pay attention to the customer service and quality assurance aspect of how they operate. From the moment you walk in the door, someone will make sure that you are acknowledged and will immediately take care of you. I have never had to wait no longer than 5 minutes for my client's orders and when I scan the dining room area, it always seems that no one is left waiting.

From the front of the house staff to the Kitchen and Management. I give everyone a 5 star rating because it seems as though they've found the right combination of skills and knowledge on how a small business is to operate smoothly. Since I'm not an employee of the company I can't speak on the actual inner workings, but based on what I can tell, they're doing something right. I will be returning as a customer cery soon and will update this review at that time.

Until then, I hope that this review is helpful. I highly recommend this is a great place to eat with a small group of people. Outstanding guys! Keep up the great service!!! Thank you.

text: My husband raved about the hat so he wanted me to try it. We went to the hat today, about 1 in the afternoon. It was packed. There was one booth available with two seats which was a good thing because there were just two of us. We ordered the pastrami sandwiches and the service was excellent we had our sandwiches in about 5 or 6 minutes. The sandwiches were huge, I had ordered mine with mustard and pickles my husband had ordered his without. Both sandwiches came exactly the way we wanted them. The iced tea, I am an iced tea lover, is home-brewed. The sandwiches are not cheap. They are about $10 each so a lunch of two pastrami sandwiches and two drinks was about 27 or $28. I find that half a sandwich was enough for lunch and my husband and I are going to eat the other halves of sandwiches for dinner. I strongly recommend the Hat. I saw a lot of other dishes being ordered good-looking chili hot dogs hamburgers Etc service was very good consistently and all of the tables were packed and continue to be packed.

I have been to the shopping center where yafa hummus is located at many times but I never stopped here to eat. Today after a long week if hard work I decided to stop here. When I saw their 5 star ratings I knew this place is gonna be my new favorite place to have lunch. Their many is simple and easy to read and order.

I ordered their back home style wrap which has chicken shawarm as it's meat. The wrap is then cut into bite pieces and is served with a sauce. The bites are a but spicy but they will ask how spicy you want it to be. Food is fresh and very flavorful. You can pretty much taste every ingredient that has been used to make the wrap.

I also ordered some baklava which was also fresh and delicious.

As for service, it was just as great as their food. Friendly people with smiling faces.

All in all I highly recommend this place whether you're in a mood for wrap or a bowl or just want some falafel.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
6/9/15

After a long morning of intense physical labor, my husband and I were more than ready for a big midday meal. We joined two other couples at the Chevy's in Union City near Hayward. Since the Concord Chevy's closed it doors years ago, I've only been able to feast on my mom's leftovers from time to time. But here we were again, with baskets of fresh, crispy chips in front of us and delicious salsa cups in front of them.

Casey and I shared the combination fajita platter with a rib addition on top. The sizzling plate comes with four pork ribs, and fajita style chicken, steak, pork, and shrimp. Also included is pico de gallo, sour cream, guacamole, corn, butter, lettuce, beans (your style), rice, and soft tortillas. I asked for a side of limes and received some lemons - that was fine. The service overall was really good: fast and friendly.

I didn't have to pay for the meal and didn't even look at a menu. Just sat down and went to town. The food was killer and we received enough to feed two very hungry adults, with nothing leftover but a little rice and tortillas. I left here feeling a little sad and  lot full; I miss our local (Concord) Chevy's.

1/3/15

My boss and his wife were taking my husband and me to a Sharks game, so we treated them to dinner before the event. We ate at the Farmers Union by their recommendation.

The place was packed - it was right before game time - but we were seated right away at a comfortable booth for four. I had the fish & chips and my husband had a Union burger with bacon added.  My boss and his wife also had an order of fish & chips and a rotisserie chicken.  All of the food was very good - I really enjoyed my dinner!

The ladies bathroom was clean; the men's bathroom however (according to Casey) had a man bleeding all over the place - my husband walked in on this weird scene and someone else called for help. Pretty sure when people say "you should've seen the other guy", the 'other guy' looks something like this guy did.

The atmosphere was lively and fun, and service was great - I'm sure they keep up with the pace of customers who are trying to get to the Shark's games.  We paid the $88 tab and then enjoyed a wonderful game with the Sharks winning in overtime! Go Sharks!

IT TAKES MORE THAN BEING FAMOUS FOR A MOVIE TO IMPRESS ME

I wish I had taken better notes on our office experience at Bridges for our holiday party back in December. It's probably good for Bridges that I didn't because there were several other negatives that would have probably earned a two-star. Three stars it is though.

Our holiday party rotates restaurants every year. We only do one out-of-office lunch a year. We do get lots of in-office lunches, but nothing super fancy.

Our $800+ lunch at Bridges was pleasant but I doubt any person at our tables would recommend this restaurant for a large group.  The set up was weird. We were at two tables next to one another with 8 or fewer people at each. However, we had ONE server. One guy that took the orders and brought the coffee and poured the wine.  It was a very disorganized event. Some people at the table hadn't even received a wine glass as wine was already being poured. Most people wouldn't even notice this or find it a big deal, and it's not really, but I would demand a higher level of professionalism if I were the management. Fine dining means training employees to pay attention to details.

The food was good. We ordered a bunch of appetizers but our server did not do a great job making sure enough orders were placed that each person would get to try each app, so then a second round of apps were ordered so that those left out could try a bite. The croquettes were okay and the quesadilla was very good. I can't remember what else we ordered. I'm pretty sure fries were involved. Yumm.

I ordered the seafood ciopinno for lunch as did one of the attorneys. We both liked it but both had to ask for a spoon to help us eat it. This should come with the meal.  I noticed no pepper or fresh parmesan cheese was offered to anyone at the table. That's always a nice option and we had several people with salads.

As dessert was being finished, coffee was brought. It seems like it'd be more efficient to pour the cups at the table rather than slowly walk with full cups across the restaurant.

Overall it was A-OK but the mediocre group experience won't have me rushing to return for date night anytime soon.

A girl's getaway to napa wouldn't be complete without brunch, so after massages on Saturday morning we stopped in to grace's table at the recommendation of our masseuse. We didn't order any drinks because they don't serve hard alcohol and so vodka-made bloody marys weren't on the menu but we all ordered breakfast and lunch meals and I am so happy with the Kobe Burger and fries I chose. I think it was $13 and the burger was a good size (for me) with plenty of parmesan fries (had a few left to share). I ordered it rare and they did a great job undercooking for me.
