name: Alan Harnett
text:
Food - 1 star
Atmosphere - 4 star
Beer selection - 4 star
Service - 3 star

I came to Giordano Bros looking for a quick and inexpensive dinner. The Pittsburgh style sandwich was just ok. I got the Coppa. Overall it was a carb overload and was bland. The sandwiches come on thick dry white bread, very small portion of meet, cheese, lots of cold fries, and coleslaw. The meat on the sandwich was amazing!

I’m all for authentic food, but perhaps they should offer sandwiches different ways (deli style, Pittsburgh style, etc.).

I also had the buffalo wings. Very saucy and they come with a side of carrots and celery. Wings were average, celery/carrots were fresh.

Atmosphere was lively. They have a large bar, shuffle board table, and a few tv’s. The beer and cocktail list was impressive.

I’ll come back but I’ll skip their signature sandwich.

name: Jonathan Adler
text:
LBP is in the heart of the exciting LA LIVE Complex and across from the Staples Center(LA Lakers home arena).

I like their ordering system-circle what I want on a preprinted card because it avoids miscommunication and saves me time.

My pizza and salad were ready in under 15 minutes and were both excellent.

The pizza bread/crust was soft, crispy and chewy how I like it.

My custom order was really tasty. My salad with large pieces of fresh, juicy chicken breast was also great.

I read over the older reviews and had a much better experience than the negative reviews.

Apparently, they made major improvements.

I highly recommend this restaurant for great pizza, salad at low prices(considering it's in a major tourist venue I give it points for reasonable prices).

I think this restaurant is ideal for families and groups on a budget while still getting high quality food.

text: I've been going to Tamazula Baja Grill for a couple of months now.  It's a very nice Mexican Restaurant, and very traditional.  The food on the menu is exactly what you would expect in a Southern California Mexican Restaurant.  It's good food, and it always comes hot.  The restaurant is a medium priced place, and it is mostly casual when I go (lunch time and afternoons).  I don't know what the dress would be in the evening, but I'm guessing it would be a nice-casual (just nothing sloppy).  The place has about 15 to 20 tables and can probably seat 60 or more people.  Every time I go there it's reasonably busy.  It's a very cheerful environment, and I often see people there that I know (in the Corona, CA area).  I rate the restaurant about 4 stars overall.  There is nothing that I can say negative about the Tamazula Baja Grill - it's a good place!

name: Amy Palmer
text:
1/19/15

Saturday afternoon my husband and I drove out to the City for my friend Emily's birthday party at SFAC. Casey used to live nearby, but neither of us had been here before.

The place was a lot of fun! Lots of TVs all around (great for sports - we watched part of the Warrior's winning game). The bar had a lot of seats around it which was where our group was primarily focused, but there is a lot of room away from the bar as well, including a spot in the back where they'll even lower bleacher-style seating for parties.

I was starving when we arrived so I ordered a menu before getting a drink. The girl next to me was eating nachos and I ordered the same thing ($11, you can add chicken for $4 but it's a lot of food without that). My husband and I really enjoyed the crispy bean and cheese covered chips. I loved all the jalapenos throughout the cheesy goodness, but a spicy slice occasionally hid in the guacamole or under sour cream, so my husband had to inspect his chips more closely. Lots of olives too - and I was treated to a homemade hot sauce/salsa on the side. Super hot! Super delicious.

I had a Bloody Mary and I was pleased that my "sort of spicy" request was spot on. Erin made the perfect sort-of-spicy drink and even resalted my rim without me asking after seeing most of the salt had kind of rinsed off onto the side of the glass. Seriously wonderful bartender. And she kept coming over to check on us, making sure we had enough glasses of water - and of course, quite a few Fireball shots. Hours later we left the bar with a $70 tab that I thought was really fair.

One thing that I've probably never mentioned in a review but is worth mentioning here: the napkins! The soft, absorbent napkins were the best! No, I'm not kidding, they really stood out in my memory. They were perfect for keeping ourselves clean while eating our finger food.

name: Castle Guy
text:
Pricey? Well, yes. But this establishment fills a void in a New Age way. Gnocchi with goulash??? Sounds odd, but Bohemian Dumplings and such that usually seems to accompany goulash here in the New World are really not that different from gnocchi.

There are Italian overtones but I urge you to stick with the Hungarian and Czech.

This is the type of place that made the City such a wonderful place to dine: a Mom-and-Pop atmosphere with unabashed ethnic focus. While not much is that way anymore, places like this deserve your patronage. And, the people that work here are as nice as the Kucera family that long ruled the Czech roost on Lombard.

name: Mihir Meghani
text: Michelin Chef Srijith continues his creative food designs with the opening of Ettan. He joins businesswoman Ayesha in a unique, aesthetically designed restaurant with a creative, exciting, and vegetarian & vegan-friendly menu. Bringing the quality & service of Taj Campton Place in San Francisco, this restaurant is a welcome addition to Silicon Valley where traditional Indian dining abounds, but Cal-Indian fusion food with ambiance & great service is limited. Service at Ettan is really good & professional. Be sure to walk around the decorations spanning the 2nd floor, ground floor, and the basement (where the restrooms are) as it is like a museum itself. They have an incredible list of alcoholic concoctions, mocktails & desserts as well. My wife & I dined here twice already. The Tender Jack Vada, Sesame Leaf, Cauliflower Black Pepper, Wild Mushroom One Pot, & Dal Makhani are incredibly good. We also liked Mung Bean Paneer, Malabar Paratha, Asparagus Vada & Rice. The Sweet Bitter Virgin mocktail is great. Try the Kin Euphorics & Lemongrass Lemon Iced Tea as well. The kulchas & "Monkey" Naan were great but have eggs - they are working on a non-egg formulation. text:
If I could give zero stars I probably would. It started strong with potato skins, drinks and corn bread muffins. It went downhill from there. Let's start with the fact that there restaurant was empty other than the four of us. The meat platter and sides that two of us were sharing came out first. It was at least 10 minutes before the next meal came out. What was ordered was the Philly cheese steak. What was served was a tri tip sandwich. When we pointed out that the "Philly" was delivered with no cheese she took it back. Fast forward another ten minutes and the correct sandwich came out. Mind you I'm still waiting for my salad and the guys' meat is now cold since they were waiting for us to start eating. I asked for my salad and she replied as if she had no clue that I didn't have my meal. Everyone else started to eat as I continued to wait for my salad.

The Food:

Potato salad was bland and tasteless.

Mac 'n Cheese was fair at best.

Sausage was actually quite delicious which was refreshing.

Ribs and tri tip were average.

Philly was good.

Salad would have been better if there lettuce was cold and cut into smaller pieces. I think they just tore it from the head and put it into the bowl.

As we finished up I noticed two Arlo cameras positioned just above our table. That was unnerving as it was clearly recording and was picking up our conversation the entire time as well. It seemed unnecessary.

Finishing our meal we saw a cockroach crawling up the wall next to our table. There was never any apology for the terrible service or for the fact that our meals were eaten in the separate sessions. We were charged fill price for everything, and in fact we were overcharged.

This spot used to be fantastic but clearly there's a reason it was literally empty on a Thursday night. If you're going here, stick with the alcohol and potato skins to avoid severe disappointment.

On my 2nd visit I had the popular Brunch on Sunday.  It is 9 courses including rioja short ribs, panseared salmon, eggs benedict, cheese empanada etc.

All the Tapas dishes were delicious and even more fun and tasty than my last time there.

Their housemade Habanero hot sauce is outstanding; they should sell it at the counter.

Service by Roberto who was my server last visit was again outstanding, totally professional and on point.

I sat outside enjoying the sun and view.

Another fun time with delicious food...I'll have to also check out their musical shows next visit.

I had not had Tapas in several months and Sevilla Restaurant did the job wonderfully in satisfying my Tapas craving.  I was immediately impressed by the very attractive interior of the restaurant with a large bull sculpture near the ceiling, colorful banners and logos giving the place a very exciting, historic ambience...I kind of felt like I was in Spain for awhile.

I was in luck that they were offering their "Bites" Menu featuring a nice variety of Tapas selections for a very reasonable price of $15.50 for 5 choices then $2.75  for each additional so I opted for 9 selections.

My favorites of the 9 were the Tuna Tartare Tower(Avocado, mango, orange-tarragon);  Grilled Spanish sausages(with caramelized onions) and the Manchego Cheese & Chorizo Empanada.

text: This was our first time visiting this place. We got to the theater 20 minutes early like they recommend, but there were only front row seats available. I like sitting in the front front row at other theaters, but damn these seats were way to close. No biggy, the kids were having fun. The food is absolutely disgusting. Ordered the chicken fingers and shrimp, nachos, and pretzel bites. The chicken was dry and not edible, the few tiny shrimp that came in the combo were hard and chewy. The batter tasted the same on both the chicken and shrimp. It was gross, and left a funny taste in my mouth. The nachos were tasteless. It's dark in theater and my old lady did the order. I thought the meat in the nachos was ground beef, but she later informed me it was supposed to be chicken. It had no flavor so I have no idea what I just ate. Lol, then the pretzel bites tasted stale and were dripping in oil. So much so that the cheese you dip them in wouldn't stay on the pretzel. It would just slide off. The food was stone cold as if it sat on the counter waiting to go out. Makes sense since it took a really long time to get our food. I'm positive everything we ate tonight was pre made and most likely microwaved more than once. It for sure wasn't fresh. The staff seemed nice enough, except for the server who collected money. They wanted to swipe a credit card, I told them I'd be paying cash. He seemed like he didn't trust me, and when we got the bill he literally told me I had two minutes before he'd be back for the cash. I really wanted to like this place, but it's just a horribly executed good idea. I might try it again, but probably not. Oh, lol. The fries that came with the chicken and shrimp combo were actually pretty good. I forgot to mention this because there was like maybe 5 on the plate. I think I got more chicken strips than fries. Lol

I saw some amazing pictures online, but sadly that was not the same experience I had. When I went in during the early afternoon on a Friday they had 4 random loafs of bread on display. One pastry case was empty, another looked like it was a closeout sale, and the last one with the baked items looked picked over.

Gone is the day when you have to go to a bakery before 9am to get the best items. They should be able to offer a selection of cakes, pastries, and baked items. Some items only last a day, but many others last a couple days. This I learned from experience as a pasty chef. This gives your customer the same great experience all day. At least 4 people came in and left during my visit due to a lack of basics.

The eclair I had was delicious. The vanilla flan was not good. It was bland, chewy, and had no flavor.

Sadly I think I’ve had a better experience and better quality at the Safeway bakery.

A friend in my office gave me a $25 gift certificate to the BH Grill. I surprised my husband by suggesting this place when he asked what I wanted to do for lunch. (Usually I sorta shrug and mumble something about tacos). We drove downtown, paid for metered parking inside the garage on Locust (that's new), then walked across the street to the grill.

I ordered the Greek Salad ($7.99) with extra olives (which I think they forgot) and Casey ordered the Bacon/Cheddar sandwich ($9.99). Two sodas for $3.98 and we were only a dollar under the gift card's amount. Perfect!

Our buzzer rang really fast - there isn't much on the sandwich so I guess it's pretty easy to put together. I started my salad wondering if it had been dressed. I mixed it around some and found more dressing at the bottom. When I actually reached the bottom it was really, really dressed. Aside from that, it was pretty good. The pita sticks it comes with weren't really crunchy, more like oily fried bread, but I ate them too.

My husband's sandwich was supposed to have a ranch sauce on it, which he even confirmed when he picked it up, but it was very mustardy tasting (which I love, and he hates). Beef, cheese, and bacon are on the bread, and that's it. The cheese is only on the top so he was disappointed it wasn't on every bite (or at least a few more bites than it was). Near the end of his sandwich he gave up on the meat (there were some oddly chewy pieces) and I finished part of it. When I returned to work, a co-worker asked if something smelled like horseradish. My goodness, it must've been me! My toothbrush and I fixed that problem, but the problem of a just-average $10 sandwich remains. Glad it was a gift certificate. I don't think I would have rated so highly had we paid ($23.83) for lunch.

text:
9/9/18 - FIVE STAR

The clam chowder bread bowl was my favorite SF treat.... until today!!! A re-visit to Boudin's by Fisherman's Wharf taught me that thinly sliced sourdough bread crisps smothered in their spinach-artichoke-and-huge-chunks-of-fresh-crab-dip is better than ANYTHING else I've eaten in the City. Ever!!! Don't get me wrong: my boyfriend and I shared an amazing clam chowder bowl here before our real lunch, then ate off each other's plates of Fish and Chips (his lunch - so freaking tender and perfectly fried with thin fries on the side) and a Crab Sandwich (my lunch - which I'd highly recommend - and I liked it even better than Fenton's in Oakland, which until today was my fave crab sand.) But the starter our table shared blew me away! Best appetizer ever. We honestly sat there planning our next trip here for more drinks and spinach dip.

Service was great from checking in at the reservation desk to picking up our bill at the end. The assistant manager Kelly introduced herself which was awesome, and her staff was just as insanely attentive to detail as she was, even by bringing out a little extra salt to me for my Bloody Mary. Our server Evelyn checked in on us just the right amount. Not too much and never left us hanging trying to get someone's attention. With great service came great food! My bff's grilled trout lunch should also be mentioned, but maybe not before our perfectly spiced Bloody Mary's, (and I can't leave out the bread they brought to our table). Everything was perfect. The view from upstairs is great, so there's that, IF you want to look up from your plate of delicious food!

I think whether you're a tourist or a kinda-local (we're from East Bay), Boudin's is one of those family-owned businesses that cares about their customer experience, and is seriously on-point. If you're not in the mood to battle a seagull or a panhandler for someplace to sit and eat a bread bowl outdoors, stop in here and eat at a luxe table with a killer view and spoil yourself with some of the best food and drinks you can find around this part of the Bay.

Absolutely stoked to be eating indoors again with food servers and drink refills and friendly, smiling faces. Okay... So it's hard to tell if everyone's smiling through masks, but it was definitely friendly service from the moment we walked in for a quick bite and were greeted by the hostess, Peyton. She told us we could wait outside until a table was ready, and texted my phone with that alert moments later.

Lots of tables removed inside but Ashanti and Alex did a great job attending to the ones full of people. In addition to the paper menus they are required to have, there are electronic ones so you can add on crispy, coconut shrimp, get a drink refill, or splurge on dessert, without having to order through your server. We even paid using this machine at the end of our lunch, after asking to be shown how to use it. Simple!

Food was as delicious as ever. Crisp, fresh salads.. Tortilla soup with rich flavors and gooey cheese on top, their hot, buttery bread... And outstanding service! Even the manager Olin checked in on us. He was so positive about the restaurant's changes and their staff's adaptations. I cannot imagine the amount of work it is taking businesses to stay compliant with all the new rules!!  Happy we stopped in to support the team here. And glad they could see our smiles as we left!

We wanted to have breakfast at a restaurant we've never visited. So we chose Southern Kitchen and it was awesome neighborhood find!

After ordering, we received our order within 15 mins. The portions are huge!!  It looked more than 3 eggs to make the omelette. We ordered the Monterey and Supreme omelette. Both were delicious!😋 The country potatoes were cooked perfectly, tender inside and crunchy on the outside.

The table service was quick and the staff were friendly and sociable.

Parking is in the rear of the restaurant and there's only 2 disabled parking in front. We're definitely be back!

We ordered the #2 original double charburger with cheese and the Teriyaki charburger. The #2 meal included a drink and fries and the total price was about $22.

The #2 burger was on the salty side but it was so tasty and cheesy. The juice from the patty was everywhere! It was so messy, just the way I like it!  I enjoyed the Teriyaki too,  the sweetness of the pineapple and the saltiness of the soy sauce in the Teriyaki sauce complimented each other.

The fries was crisp and lightly salted. They must have double fried it. I'll definitely return but I'll request to lay off the salt.

What I actually received was one sausage patty and half a slice of ham (both cut in half and passed off as two servings of meat). So in actuality you get 2 strips of bacon, 2 halves of a sausage patty and 2 quarters of a slice of ham. You know your fractions...you can figure it out. And though service can be a little slow, the orders come out quickly and they do check on you regularly once you are seated. Bottom line is that the food is good. It's worth a visit and I will be back. Now that I know what to expect.

The pros: great looking truck- the look and feel and people are nice and friendly, the price is good for an acai bowl (people on yelp complaining about price must not know the industry standard.)

The Cons: the only con was the taste (which is obviously a big con) the toppings were great, but the actual smoothie was bland and icy tasting, not fruity tasting like it should be.

I love smoothie bowls and this was not the best one, I would not return here because it just didn't hit the spot like a good smoothie bowl should. I am still left craving a good smoothie bowl for when I am in San Francisco. *Sigh*

name: Alan Harnett
text:
Amazing experience! Trestle is located in the 555 California building. You enter through the building lobby. The restaurant is small, but it’s well spaced out due to covid. They have the doors open to allow for a cross breeze. The menu features a prix fixe menu with 3 courses for $39. There is an optional pasta supplement for $12. The portions are average. With 3 courses you’ll be pretty full, and with 4 it will be a full meal.

The food itself is focused on in season ingredients, simple presentation, and with an upscale vibe. Every dish had a little flair to it which made it unique. I’m so glad I got the pasta. The mushroom risotto was perfectly cooked and has a depth of flavor. It was evident the culinary staff were well trained.

The staff is friendly and knowledgeable. The pride flag at the entrance was a nice touch and made me feel welcome.

A must try are the cocktails! They have some amazing combination of flavors, cool names, and are well presented.

You can lark on the street. Garage parking with security is available for $12 after 5pm in the building. No validation required.

name: Jonathan Adler
text:
I was at their oceanside property which was great and I read good things about the original location in Old Town so I went last night.

First, I read some reviews that it's small and cramped but it's actually good sized with comfy seating, bar and outside patio. There is a cool acquarium in the middle to gaze at during the short waits for food.

I was hungry so I had their Mongolian Stir Fry(great sirloin meat with honey sriracha sauce and rice)-it was really delicious and filling.

My Nigiri were Saba(mackerel), Black Cod and Hamachi(yellowtail).

The Cod is phenomenal and a real standout. I can't wait to have it again.

For dessert, I had a Sapporo Beer and vanilla bean ice cream(3 scoops, bigger than avg.)which were also great.

Service was excellent by Chelsea. Everything came out with short waits.

They have a large selection of sushi, sashimi, cocktails, sake, regular entrees....wow!

Harney sushi, in my opinion, exceeds its reputation as one of the best of its kind in San Diego.

I rank it top ten best Japanese in Southern California.

Also, the large 3 course meal with beer was just over $50 which is a great value for a sushi restaurant of the best calibre.

Don't t bother ordering the boneless buffalo wings, it looked nothing like the picture on the menu! It was just a few small pieces of  chicken lathered with their sauce.

The side choices were how many different ways to serve potatoes...baked, mashed, and fried.

The only item we enjoyed was the thai shrimp  salad. It was spicy and was full of flavor.

However, we will never return!

UPDATE: We've found the truck to lunch there is to beat the late lunch rush.

Dinner however is still a problem. The wait went from 10 minutes at 5:45pm to 70 minutes at 6:15pm. We went for my hubby's birthday and it was a joke.

First you start your experience by hearing the heavy wood doors slam bare metal every minute or so because they don't have any impact buffer on the outer doors.

Dinner couple have been ok despite it being packed and horrifically loud, that just seems to be a problem with the area. There were not enough waiters. Our daughter was starving so I put her order in via the ziosk like we do at lunch, along with sauce for the breadsticks. We told or waitress this with our drink order. She came back for our food order with our drinks. We ordered two entrees and appetizer and reminded her of the ziosk order, and asked her to bring it out as soon as it was ready. When our salad and soup came out she informed us that the ziosk at our table was for a different table. She took our daughters order again. All the entrees came out together and we hasn't even gotten our soup and salad done and had not gotten our appetizer. We asked for boxes and then she brought out our appetizer. We took one bite of the appetizer, both of us could tell it was off, so we sent it back. We finally got refills after she boxed the food. She forgot straws until after bringing back the check. This was the worst part. We waited almost an hour to be seated. We felt rushed through our food it took 30 minutes for all that food to be put on our table, which made it way too crowded to enjoy. But then it took an HOUR to get a single refill and our check taken care of. And half the time it wasn't even or waitress dropping and picking stuff up since she had tables all over the restaurant.

My husband and I have been sick since eating the appetizer too boot.

-------
We were seated with only two place settings even though they clearly had three menus. They brought my child an adult glass, and when we asked for it to be fixed it was not done in a timely manner, the server brought food for all four of our neighboring tables. The server was polite but obviously stretched way too thin, I felt really bad for her. She was having trouble keeping track of orders and getting things from the kitchen and the bar.

name: Mark Ames
text:
It's been 5 years or so since I visited a Popeye's. Today I was reminded why it's been so long.
To begin with, the drive-thru was probably the slowest I've ever been in. This may have something to do with the fact that they ran out of their popular chicken sandwiches and customers were frustrated and having to make another choice, or it could be because they require you to sign the receipt if you use a debit card. I chose the seven piece spicy chicken tender combo, which was not spicy and it was barely chicken. These tenders are cut about a half an inch thick and are breaded to make them appear three times larger than they really are. The result is barely any chicken and tons of breading. The fillets actually reminded me of squid (which I like) in their shape and consistency, but not chicken. As a side I picked coleslaw, which I knew would be a good window into quality.
The coleslaw was just as bad as the chicken if not worse. It had a chemical taste and smell to it which I couldn't put my finger on (is it the cabbage? Is it the sauce?), and I couldn't eat any more than three bites.
Needless to say I doubt I'll be back in five years to try it again. There's a reason why Popeyes isn't more successful. In this trip I found 4 reasons. The good news for them is the only way to go from here is up; it's doubtful they could be much worse. I really was hoping that this visit would have turned out differently, but sadly it didn't.

text: Well for starters, my date and I ordered a drink, it had to have been 80% ice. We lucked out and got the server being trained.  Very nice young lady, just a bit to chatty for my liking.  Ordered the appetizer sampler.  That was delicious.  We order our dinners and both of us ordered our meat to be cooked Medium Well. Well after I'd say 20 plus minutes we had gotten our salads, the appetizers were cold and just about finished with my second drink and no food.  Here starts the trouble. Right!  Our dinners are taking longer because of our cooking selection. 5 more minutes .  Well after the 3 or 4 5 more minutes ago, we still don't  have our dinners.  The Manager  comes to the table to see if he can find out what's the hold up with our orders. Finally here comes our dinners, with medium Rare meat.  Taking credit for delivering our dinners, like Moses parting the Red Sea, all proud of himself.  I took one look at the meat and when it's RED on the outside, it's RED IN THE INSIDE.  Discusted I started to complain, but decided this is not how I want my date to see me.  I told the server, this is not how I had asked for my meat to be cooked, but I would live with it.  30 minutes and still I get a rare steak.  Well the bill was insanely crazy. The drinks were ridiculously expensive. The dinner was marginal at best, and not getting a steak that was not even enjoyable, made the bill of $191 even more difficult to choke down.  I would describe that dinner as bad as a first date that goes totally bad.  I know I won't be recommending that restaurant, but I will be warning others about the experience I had.  My date developed a headache and wanted to go home.  Ruined dinner and broken heart.

First of all, I was able to choose a table and be seated immediately. Then the service was outstanding. My server Lynn A., was very attentive, even though she was rather busy. She made me feel as though I was her only customer. And even other servers would check on you periodically as they dashed from table to table.
My breakfast came out in a reasonable amount of time, piping hot and cooked to perfection. And even though a slight morning chill was still in the air, my meal didn't cool any faster than expected.
Finally, I noticed as I sat down and observed as other diners got up, that everything was throughly sanitized before and after each customer. If every restaurant was this efficient maybe this "new normal" won't have to last forever.

text:
This place is okay. If you need a quick Thai fix while shopping on El Paseo, here you go. Otherwise, very generic, bland flavors. They have an old reputation that continued to fade each year.
Pad Thai: has chicken and shrimp. The shrimp is clean tasting, not fresh tasting but clean and decent. The chicken had a bit of an odd flavor today... the rest of the ingredients are okay. I'm sorry but I compare it against Le Basil which is just a skip car ride away (down at the end and across the street) which has night and day ultra dramatically better food. Anyway, I dont mean to beat this place up but it truly is simply okay, nothing stands out to compete out there.
Spicy tofu: its okay honestly. Make sure you order it "extra crispy". Trust me. Again, bland on flavors but it has a kick and is still tasty. The bamboo shoots over power the entire dish, I wish it had more mushrooms and a little more flavorful sauce.
The shining star here is the thai smile fried rice, its good! When it's bad, it's just bad. Weird flavor, not sure if due to dirty or old oil or what but anyway you get it.
Again, if its convient and you MUST HAVE Thai, stop in and maybe order using this review to tailor your experience. Otherwise, the best Thai is a few blocks away, Le Basil.

The food was really good and my boyfriend and I waited for our to-go order at the cute bar next door, which was fun. But, a little disappointed in a forgotten item. We were picking up burritos for his boys, and some tacos for us, a couple sodas too, and at the register the cashier suggested guacamole and chips which we decided to buy, and all together our bill came to $64.03. How disappointed were we when we arrived back at the hotel room to find they had forgotten the guacamole! After they suggested it!

I called and they said I could come back in and get some, but it was too late that night to go back out, we were at Disneyland until after they closed the next day, and the following day was Labor Day and we headed home that morning.

My daughter and yours truly wanted to try out a new place for lunch. So we decided on this fine place.

There's plenty of parking and lots of space inside. There's booth seating and two standard tables. If you like to eat up close and personal. You can sit down in front of the front counter.

It wasn't too busy inside and we picked out where we wanted to sit . As I was walking to my table, I saw a co-worker of mine. He recommended the Hunan chicken. I'll probably get that on my next visit.

My daughter picked out a lunch combination. Almond chicken with rice and veggies. I picked out veggies with chicken and sweet and sour pork. Oh they both came with chow mein. I'm not the biggest fan of chow mein. But I really enjoyed it here.

Just a note breakfast, lunch and dinner is served all day.

The food was very tasty and delicious. The portions are pretty big and they don't skimp out here. The chicken is pretty bomb, I like that they are some strips and not diced up like little cubes.

The service was pretty good and we had a great time here today. We'll be coming back pretty soon in the near future.

name: Mihir Meghani
text:
This is not your typical Indian restaurant. The menu is very creative, so you have spinoffs on typical Indian dishes, often with non traditional ingredients. There are also some typical Indian menu items that frequent diners to Indian restaurants would know about. The portions are appropriate, so you could easily be full with one entree, but could stuff yourself with an entree, & splitting an appetizer & dessert. The menu's core is South Indian but some North Indian dishes are offered as well. They do not have traditionally associated with other regions of India such as Gujarat. Vegetarians & vegans will not have problems here as the menu has marked items & the staff are familiar with ingredients as well.

My wife & I have had:
Great beet croquettes, rava dosa, the winter uttappam, masala dosa, kale fritters, the 5 mini uttappam combo & the desert rasa malai.

3 things I do not like are:
* tables are very close to each other so it can be difficult to hear the person in front of or next to you that you actually want to hear
* reservations are hard to get, though you can walk in &  possibly get seated
* the salt lassi drink was extremely thick & salty.

name: Maxwell Norans
text: The French Revolution (French: Révolution française [ʁevɔlysjɔ̃ fʁɑ̃sɛːz]) was a period of far-reaching social and political upheaval in France and its colonies beginning in 1789. The Revolution overthrew the monarchy, established a republic, catalyzed violent periods of political turmoil, and finally culminated in a dictatorship under Napoleonwho brought many of its principles to areas he conquered in Western Europe and beyond. Inspired by liberal and radical ideas, the Revolution made a profound impression on the course of modern history, triggering the global decline of absolute monarchies while replacing them with republics and liberal democracies.[1] Through the Revolutionary Wars, it unleashed a wave of global conflicts that extended from the Caribbean to the Middle East. Historians widely regard the Revolution as one of the most important events in human history.

7/24/14

This is definitely a place I will return to in order to try the fried, crunchy, hot food. My initial visit in April came after a trip to Annex Burger across the street, where the veggie burger is actually a meat patty with veggies. I'm not vegan but I wasn't in the mood for meat so after my husband finished his meal, I came here.

I wasn't in the mood for a big meal so I ordered a green salad. I was hoping that a vegan restaurant would throw together a green party salad for my plate. But it was just a plain salad, some cucumbers I think but not a lot of other veggies. There were no croutons or sunflower seeds or anything to give it crunch. My total was $5.99 and I was pretty disappointed.

Also, it took a very long time to arrive. It was just a cold salad! The server the brought the food explained he couldn't find my number since I was sitting at a table near the front. Then I was left with no silverware. I feel like I was there on an off-night, and they deserve another try. Plus, I should ordered something with more soul than a salad, since most of the other reviews have wonderful things to say about the hot plates.

7/17/13

My friend's recent bachelorette party started at a spa, followed by a limo ride to dinner at AsiaSF. Holy $#*! This place was amazing. Our reservation was for 7 and a dinner selection was pre-chosen that included lots of menu items. It requires a minimum party of 6 to feast the way we did, or I would have already returned to eat again.

I can't say enough good things about the food. Everything was served in a shared manner but there was plenty enough for everyone to get a taste of it all. And a TON of food was brought out. There was nothing that we didn't enjoy. The special requests of one veggie/gluten-free girl were also catered to.  A boutiquey place like this could totally get away with a crap meal because you're mostly there for the show. We were all surprised at the quality of food. And the drinks! They were great! We received a comp shot for our bachelorette party celebrations and some of us received an additional one for checking-in on Yelp. Heck yes!

The show was hot. The ladies were smokin'! And the male staff (like the guy bussing our table with the snakebite piercing)... they were all gorgeous too!  How does it feel being really, really, ridiculously good looking?

Everything about the night was special. They even personalized our menu so that we could keep it as a keepsake. We interacted with lots of staff and they were all very attentive and friendly.

After dinner, we went downstairs and danced in the nightclub. Free admission with dinner. The vibe was awesome! I wish we had stayed longer than we did but the bachelorette celebrations continued elsewhere.  I've already started working on a group of 6 for a return. Can't wait to eat here again and oogle all the sexy dancers some more.

In the afternoon we walked by Epic Steak and decided to try it. We were taken outside to the patio area with a awesome view of the Bay Bridge.

We had the ceviche, Cesar's salad, dry aged 14oz  ribeye steak with a side of smoke apple wood bacon, sauteed spinach, and fries. Our kids ordered from the kids menu with the usual choices.

While enjoying our meal, I mentioned to my wife, that Epic should be on DDD or Delicious Destinations. Our waiter overhead our conversation and he said, that Epic was in fact,  featured on Delicious Destinations!

It didn't surprise me... the ambiance, the view, the food. It was the best dining experience we had in awhile.

As expected, it's expensive to dine here. Our bill came to $207 for a family of 4. Normally, we would spend at least $60 for lunch.

text:
If I visit Rally's again I'm going to stick to their fries. Service is friendly enough, though usually slow - even when there are not many customers.
The last four times I've stopped at a Rally's - different locations, even - the food has been lacking.
Every time recently there's been some issue with the order. Wrong items given, food either overcooked or lukewarm... Soft drinks that are 3/4 full of ice.
For some reason, also, I've noticed that every item I order seems to come liberally seasoned with ground black pepper. Burger, fish sandwich, chicken sandwich. Pepper overpowers my taste buds - literally drowning out any other flavor. I don't remember that being the case in the past.

I used to love Rally's and could always count on their quality.
Not any more, it seems.

text: I've been here many times over the past 4 years. Family friendly, the music isn't loud, service is above average...at least that's how it used to be. It's taken a dip in the past few months. I'm writing this as I'm sitting in the restaurant and I can say it's changed even more than the last time I came, and not for the better. You have the same usual wait time during the peak hours (30 to 45 minutes for a table of 5), but the service was less than stellar. Most of our servers and our waiter look like they don't want to be here. The food doesn't have the same quality for the price. It's definitely not high end sushi, but I expect to pay less for sushi that falls apart after lightly dipping it in soy sauce. The music was once at a moderate level and tasteful, but now I currently have a headache from the volume and the erratic electronica  they have playing. I'm not saying don't come to this place (if you like high energy, hip scenes this place is for you), but I'm just saying it used to sit a little higher in my repertoire of eats. It's worth coming here at least once, and therefore deserves at least 3 stars.

text:
Eclipse chocolate bar not only excels at chocolate creations but also at scrumptious breakfasts.

I had the crispy quinoa fritter with maple, muscovado glazed bacon and cheddar cheese add ons.

The result was one of the best and most interesting breakfasts I've ever had, not to mention very healthy and filling.

The combination of flavors really worked well on the tastebuds.

The local Dark Horse Roasters Brazil/Guatemala coffee gave me an excellent pick-me-up and bold flavor.

The Star was the frozen chocolate peanut butter mouse with vanilla semifreddo(close to a gelato).

It had a salty, nutty mixture resulting in one of the best chocolate desserts I've ever had and the #1 standout dessert for me in 2018.

Service by Manager Daniel was exemplary.  I was impressed with his knowledge and attentive, courteous service. 10 plus!

Eclipse achieves my 10 best ever ranking for breakfast as well as dessert.

I consider this restaurant a "must visit" for chocolate afficionados for San Diego.

text:
4/18/18

Ducey's is an upstairs bar/grill and a downstairs restaurant. Our afternoon on the water ended with some Duck Quack shooters ($9) Bud Lights ($4.50) and a basket of onion rings and garlic fries ($7.50). And then a couple more Duck Quack shots because they were that good. The sun sparkled down all around us and our server, Jessica, did a great job of checking on us at appropriate times and making drink suggestions when we asked. Loved her! We finished up our late-day snack staring at the pretty water we'd just been swimming in, which was perfect!

Fast-forward a few hours and we found ourselves on the first floor of Ducey's. The romantic lakeside restaurant has an incredible view of it's own. We were staying in a chalet at Pines Resort so we brought most of our own food, but it's hard to turn down the temptation of shared dessert. Creme brulee to die for here! Plus, only $6 for a fairly large serving and it was very, very good. Bill was the host who greeted us and served us the sweet treat. He's also a cat lover.

We meandered back upstairs one more time before the night ended, around 8:30 p.m., and each enjoyed a chocolate martini ($12). Ryan makes a delicious drink and we sipped on those for a few more minutes before heading to bed early. Does life get better than that?! Five stars all around for Ducey's.

name: Jack Flynn
text:
Inventive Drinks with some Great Food

Orchard City Kitchen, is an experience when it comes to dinning. It isn't so much about the flavor parings as it is about joining with a group of friends to share $12-$20 tapas and sip stiff drinks. At the end of the night, you'll have gone through layers of the menu feeling satisfied with some highlights, but a lot of "I was expecting more" feelings.

The drinks are strong, yet come in interesting vessels, there is a love of unique flavors, that will make most people either fall in love with the boldness or find their meal sidetracked by the oddity of the drink.

The individual plates range from the unique shaved raw brussels sprouts with a vinaigrette just the right crunch of croutons, to a tender octopus overpowered by liquid smoke. There's high notes where flavors are dealt with a subtle hand, letting the customer wonder if the chef really is this brilliant, or if they just stumbled upon what makes people love food.  Then, there's the low notes where your mouth is blown out by the fishiest of shrimp ever put on a plate.

There's moments of brilliance where their signature Biscuits Bacon honey Butter makes you stop and forget that you're not supposed to eat gluten anymore.  You find yourself wishing there was more bacon, more butter, more biscuits, and more time to relish the perfect pairing.

Then there's moments where you look at the tiny cold duck breast with bland lentils making you wonder if the chef decided to take a smoke break.

Overall, this is a fun place to go and spend $100.00 on a couple of drinks and a few plates.  It isn't somewhere you'll rave to everyone you've ever met about the succulent morsels you've put in your mouth, but you won't be overly disappointed either.  If you have two drinks you'll probably find the entire night enchanting and fantastic, you'll also need an uber home.

This is a solid 3 stars, maybe a 4th if they toned down the overpowering love of smoke flavor.

Family went to this place for lunch for the first time and when I received the bill. I noticed a "ACA MANDATE 2 %" fee!? I asked our waiter, "what is this charge?" He replied, " it's mandatory charge for health insurance" " Why am I paying for health insurance" ? We just came here to eat!

Still didn't answer my question, after doing some  research. It's a tax penalty to ensure that companies who choose not to provide health care for their workers are still paying into the healthcare system.

So this restaurant is too cheap to offer health insurance for their employees but to off set them being penalized, they pass on the costs to their customers!

Also,  as a  customer I should be    informed before ordering by the staff or documented on the menu that the restaurant will be adding the ACA Mandate fee to my bill!

At least I will have a choice to patronize this business or not!

This is our first and last time eating @ this restaurant!

name: Jack Flynn
text:
Solid Food

If you want a burger and some fries this is a great stop in Sunnyvale. It has solid food, nothing you'll write home about, but a good bite and will satiate you until dinner.

They have a ton of different options for fries with toppings.  My office has tried them all, the favorite has been the pizza fries and the cheese and ranch fries.

The fries are crispy, salty, and fresh.  When you are having a hankering for fries, this is a good stop.

As for the rest of the food, everything is ok, it tastes like bar food and you can see into the kitchen, so you know it is fresh and clean.

As for inside, the place is a bit noisy for my taste, but I usually like a more intimate gathering spot. It has lots of sports on multiple flat screens. There's booths and benches for easy sitting.

Overall, a good place, that will satiate the hungry and remind you what a good burger tastes like.

name: Maxwell Norans
text: The Enlightenment emerged out of a European intellectual and scholarly movement known as Renaissance humanism. Some consider the publication of Isaac Newton's Principia Mathematica (1687) as the first major enlightenment work. French historians traditionally date the Enlightenment from 1715 to 1789, from the death of Louis XIV of France until the outbreak of the French Revolution that ended the Ancien Regime. Most end it with the beginning of the 19th century. Philosophers and scientists of the period widely circulated their ideas through meetings at scientific academies, Masonic lodges, literary salons, coffeehouses and in printed books, journals, and pamphlets. The ideas of the Enlightenment undermined the authority of the monarchy and the Church and paved the way for the political revolutions of the 18th and 19th centuries. A variety of 19th-century movements, including liberalism and neoclassicism, trace their intellectual heritage to the Enlightenment.[4]

name: Maxwell Norans
text: He was born Napoleone Buonaparte(Italian: [napoleˈoːne ˌbwɔnaˈparte]) in Corsicato a relatively modest Italian family from minor nobility. He was serving as an artillery officer in the French army when the French Revolution erupted in 1789. He rapidly rose through the ranks of the military, seizing the new opportunities presented by the Revolution and becoming a general at age 24. The French Directory eventually gave him command of the Army of Italy after he suppressed the 13 Vendémiaire revolt against the government from royalist insurgents. At age 26, he began his first military campaignagainst the Austrians and the Italian monarchs aligned with the Habsburgs—winning virtually every battle, conquering the Italian Peninsula in a year while establishing "sister republics" with local support, and becoming a war hero in France. In 1798, he led a military expedition to Egypt that served as a springboard to political power. He orchestrated a coup in November 1799 and became First Consul of the Republic. After the Peace of Amiens in 1802, Napoleon turned his attention to France's colonies. He sold the Louisiana Territory to the United States, and he attempted to restore slavery to the French Caribbean colonies. However, while he was successful in restoring slavery in the eastern Caribbean, Napoleon failed in his attempts to subdue Saint-Domingue, and the colony that France once proudly boasted of as the "Pearl of the Antilles" became independent as Haitiin 1804. Napoleon's ambition and public approval inspired him to go further, and he became the first Emperor of the French in 1804. Intractable differences with the British meant that the French were facing a Third Coalition by 1805. Napoleon shattered this coalition with decisive victories in the Ulm Campaign and a historic triumph over the Russian Empire and Austrian Empire at the Battle of Austerlitz which led to the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire.

text:
2/18/18

Still consistantly the best clam chowder on the wharf. I love stopping at their outside counter and grabbing the roasted garlic ($3) which they will heat on request. Their clam chowder can be served ready-to-eat in a bread bowl ($10) or taken to go if you want something delicious to enjoy at home. They also have awesome slices of smoked salmon ($14 for the piece I grabbed today.)

Indoor seating is available if you want to sit down and enjoy your meal, but if the weather's nice, it's always wonderful to take the food to-go and eat outside next to the water.

8/20/12 - Five Stars

VAMPIRES, BEWARE!

Oddly, on our stop at the wharf a couple weekends ago, the Grotto wasn't giving out samples of their great Chowder. But we didn't come for the chowder. We drove pretty far out of our way to stop here, just for some roasted garlic and delicious garlic bread.

The line was so long this particular night! Alfredo D. gave us helpful service when we reached the front! We were there just for the outside food!! No other restaurant had a line. But I wasn't chancing getting the garlic from anywhere else. It's the best here. Finally at the front of line, we learned they were out of (sourdough) bread! The guy working (Joseph!) was super friendly and efficient and we enjoying talking briefly with him while our garlic heated.  We ordered a few pieces of garlic bread and some roasted garlics (Garlic $2 Bread $1.) (The line was gone once people learned about the bread!)

We weren't even able to walk and find seating before we'd finished it all. If you're a fan of garlic, the roasted ones here are awesome! I eat the whole thing. I've tried to duplicate what they do at home and it's impossible.  The garlic bread is probably the best I've had anywhere. It's consistently a perfect match of garlicky butter on top of fresh bread.

After a search for a bar and a couple of decent cocktails, we were planning to head home, but decided to stop and see if they had more sourdough yet (to take with us). They did! Our same employee was still there and helped us again. One of his coworkers was eating on the other side of the counter. I can imagine how hard it'd be to not eat all of the delicious food if you worked here, but if you're on break, take the consumption somewhere else.  We ended up getting more garlic and garlic bread at the same time - so glad we did! It was amazing on the whole drive home!

NOTE: Garlic is one of the most popular healthy herbs today. It is toxic to cats. Drinking lemon juice or eating a few slices of lemons will stop bad garlic breath. It has anti-cancer agents and has been shown to reduce cholesterol.  It promotes healthy immune function and weight control. It's fun and EASY to grow! And I'm pretty sure it works as a natural mosquito repellent. Cuz those things NEVER bite me.  :)  With West Nile back in the news, it might be time to get out your garlic recipes!!

I went with the Il Pesce seafood bistro with lovely balcony seating overlooking the twinkling lights of century city.

I had a late night snack of mussels and a cocktail.

The Hola Bella("Hello Beautiful") cocktail was very nice with rock salt on the rim consisting of vodka and fruit juices. The Prince Edward Island Mussels(off New Brunswick Canada)were amazing-all plump, expertly cooked swimming in tasty broth(I love scooping up the broth with the shells).

The Mussels were some of the best I've had in years. The starter portion was almost the size of a full meal and filling with the fresh bread and butter.

I had a great time and plan on returning to try more fresh shellfish and pasta dishes at the other Eataly Bistros.

text:
Starbelly is located on 16th street and Market St and a block from Castro st. We visited here on a Saturday, we reserved the table ahead of time, there was one hour wait, it was perfect for us since we were driving from Cupertino.
Now they have outside dining, both in the backside patio, as well as in front of the restaurant with covered seating, each tables are separated. Also they were nicely following all Covid protocols, we were supposed to wear masks when waiter was close to the table.
They have brunch menu during  the weekend, we ordered Margaritas, French Toast, fried chicken po’boy, jalapeño & radicchio slaw, sesame bun  and smoked mozzarella, broccolini rapini, Aleppo chile, garlic & lemon,
Service very courteous and reasonably quick.
Drinks were great, French toast was delicious and aesthetically pleasing. Chicken burger, fries and Pizza were very tasty. First time I had a pizza with lemon zest, it was an interesting combination.
There are two gender neutral restrooms, which were clean and well maintained.
Regarding parking near restaurant, you have to depend on street parking, just like most places in San Francisco.
Dining out in the city after a long time, we really enjoyed the whole experience. Highly recommend this place.

POTATO TACO, OH HOW I LOVE THEE

First potato taco experience! Best thing ever!!

Unfortunately our overall experience at LaMor wasn't fabulous, but my crispy potato taco was so good. It's too bad I couldn't put any salsa on it because it was so watered down.  I think my husband was a little envious of the crunchy potato taco and he's usually not much of a non-meat guy. But the soft tacos we had with chicken and carnitas just weren't very good.

The shells were fresh and that's a big plus, but the meat on the inside of the street-style tacos was a little fatty and we really didn't enjoy the taste.  The chips were nice and fresh but the salsas (both regular and hot) were so watered down it was difficult to get much salsa on the chips. And the times we did it was a dripping mess all over the table.

The lady working was super nice and even came over to refill our chip basket, even though we didn't have a big order. She had a really friendly smile. The place was overall very clean - well, not the top of our table as we got up to leave!  I'd go back for another potato taco if I were around here. For sure! But I'd prob bring my own hot sauce.

text: First time here and was super dissatisfied. We ordered the fat Jerry and the pepperoni pizza burger. The portions weren't nearly as big as expected. Ordered the burger for my son and I to share. He is 7 years old and was able to finish the entire thing by himself. The fat Jerry we ordered is supposed to come with Cheesesteak, chicken fingers, mozzarella sticks, crisp bacon, fried eggs, fries, mayo ketchup, salt and pepper. We were missing the chicken fingers and the mozzarella sticks!!! So basically half the sandwich. The bacon was also not crispy, had the consistent of uncooked turkey bacon. And the fried EGGS...no....just one egg. And whatever we did have on the sandwich was just piled in the middle. The ends of the sandwich were basically just bread. I think I'd have to say subway is more generous with their sandwich toppings. Got fries as well with the combo, seasoned. Seasoning was gross and the fries were so cold and almost tasted stale. I suggest getting the regular fries, seasoning is not worth it. I am graciously giving two stars due to the fact that when I called to complain they did give me my money back for the fat Jerry and also gave me credit to come in and get a new sandwich. We embarked on this venture @midnight so I'm going to blame these mistakes on the staff being tired and not so detail oriented. Next time I come back I will definitely make sure I go earlier in the day especially to make sure my food is fresh.

text:
Came for an early dinner. Coming from Kansas City and having spent time in Texas I’m a pretty hard judge of bbq. Aptos St Bbq was pretty good. The menu was typical, prices were reasonable, staff was friendly, and the atmosphere was great. I saw a lot of people ordering take out.

My ribs were meaty and tender. The sauces were self serve and were awesome. I got coleslaw and baked beans as a side. The coleslaw was good, and pretty standard. The beans were more like chili beans. I see this a lot in California and not sure where people think baked beans should taste like chili.

I didn’t get a beer, but it was a neat experience watching people. They offer samples of all their micro brews so you can pick the one you want. It was very hard to read the beer menu! But it looked like a good selection.

Little touches like free soda refills and wet naps added a nice touch.

Parking only on the street.

text:
OK so first of I want to start by saying I been wanting some good old fashion New York style pizza for years. My family and I did our individual research on where we should try the New York style pizza we all agreed on Giovanni's; however I was very disappointed.
The wait time was 15-20 mins which wasn't bad. The place seem very clean and friendly. I only had a quick chat with the staff no small talk at all. Didn't ask how my day was or if I was a returning customer, didn't bother  me. What did bother me was when I return home with the pepperoni New york size 18 inches it was burned and greasy! You can see in my pictures. The crust was rock hard! I was very disappointed In this Pizza shack after I saw all those wonderful reviews people all over Sacramento to left. They had plenty of staff on board and the place wasn't busy at all, there shouldn't be NO reason why they have to lack on quality so bad. As you can we still ate it because I wasn't going to make an extra unnecessary trip back and to another pizza place. We sucked it up and ate a crummy pizza. Not only was it +$33 but they don't even deliver! I thought we were in 2018? Adapting is what makes a business successful. I will not recommend this pizza shack to anyone. My family did mention the Ranch was amazing. So we would give the ranch 5 stars.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
10/26/14

We had a horrible experience here a couple of months ago. After bringing our crab-for-two our server sat at the table behind us with another girl and complained about how he gets no tips and is disrespected.  We finally turned around to let them know we could hear every word and the girl rudely asks "yeah?!" Oh, sorry, did we interrupt your conversation?

Our server then told us that they were watching us eat, and that it was like "dinner and a show" for them. We had to ask for him to bring melted butter and when he returned he made a joke about us getting FOOD POISONING. I was in Sacramento for a legal convention and the fear of getting sick and missing my lectures was not a good one. Why would anyone ever joke about this while serving expensive seafood?

Our server asked if I was still using the salt on our table halfway through our food. I had potatoes left so I said I "wasn't using it at that moment". He told us he wanted to get out of there quick so he was just going to clean it up. He took the salt from our table, wiped it down, and then finished cleaning the section. As he swept up under tables he and another employee again talking rudely across the room about how much money they could make somewhere else. It wasn't that late and there were other diners at the tables around us, but outside of his section. We were his last table and he was obviously trying to rush us.

The server disappeared after bringing our big bill. I had to ask someone else for more salt, and finally had to ask someone for a to-go container. We left really upset. An employee outside told us he thought Michelle was the manager that night but he didn't know. What sort of manager doesn't make their presence known and check on employees/diners all night?! No wonder service was horrible.

I called the manager as soon as we returned to our hotel room. (I think I spoke with Samantha?) I explained exactly what was happened and she was apologetic. However, we saw the same server working the next night as we walked by. Guess joking about food poisoning isn't that big of a deal. The food was good but it was hard to swallow when service is that retched.  I'd never return to this location knowing that they really don't care how their customers are treated.

text:
Barleymash is a large restaurant with a full bar, alot of seating and large screen TVs with sports.

The food is excellent with a large variety of offerings. I had the salami/pepperoni flatbread, seared albacore tuna(sashimi quality)with salad/goat cheese. House made garlic pretzels with cheddar sauce and honey mustard.

My drink was their popular "Stay Classy"(vodka, lemon, peach).

For dessert, I had the vanilla ice cream on chocolate/oatmeal mega cookie(very large!).

Everything tasted amazing!  The pretzels and sauce was some of the best I've ever had!

Service by Uli and manager Greg was superb.  These guys really know how to treat customers.

The place was packed but service was not compromised in the least.

Greg told me they have Karaoke every Tuesday, standup comedy next week on Thursday and a DJ every night from 10p-2a!

Impressive...I plan to be here again and try out more fantastic food and entertainment.

Barleymash, in my opinion, ranks as one of the best fine dining and entertainment venues in southern cal.

Prices seemed a bit high, but maybe that’s the average price in the area.

Unfortunately, even during the worst of times, there were a few things they could have done to improve. Hand written signs, dirty tables, dried old pineapple in the gelato, and poor customer service. There was also a non customer working or studying outside, using their table, and listening to music. The server never came outside to address it. His music ruined the atmosphere.

I was immediately seated with excellent service.  The Ikura rice bowl was very good, however, there could have been more of the tasty Ikura salmon eggs I like so much.

The entree, Tonkatsu with chicken breast, was also very tasty with thick hearty broth and a nice amount of Ramen noodles.

I subtract a star for lack of atmosphere and the place was very hot, needing some aircon. There also should have been more Ikura in the bowl.

Overall, though, this is a solid choice for Ramen and at under $20 for 2 dishes the prices are reasonable

text: Great place - I came in the first week of 2018. I had a decadent seafood lobster rissoto that was fantastic. I thought it a little small at first, but with a beer, and some nice bread, it was quite hearty and filling. The restaurant is nice, very upscale, and has a modern feel. I saw a lot of folks here dressed up, especially the ladies, but the place  definitely has a casual vibe too. The bar had lots of great liquor, lots of great beer, and wine to choose from too. Leroy's seemed to be one of the nicer places in the area, and pricier, but if the rest of the menu comes out as well as the rissoto, it'd certainly be worth it. I was only in town for a week and was glad I got in there at least once to try it out, and believe, I hit the jackpot ordering that rissoto. I sat at the bar, the dining room was very nice, and there's a large outdoor seating area to choose your seating option. Obviously I went in winter time and the place was still pretty busy, during high season you better call for a reservation. For a night on the town, get dressed up, and hit Leroy's for a great time!

Before meeting with a client in San Leandro, my boss recommended that I stop for a bite to eat at Blvd. Burgers.  My husband did the drive to SL with me so he was happy to rewarded with a beef patty, and I was excited for the veggie burger!

The simple burgers we ordered ($6.70 ea.) came with fresh tomato, lettuce, pickles and red onion.  My veggie burger was really good, but the patty was kind of small. I added the veggies from my husband's plate to mine and ate it all.

The tables each have condiments on them: catsup, mustard, spicy mayo, hot sauce, relish, etc. and there is a fountain soda machine ($1.75).  I had water, even though the ice cream shake was recommended to us.  (And we saw one on another table that looked great!)

Caitlin was working the register when we ordered and another young man promised to clean up our plates as we left.  Service was very friendly and the place was really clean.

Little bits of sausage combined with the right amount of pepper made the gravy perfect. I could have just had that for breakfast and would have been fine. The chef at this establishment really knows food and must be a foodie like me because the dish was prepared as if it was going to be photographed. While we were eating THE OWNER came to our table to refill coffee and asked how everything was. Dining room was clean and well kept. 7/24/14

My husband and I stopped in and ordered the potato nachos. He wasn't very hungry so it was my choice. The $9 plate of chips, cheese, bacon, and spicy sour cream was a little disappointing.  Before it arrived though, a swarm of flies surrounded our table and we had to keep batting them away. (No, they weren't following us, they were just in the place all over.) One even rested on my water glass. It kind of freaked us out and we didn't even have our food.

When the nachos did arrive, most disappointing (for husband) was that less than one piece of bacon was chopped onto our plate of chips. I know, because I had one little tiny piece of it, and Casey ate all the rest, and verified that there was almost none.  He wasn't able to eat the chips with the spicy sour cream because it was too hot for him so he ate around those.  I added Chipotle hot sauce and sriracha (yes, both!) to my plate, as well as some salt. My chips were crispy and very spicy.

As we neared the end of the chips, there were so many left with no cheese at all.  The housemade chips were very good, but at that price, I would expect more cheese, more bacon, and more care to the plate that youre serving customers. Make sure it's consistent and appears well put together.

Our server (Kinder) was excellent, and at one point I think a manager also helped us and even offered to "expedite" our payment upon seeing my credit card out, but we weren't in any rush. Service was good all around.  We would definitely come back to try something else or order a drink, but the potato nachos just weren't a good value ($9.74).

text:
Really enjoyed this place. From Creole, to plant based food, ramen, Mediterranean and burgers there is something for everyone here. I looked at all places before I finally ended up at Pig Pen. All the various choices appeared to be offering top notch IG worthy fair. The ingredients all appeared to be fresh everywhere. I want to try the creole place next. Bignets anyone?? Okay so for my review, it will be for where I actually ate, Pig Pen
I ordered the Bacon something burger (will edit when i can find the menu) and the mac flamingo frys (this too I need to edit.
Burger: slightly on the salty side and slightly over cooked (even after confirming if I am okay with medium at the register) but over all super good. The brioche was a 7 out of 10, not perfect but not bad, slightly dry. The quality of the beef used was lean but also very delicious. Seasoned well, again slightly on the too salty side but really really good. The onion straws and candies bacon were amazing as well as the bacon spread.
The fries were amazing, covered in macaroni and cheese, bacon and crushed flaming hot cheetos I highly recommend this. Fries got soggy really quick so eat them first and fast. I only ate about 60% of my burger and 35% of my fries and was full. Keep that in mind. Eating here is also quite a bit more than a good sit down restaurant so expect to pay big to play with this wild instagram food. The burger and fries were $21 and i topped 15% which i regret as i received no service after making the purchase. Not sure what the tip was for, also seemed forced as you get a guilt trip for not pushing anything on the screen, I'm sure that's intentional and works so hey, go ahead. I personally will not be ripping again. I couldnt justify spending another dollar here so I went with a cup for water... which is the smallest dang cup ever, maybe 4oz or so. Gulped it up quite quickly before even receiving food and then the gal didnt seem too keen on getting me more (she was busy on her phone). Bad deal. Anyway, all in all if you dont mind spending big for a unique good experience, this place is cool with solid good food. Just know up front I wouldnt tip and budget for a price you wouldnt typically expect from a place like this.

name: donny blaze
text: If you want to feel and taste the meaning of San Diego look no further. This vibrant traditional Mexican restaurant reminds me of grandma and grandpa's house. From the beautiful patio to the traditional decor, Guadalajaras food is grandma's recipes to your plate. I personally love the fish burritos and the margaritas.  Parking is tuff at night

name: Jonathan Adler
text:
On my 2nd visit and 1st in 2019 I was really hungry and had the Queso Fundido Con Chorizo appetizer(melted jack cheese topped with spicy beef chorizo). It was a great starter. The jack cheesiness hit my sweet spot definitely.

My Pollo Asado entree(beautiful presentation I might add arranged artfully on a handmade painted plate)is also a standout with a medley of sauteed veges surrounding a grilled chicken breast.

Their salsa and chips may also be the best I've had in a Mexican restaurant with plenty of refills.

Service was outstanding by their 14yr veteran Cynthia-flawless in every respect, one of the best I've met with grace and class(hard to find these days).

This daytime visit I was able to enjoy a large table to myself in their gorgeous courtyard with beautiful murals, fountains and exotic foliage.

Overall, I was even more impressed on my 2nd visit and rank Casa Guadalajara as my #1 favorite fine Mexican restaurant in San Diego.

Well done CG team.

Very highly recommended.

of the best fine dining Mexican restaurants in my estimation.

The place is huge and was packed when I was there with alot of locals which is usually a good sign.

The atmosphere is fun, energetic and festive.  There was a nice Mariachi band visiting tables keeping the place hopping.

I had their signature Tequila lime shrimp and rolled Muchisimos Taquitos which were both delicious.  I ate at the bar and the server/ bartender Francisco was great and very professional.

I also really liked the decor there featuring Mexican art, statues and paintings.  Even the walls are nicely covered with gorgeous mosaic designs.

This is probably one of the best fine dining mexican restaurants in the nation and certainly top ten in san diego.

I recommend reservations as this is a very popular restaurant.

name: Add Wheelslip
text: The House of Prime Rib, a SF institution.  Bask in the old timey digs.  A recent remodel is palpable and although borderline cramped, still comfortable.  Prime rib takes center stage and comes with several sides.  Tell the waiter the cut you prefer and await the stainless steel zeppelin.  First off, a salad is tossed table side and a warm loaf local sourdough at hand.  Then, a mini Airstream is wheeled table side, filled with au jus, sides and prime rib glory.  Oh yes... it is a glorious sight.  The chef makes quick work of your order.  Simultaneously, your server is dressing up baked potatoes table side.  Next thing you know... you are staring down a beautifully prepared prime rib, swimming in decadent au jus.  Creamed spinach, creamed corn, yorkshire pudding and a fully dressed baked potatoe.  A unique experience no doubt.  However, the service was robotic and cold.  The food quality was good, but lacked the 5-star pizzazz.

The $45.85 cut of prime rib was insane. I had forgotten how tender, flavorful, and juicy their cuts are. Hard to forget about the sides (which are just as good) but you want to focus on your meat plate. Creamed spinach is very popular, as is the Yorkshire Pudding! Yumm!! I had to ask a couple of times for more au jus but overall service was fantastic for being as packed as it was (as it always it). Oscar was our primary server - very nice! - but other staffed helped out as well.

A couple of drinks brought the bill to about $220 before tip. But that's really not that bad for the quality of food youre getting. If you haven't been here before, go spoil yourself!

Ordering was at the counter, and food was delivered to your table.  Take-out was at a different location in the restaurant.

Five (5) stars?! Is that ALL I can give?! Pfffft. Doesn't seem fair.

So I'm a little behind the game sometimes. This year was my first time watching the show 'Survivor' and I even participated (and lost) in a pool to determine the winner. I just saw my first ever episode of 'Big Brother' a couple of weeks ago. And yesterday was my first time dining at Digger's. Guess someone finally moved that rock I was living under.

I've been thinking about the garlic fries here for a long time. I love perusing Yelp pictures and the garlic fries (and so many other things) were very memorable. I wanted some jalapenos on my fries so I was shocked when I saw this is actually a menu item! Cajun garlic fries with jalapenos and cheese. I ordered this without the cheese. Husband had a grilled ham and cheese sandwich. And our friend Val had a burger that could probably win awards for size and good looks.

I live in Concord but not very close to here so I would never have known about this great Diner if not for Yelp. I love diners. I love their atmosphere and food and service. The employees here were all friendly with smiley faces. We looked at all the advertising printed directly onto the table while we waited for our food. There was a gravedigger pictured that I pointed out, picturing the man who apparently started this place (the decorations started to make some sense). Husband Casey teased me and pointed at a guy working in the kitchen and said "that's the owner/gravedigger". It wasn't. But RIGHT AT THAT MOMENT the guy actually walked in the front door. OMG. I asked our server if the guy in the doorway was the same as the one on the table. Yes. Yes he was. We even got to meet him and he was awesome.

Food was awesome too. It wasn't a long wait before we were served and everything was great. Even though the fries are cut medium (and I prefer skinny cut) they were still very crispy and good. Lots of jalapenos! And a really good value - tons of food for not a lot of money. We will definitely be back.

9/24/15

One of the first dates my husband and I went on was to Va de Vi. We both love this place. It's a great place to come for a nice lunch, or if youre going out with friends. You can share small plates or each order your own - and their food is terrific.

Your wait on the weekend will be close to half an hour without a reservation, but it's well-worth it. Especially if you get one of their adorable outdoor patio tables. Water fountains and decorative lights in the trees - it's wonderful!

Service is great and there's a hard-working gentleman (manager/owner?) that is always there when I'm there overseeing the staff and keeping things running smoothly.

My favorite dishes to share are the blistered shishito peppers and the garlic fries. The meat charcuterie plate and cheese plates are also fantastic group dishes.

My group of 7 girlfriends was out last weekend celebrating 3 of our birthdays. The 6 other girls were here from out of town and we waited about 40 minutes for our table once we put our name in.   Before we were seated inside I let the hostess know we were celebrating birthdays (my birthday is in two days, another girl's bday is tomorrow, and 1 of our party had hers last week). She said she'd let our waitress know, but either she forgot or our waitress forgot, because after our plates were licked clean and every last drop of cocktail and wine were finished, we paid a bill of over $200 and left without even a verbal "happy birthday" acknowledgment. (For the size of our group that bill was extremely reasonable and we were happy with every dish/plate/drink and the service). But wished our celebrations had been acknowledged. We actually weren't even offered a dessert menu to look at.

name: Jonathan Adler
text:
This is a well known pub/restaurant that was on Sunset for over 30 years and just recently reopened on Highland just a block North of Melrose.

I happened to walk in yesterday and was really impressed with how nice their new place looks.  It is spacious with a patio area, 2 bars and cozy interior seating.

The Staff is really professional and treated me great.  The atmosphere is relaxed, fun and conducive to meeting friends, dates and business.

I was really hungry and started with their Gardner Salad(named after the founder) which was excellent with spinach leaves, roasted corn and cherry tomatoes.  My main fish and chips is the best I've had in the area.  The dessert, raspberry tart was delicious and even the coffee was single origin from Rwanda called Silverback and purchases help small farmers there.

The drinks I had were amazing-Sprecher root beer from Wisconsin and a Covent Gardens cocktail(vodka, kiwi & fresh lime juice).

I had a great time and this is now my favorite pub/restaurant to unwind and meet friends in the Hollywood area.

There is also Valet parking there.
