name: Alan Harnett
text:
This Everett and Jones location is in the heart of Jack London Square in Oakland.  It's a fairly big space that would be good for a large group or event.  It has modern, cheery decor and a full bar.  Lunch prices are very reasonable and the portions are large.

Sadly thats where the positives end.  Parking can be incredibly challenging in the neighborhood.  There were about 10 people inside the huge restaurant when I arrived for lunch.  I ordered the ribs which come with wheat bread and potato salad, with your choice of sauce.  The ribs were incredibly tough and had a lot of gristle.  I eat BBQ a lot both in the Bay Area and back home in Kansas City.  These ribs were just bad.

Its sad that you cannot choose your choice of side.  It would be ok, if the potato salad was ok, but it was just mediocre.  Its typical to get bread with your bbq meal, but usually its just one piece of bread used to soak up the sauce, or at a good place you get thick toasted bread with garlic butter top.  This meal came with two full slices of cold plain wheat bread stacked on top of the ribs.  Below the bread was the mound of potato salad.  My ribs tasted like potato salad and turned cold below the cold potato salad.  Just gross.  Could you offer a choice of side (besides potato salad) and allow some sides to have an uncharge?

In the background you could hear the cooks cutting ribs or meat.  But either the knife was dull, or the meat was tough as they were loudly slamming the meat cleaver each time.  Slow cooked, tender bbq does not need this.

The ribs were described as "award winning and slow cooked cooked to superb tenderness".  I would say these are all lies.  The Oakland Tribune where the award came from is no longer in business, the ribs were tough and did not fall off the bone, and had no smoke flavor.

There are much better bbq restaurants in Oakland and in the Bay Area.  Please choose these first before coming to Everett and Jones.

4/24/13

HAPPY HOUR OYSTER HAPPINESS

I should probably make a Yelp list soon of all the Happy Hour (HH) places that serve $1 oysters. This one would top the list. The oysters we had were in these small, thin little shells (almost see-through when empty) and were very likely the best oysters either of us had ever had. East or west coast. They were Chef's Creek and the thin shells sitting on crushed ice made them extra cold as we consumed. I imagine that is part of what made them so memorable.

We washed down the $1 sea bites with beers in tall glasses. The bartenders were attentive and fun - I think one was in training. I actually knew one of them from high school (Justin) and he was able to keep his level of professionalism high while being very friendly and chatting with us for a few moments. Quality service all around from the bar staff.

It was overall a great experience and we'll be back for more happy hours.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
6/18/13

HAPPY BIRTHDAY TO MY COUSIN

My cousin was scheduled to come to SF from Seattle for work the week of her bday, which gave me an opportunity to celebrate it with her. We picked a place close to where she was staying in Union Square and picked her up. Traffic was horrendous getting to Canela, but we found street parking out front and were on time for our 6:30 reservation.

We ordered the Padron Peppers upon seating (before even looking over the rest of the menu). I haven't seen these outside of Firefly in Vegas and love them! The peppers were more heavily fried here. Very tasty but not quite as crispy and crunchy as the ones I love in Nevada.

We also ordered a full order of shrimp ($15) which were very, very good. Large and juicy. Cooked nicely with great flavor. I spooned up all the broth when the shrimp were finished. My husband ordered ham croquettes ($10) and the one I had was wonderfully crispy on the outside with a creamy inside. Like the ham and cheese had blended into an awesome melty sauce. Garlic fries ($4) were good but they were thick cut and not crispy enough for me. I had a few but didn't really enjoy them as much as the other two at the table. The sauce was good, slightly spicy.

Husband also ordered the tapas plate of meatballs ($12) and I enjoyed one but liked my shrimp better.  My favorite order was the veggie plate ($16 for full order plus $2 for anchovie add). There was a great assortment of veggies and it was a good amount of food (though, $16 is a lot for a vegetable plate). Even though this was my favorite dish, I thought it was a little oily. (probably why it was my favorite) All of the vegetables were saturated - it was still really good though!

I asked for hot sauce to accompany the meal and received a nice, homemade hot sauce in a cute serving container. It was great and went well with the dishes we ordered.

The server was good, though a little slow. We weren't in a hurry but I felt like he should have asked if we were ready for the check after dessert, instead of us having to find him to ask for it. Our drinks were refilled though and he was friendly.

We ordered two desserts. Even though it was the day-of for my cousin's bday (which we'd let them know in advance) there's no bday dessert and they were each $8. She did get a candle with her churros. And they came with a melted chocolate dipping sauce. Very popular at the table. I preferred husband's creme brulee-like dish called Catalana but thought it was sort of small for $8 and would have liked more of the sugar-shell-topping. The custard filling was outstanding.

All in all, great bday, great dinner, great restaurant.

text:
We went there last night and were very clear that we had two people who had allergies. One with celiac one with a severe gluten allergy.

We checked with the waiter about it and were assured the dishes we picked would be safe. We ate and went back to the hotel. The person with the gluten allergy became violently ill shortly after our return. With a full blown reaction from eating there.

After a fun filled night of vomiting, diarrhea, and horrific cramps we now get to head home.

We were very disappointed at this carelessness. If it had been our little one who has full blown celiac this could have been even more tragic.

We won't return due to this.

On the plus side the food was well prepared and tasty. If you don't have any food allergies it would be a nice place to eat at.

EDIT:
Added our receipt so people know this is a true review.

EDIT 2:
Andrew from Scala's called and was very nice and was horrified and shocked this happened. They have gluten protocols they follow due to understanding people with allergies and sensitivities. text:
I popped in for a pizza to go. I was greeted by nearly every staff member while I waited. The place smelled amazing so I grabbed a beer while waiting for the pizza. The chairs were cloth covered little jewels, so soft that it makes a girl like me feel like I'm welcome to make myself at home. I wish I had visited the bathroom on my way in because I probably would have played the old-school arcade game. This quaint little pizza spot has a lot going for it and I haven't even talked about the margarita-ish pizza.
First off, I was super pleased with the chewy and crispy crust. The sauce was a spicy and surprisingly warming tomato base and the cheese was placed like how I always imagined the original pizza makers did. Slices of mozzarella were strategically set to give a great cheese to sauce ratio. Cherry tomatoes and basil topped the pizza but no vinaigrette drizzle which is fine because the flavor kick I look for in the drizzle was in the sauce. The look of the spiced red sauce on the toasty crust topped with the deep green herbs made it irresistible. I had a slice of my to go order in store and had no regrets about that choice. The temp was perfect! It's very refreshing not having to breathe like a dumb dragon after biting into a pizza fresh out of the oven.
It's a very clean pizza and it's delicious hot, heavenly at car temperature, and super satisfying served cold for breakfast. So I have to say...... I highly recommend!

The price was a little steep around $12  bucks. I picked out the $6 box, came with drink, cookie, fries, cheese burger and a spicy chicken sandwich.

The wait time wasn't too long. Before we knew it our food arrived. The customer service was non existent. But not knocking them down too much because of it. I just noticed the short staff on a Saturday night.

Inside was pretty clean and the plus was the free WiFi.

I really enjoyed my meal everything was piping hot and on point. No complaints on my end.

My daughter thought her burger was going to have slices of avocado. She miss read the description. It was an guacamole burger not an avocado burger. She thought it wasn't too bad.

If I'm in the area again, we'll probably stop on bye.

I stopped in and ordered lunch to go for my bf and myself the other afternoon before visiting my bf at work. I happened to be headed somewhere else, but as I was driving by, I noticed their sign, and having just come back from SE Asia, the idea of noodles drew me in quickly.

I ordered egg rolls, popcorn chicken, and a spicy noodle dish for us to share. I sat at the bar with a glass of water while I waited for my order. I only saw one person dining as a waited, and it may have been an employee because they also thanked me as I walked out with my order.

Food was delicious, but I specifically asked if hot sauce, forks and soy sauce were included as I was handed the bag. I was given an assertive yes, but low-and-behold, no soy sauce once I opened everything up. You don't get a discount for take out, so it's disappointing when you finally go to eat your food and something you asked for is missing. But aside from being wrong about including the sauce, everything was good. For what they're charging though, they should never forget to include the sides/sauces.

text:
I heard alot about Greystone, walked by last night and was able to get a table.

The atmosphere/ambience is upscale, exciting and elegant. GM Sara impressed me with her gracious, professional manner and attended to me with outstanding server Bryan. Everyone dresses well by the way and made me feel very welcome.

Sara started off recommending their "Twisted Boar(with Polenta)". This was my first time eating Boar and it was fantastic-can't wait to have it again. It goes perfectly with the creamy polenta.

I love tuna tartare and steak so decide on having both. San Diego has the biggest tuna fishing port in the US and this local catch was superfresh with exemplary flavor.

The Stars of my feast were the Wagyu Australian steak recommended by GM Sara and my choice of Duckhorn Estate(Napa Valley) Cabernet Sauvignon wine. The steak topped with buttered bacon was perfectly juicy. The flavor unforgettable with the marbling and meat texture creating a taste explosion. This was the best steak I've had all year.

The wine was the best CS I've ever had-still thinking about it's crisp, bold eclectic impact on my taste buds.

Sara was nice enough to show me around their gorgeous place with a private dining room/upper floor for special occasions like birthdays, important business deals and family events.

Bartender Joanna was also outstanding explaining the particulars on the famous Wagyu.

My first time at world renowned Greystone turned out to be one of the best dining experiences I've ever had.

6/10/13

FINALLY!

I've been hearing about this place from my Pittsburg (and other) friends for a long time. So when I was called to do a notary and the lady asked me to meet her here, I happily agreed. Husband and I were starving so we left home and arrived an hour before she was due to be there. Perfect!

We were seating right away, but it wasn't long before there was a big line forming in the hostess area. We did noticed a man (manager perhaps?) bring out a quesadilla to a family with little kids. So sweet!

It took forever to get our waitress to come take our order, and all she took was drinks. Then she brought them but had to drop other drinks off. THEN she came back and took our food orders. We each ordered two a la carte crunchy tacos (one potato and one carnitas for me).

It was forty (yes, 40) minutes before we received our food. We had some great chips while we waited. Our waters were never refilled for the hour we were seated. I spotted some hot sauce that I added to the really watery, mild salsa and that went great with the chips, but I was surprised the salsa wasn't as good as the rest of the food. Husband ate complimentary bean dip but I think he was mostly interested in the cheesy top layer. The hot sauce wasn't bad. When the tacos did come they were terrific. Most notably, the shells were really crunchy and had fresh, amazing flavor! It was a great dinner.  BUT.... it took an hour to get two tacos. It was $18.63 for 4 tacos and one soda. And it was all the way out in Pittsburg. When I'm back in Pittsburg, I'd love to eat here again - but not if it's packed.

name: Amy Palmer
text:
11/6/17

This review deserved an update a long time ago. Our company used to work next door to Kevin's and now that we've moved to a different area, the thing I miss most about working on Main Street is walking over for amazing pho on cold (and even really hot) afternoons.

Their soup is (in my opinion) the best, most flavorful pho around this area. I usually go for the seafood with chicken broth, and lots of garnish on top. With a Thai iced tea on the side.Large portions and great prices. No wonder it is ALWAYS packed at lunch.

I miss you, Kevin's Noodle House!

6/18/12 - 3 star

I work nearby so I've been in a few times since they opened. The last time was 6/15/2012 and while it was nice because it was a late lunch and it wasn't crowded, it was the first time we ordered off of the main menu (non-soup).  My fiance wasn't excited for soup in 100 degree weather so he ordered #41 - a combo meal with fried chicken wings, a pork chop, salad and rice. ($7.50)

Even the salad wasnt' very good. It came with a bowl of chicken broth on the side that was okay but the pork chop was almsot inedible. Very fatty - the flavor was terrific.  The fried chicken should have been prepared the same way. It was the opposite. Nice pieces of meat with absolutely no flavor. Incredibly disappointing. He didn't eat more than a bite or two.  The only thing I took home from his plate was the rice. And I hate wasting food.

I had a small bowl of seafood soup with egg noddles. ($5.25) The noodles were terrific but the soup was only okay this time. It had an off taste.  I reheated it the next day and even though it could be unrelated, I was up sick all night long. It was the only thing I ate Saturday that my fiance didn't eat. I didn't call the health department since I had taken it home... but honestly it'll be a little while before I go back.

We had a soda ($1.25 for a can) and a Thai iced tea ($3) for a meal total of $18.40.

Note: I did not know that Thai iced tea was made with Half & Half. No wonder they are sooooo good.

12/16/11 - 5 stars

I have been watching construction of this restaurant and the VW dealership next door to it for the last year.  They finally both opened last weekend and I braved the line for Pho (which was fast-moving, but still long at 1:00). Well-worth the wait! Every table was full (of course, it is still their grand opening period)... but I have a feeling it will remain busy as long as it's there. Pho is a noodle soup often with either a beef or chicken broth base, choice of meat and choice of noodle.
I customized mine some and ordered a clear noodle with shrimp in a chicken broth. It was served very hot with jalapeno, lime, and cilantro on the side to add to increase aroma and taste. I requested basil as also, which I believe is typically served with beef broth, rather than cilantro. I like both.

I ordered the Large which would probably feed 3 people :) I always order the large when ordering Pho because I enjoy it leftover.  I thought this broth had a little more flavor than the Pho place on Newell (the only other one in WC I am familiar with). Their table hot sauce and hot oil were delicious, though probably meant for an appetizer rather than the soup. The spring rolls on the table next to me looked awesome. (*next time*)

My large soup and a thai iced tea with pearls came to $11. Very reasonable! I'll definitely go back.

On a side note:
I finished the broth and had some noodles left that I didn't want to waste so I bought a packet of Pho powder and made my own broth at home and added the noddles and my own veggies. ($3 packet at the Asian market on N. Main Street and made 10 cups of Pho broth).  I may try making this at home again soon because I enjoyed all the extra veggies.

1/10/18

This is such a fun location to stop and walk around. There's a great restaurant, cute store, and a bar in the back! Even the restrooms are decorated to their homey theme and always kept clean!

Couldn't believe our most recent drive back up the 5, my boyfriend told me that he'd never had their pea soup. What?! Stop the car. We skipped my usual stop at Del Taco in Santa Nella and went straight to the windmilled location!

Get their soup in a bread bowl for all the fixings that come with it. (Or get 1/2 soup, 1/2 salad and you still get a large serving of both).  Service last time was outstanding, as usual. I think our server's name was Sara. Loud, bubbly, full of energy. It was a wonderful stop and Fred appreciated the delicious pea soup as much as I hoped he would. So good!

2/7/14 - five star

For my husband and myself, great service is more important than good food. There are tons of restaurants with awesome food, but very few get my return business unless I enjoy the overall dining experience; namely, terrific service.

On our way to southern CA for a very sad funeral of my young cousin, we pulled off the I-5S and stopped in for a bite. We were only a couple hours into the drive with almost 3x that distance to go.

The soup and salad I ordered ($10), and my husband's Monte Cristo sandwich, plus 2 drinks, was more than worth the $30 bill. The food was great and we never had to ask for refills. Roberto was on top of it and a really sincerely friendly server as well. He went beyond his server duty of asking polite questions. He seemed to care about our responses.

I asked for hot sauce with my food and he personally made me a hot salsa. In the back; in the kitchen! He even told me how he made it and warned me of the heat. It was So good and his thoughtfulness went a long way for two melancholy travelers. Thanks for being a kind person! His tables were full, the place was packed, and this unexpected act of delicious kindness deserves real recognition. Request Roberto for great service to complement your wonderful food.

text: The Westlake Village Inn in golf course is quite well known. Tiger Woods has played many competitions here as have other very well-known golfers. It is quite easy to get to off of the Agoura Road. There is a lot of parking in front, as well as very attentive parking attendants. You walk into the main hall, it is very open and spacious with a few steps up to the main reception area with a beautiful view over the golf course. The drinks if you want to buy alcohol are extremely expensive, $9 for a well drink. I thought this was rather excessive. I was there for a Homeowners Association Convention so there were a lot of vendors, there was a lot of room to set up and it was quite comfortable. We then went downstairs for a catered dinner. I was not particularly impressed with the quality of the food, there was a kale salad, I don't like kale. Dinner was a roast chicken breast with some sweet potatoes and broccolini. I thought it was quite simple for a restaurant that has such a significant reputation. Dessert was a creme brulee that was not that good, my husband was with me and he said that I made much better ones myself.

GBC is a brand new, upscale breakfast venue in the Gaslamp district bordering East Village at the corner of J and sixth sts.

They are the same company that owns famous Breakfast Republic.

Upon entering, I was very impressed with the attractive decor, roominess and organization.

Eric, the Asst. Manager, was very courteous, attentive as well as GM Zachary. They answered all questions well and exhibiting perfect demeanor.

My servers , Alexis & Colton, did an outstanding job with awesome personality. I recommend guests ask for either, if available.

I had the California Burrito and Brioche Egg Sammi(poached eggs, cheese, bacon) for the Main. Both were phenomenal tasting in large portions.

The berry kombucha and cinnamon coffee cake are also 10+.

I can find no faults with this new, exciting breakfast restaurant.

Highly recommended-one of the best in southern california.

I liked the restaurant. Typical Chinese  Japanese style buffet restaurant. Clean and cozy. But I think the branch in Glendale is better than the Long Beach.
has all the favourite items that is common in these types of restaurants. I enjoyed having the different types of susi and poke to offer. There are a lot of variety of fresh fruit, baked dessert and ice cream. Also occasionally they have crab in menu. For the price you pay for all the food that is offered is very reasonable. I enjoyed the meat section of the restaurant as well. There was choice of good pork sausage, beef roast and pork roast which tasted very yummy. Also I liked the baked shrimp with cheese - this was something new that I had tried. There were some cheese and pork wantons and they were really delicious. I think the variety of sushi in this restaurant was amazing, almost 10-15 different types in offer including fried sushi.they have a very good bar on site and you can order beer, sake and cocktails from the bar. I had tried the margarita and that was also good. Overall the place was clean and the waiters were prompt to attend you and clear up the plates form the table. text:
Great ambience. Great service. I am downgrading my review from last time as the food is just not up to par with Mandalay, which is the SF area's premier Burmese restaurant, or with local Thai restaurants, or with Palo Alto's Three Seasons or Tamarine. The food is quite simply not great, but certainly not bad. There is good vegetarian variety but the food is honestly not that tasteful after trying a variety of items on 2 occasions. It needs more flavor & spice. With other Burmese & Asian options, I will not be trying this place again.

The tea leaf salad is a classic, but is different from Mandalay in San Francisco in that this actually has lettuce - this saves the food part of the review. The samosa soup is also very good. The garlic noodles were eggless, & were good - quite light to the taste - refreshing from the quite heavy drunken noodles you get at Thai restaurants. The Seasonal Pea Leaf was good, not spiced. The yellow tofu red curry uses beans instead of soybeans & was good. The vegetarian palata is not your typical Burmese, Malaysian or Thai roti paratha type item as there is no curry dipping sauce - just some thick red chutney which did not taste good. Avid the Burmese ice tea which was way too creamy. The coconut pudding with mango ice cream was good - not too heavy for me and my wife.
